teachings.summary: The remnant in Amos 5 is not a Calvinist election of certain men but the promise that whoever seeks the Lord shall live.
teachings.text:
**Amos 5** continues the prophesying against Israel, whose destruction is nigh. There is no salvation for her. God's judgment and righteousness are at hand.

But, as always, there are a remnant of believers still in the land. Illustrating this in verse 3, in each of the decimated cities. A remnant because of the promise of the Lord that those who seek Him shall live.

Note that the number is not set in stone, it is an example. The remnant aren't chosen by God, and it isn't a promise that there will be a tenth spared. As with this entire chapter, it is an encouragement to repent towards God.

Many Dispensationalists put the wrong emphasis of there being a remnant on God to elect one. To be a Calvinist God Who forces certain men to be saved. They sometimes argue that verses like this are a guarantee that God has decided to set some people aside to be saved, rather than a process by which they can be. And so, the emphasis should be on the promise, that those who call on His name shall be saved.

Amos, speaking the word of God warns, seek Him, not Bethel in the Northern Kingdom of Israel where a golden calf was set up by King Jeroboam as a false religion. Not in Gilgal, on the Jordan where idolatrous practices to false gods were held. These vain hopes would come to naught.

Seek the Lord and ye shall live!

Failing that, He promises His wrath will consume them.

And they, specifically the children of Joseph, 'all Ephraim" as the prophets call the Northern Kingdom of Israel, deserve it. They turn right judgment to wormwood, thinking it bitter, rejecting the way of righteousness. They rebuke prophets, hating them that preach God's word. They take advantage of the poor and the weak. They build up their riches by their unrighteousness. They afflict the just, take bribes and turn aside the poor seeking help. They show no mercy and so God's mercy is gone from them.

But the offer stands;

*Seek him that maketh the seven stars and Orion, and turneth the shadow of death into the morning, and maketh the day dark with night: that calleth for the waters of the sea, and poureth them out upon the face of the earth: The Lord is his name: That strengtheneth the spoiled against the strong, so that the spoiled shall come against the fortress.*

Amos preaches against sin and warns of the coming judgment, and the offer of hope in salvation by faith in the Lord. Just as we are called to do today.

teachings.title: It is always a choice
teachings.summary: Israel chose of their own free will to leave the work undone, and God gave His word as testimony so men would believe, using even their disobedience for His purpose.
teachings.text:
Just to recap the theme going into the **Book of Judges**; God having delivered the people into the promised land commanded them to utterly destroy the inhabitants and to smash down their altars to the false gods they worshipped. The Lord had been with them in every battle (save one, thanks to the abomination of Achan). He had driven out the people that Joshua and his armies went against. He delivered 33 Kings into their hands. The Lord God rained hail the size of boulders, drove men out with hornets, felled the walls of cities with the shout and trumpets of the Israelites.

But yet they did not fully eradicate the Canaanites and others in the land. They resorted to allowing them to stay in tribute. Valuing their gold more than the commandments of God.

They had the knowledge of the will of the sovereign God, and *chose*, of their own will, to ignore His word, to do as they saw was right in their own eyes. Despite all their valiant deeds and the miracles they witnessed while obeying Him, they slacked off in their duty to do that which was comfortable. Easy. To leave the work unfinished.

By their choice. By free will.

And God responded by removing the hedge of protection around them. By allowing them to feel the consequences of their actions. By using these nations as a thorn in the side of Israel, to prove her that they may learn the ways of war, rather than peace. To be a snare with their false gods, so that the glory of God could be known. That in their tribulation they would call out to the Lord for salvation, and He would place His Spirit on a judge He would raise up to deliver them.

The Bible is the record of God's will for man, in Christ Jesus. And it demonstrates that He gave His word as a testimony, that man should believe Him. The Godhead being three persons, that the witness be true, just as the law requires. Jesus appeared resurrected to witnesses that others believed their report. The Spirit indwells believers, that it testify to them they have eternal life, that they may **know**. The Bible exists, inspired and preserved, that we may hear the word and have faith that it is true, and obey His commandments beginning with the gospel of Christ.

It is always a choice. And God uses our choices to His purpose, even when we are disobedient. Even when some don't believe the report. Even when people fall away from the truth.

teachings.title: The covenant was glorious, the fault was theirs
teachings.summary: He argues Calvinism makes the covenants, the law as schoolmaster and Christ's obedience meaningless and limits God, whose will is done despite man's disobedience.
teachings.text:
Calvinism demands that a sovereign God removes that choice, the need for His word as testimony, the Spirit to believe, and makes all of man's shortcomings God's responsibility. It denies the power of God to see His will done **despite** our failings. To use our sins as a means of shaping the clay as a Potter.

The covenants become worthless, because why make promises and give blessings for man's obedience when the obedience is given to them?

The Israelites failed to harken to the commandments of God, and lost those blessings and protections. Just as the covenant with Moses in the wilderness established as terms; I will be your God, and ye shall be My people. But if they took up the gods and abominations of those in the land, it would be a curse, and they would be troubled until they turned back to the Lord.

The covenant was glorious, but the fault was with them.

None of this makes sense in a Calvinistic world view. There is no lesson to learn from it. If they were predestinated to disobey, then the punishment they received wouldn't be to prove them and provoke them to repentance. God's decision to let them suffer the consequences to teach them their need for salvation in Him wouldn't make any sense. There's no need for the law to be a schoolmaster if faith and obedience is handed down by the good will of a sovereign Lord, on whomever He will.

And it limits God, showing He needs total control of man's actions in order to have the outcome He desires, rather than the glory and power of His will being done despite man's disobedience.

And it makes Christ's obedience to the Father's will unto death meaningless, for if man's obedience is forced upon them, why would the Son saying "not my will, but the Father's" mean anything at all to us? How would that perfect obedience save us? How is it an inspiration to strive for that perfection?

The gospel of the Calvinist is a hopeless thing, and their false god is weak and capricious.

teachings.title: Choose life: against Calvinists and Zionists
teachings.summary: Against dispensationalists, Calvinists and Zionists he teaches that God makes salvation an individual choice of the heart, Jews included, not forced or by birth.
teachings.text:
For the Dispensationalists, the Lord who cannot lie and Who keeps His promises forever, as they are fond to remind us, had this to say;

*But if thine heart turn away, so that thou wilt not hear, but shalt be drawn away, and worship other gods, and serve them; I denounce unto you this day, that ye shall surely perish, and that ye shall not prolong your days upon the land, whither thou passest over Jordan to go to possess it.*

"Aha, but if they turn again to the Lord they shall be graft in!" Yes. Individual jews who choose life, seek the Lord and find Him in Christ will be forgiven and be made heirs to the promise.

But that choice is theirs to make, as individuals, choosing between death and life in Christ Jesus.

Calvinists and Zionists share the same twisted theology; that God will force individuals to believe, just as He keeps them from obedience to the Gospel. But here in **Deuteronomy 30** (and throughout scripture) God makes it clear that we all have a choice. That it isn't by who we are, but what our heart believes. That it is by choosing to love the Lord, and in doing so, living by faith.

Choose life.

teachings.title: Hath not the potter power over the clay
teachings.summary: God's predestination is the election of believers in Christ, not choosing who believes, and He may use vessels of wrath for His glory.
teachings.text:
Is God then unrighteous? Is it unfair that some are saved and others burned, that those who are elected in faith through Christ are shaped to His purpose, while those who reject the faith and deny the truth have their hearts eventually hardened, cut off and burned?

*Thou wilt say then unto me, Why doth he yet find fault? For who hath resisted his will? Nay but, O man, who art thou that repliest against God? Shall the thing formed say to him that formed it, Why hast thou made me thus? Hath not the potter power over the clay, of the same lump to make one vessel unto honour, and another unto dishonour?*

Who are we to judge God?

*But we are sure that the judgment of God is according to truth*...

It is His will to be done. That Jesua would be born of a woman, live, be crucified and raised again, to be made Lord as His son, and that all who believe be given eternal life, sealed by the Spirit and given hope to the resurrection, heirs to the Kingdom. Made sons of God.

This is the predestination of God. Not picking and choosing who believes, but the elected in Christ, using those who do to His purpose.

And if His purpose is to show His glory and righteousness through those vessels of wrath, then so be it.

*We are sure that the judgment of God is according to truth against them which commit such things.*

teachings.title: Predestinated in Christ, not chosen to believe
teachings.summary: Predestination in Ephesians 1 and Romans 8 is in Christ, not God choosing who will believe, since God will have all men to be saved and draws all men, so Calvinism and limited atonement are doctrines of devils rooted in pride.
teachings.text:
**Ephesians 1:3-6**
*Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who hath blessed us with all spiritual blessings in heavenly places in Christ: According as he hath chosen us in him before the foundation of the world, that we should be holy and without blame before him in love: Having predestinated us unto the adoption of children by Jesus Christ to himself, according to the good pleasure of his will, To the praise of the glory of his grace, wherein he hath made us accepted in the beloved*.

So what is this that is predestined? The saved? Or Christ Jesus by whom we are saved?

Calvinists read this and **Romans 8**, and place the emphasis on themselves, rather than Christ, and so, they claim, that God picks who will believe. This doctrine of devils, like all false gospels, is based on putting themselves before the Lord. Just as works salvation is predicated on the person's own righteousness, not Christ's, the special boy doctrine makes it that they are the elect, not of Jesus perfect work, the lamb slain before the foundation of the world, that all who believe on Him will be saved, but by God's "sovereign will."

But we know that God's will is not for a chosen few.

**1 Timothy 2:3-4**
*For this is good and acceptable in the sight of God our Saviour; Who will have all men to be saved, and to come unto the knowledge of the truth.*

If God exerted His sovereign will, we would all be saved.

As Jesus says,

*And this is the will of him that sent me, that every one which seeth the Son, and believeth on him, may have everlasting life: and I will raise him up at the last day.*

Every one.

Limited atonement is a doctrine of devils. It is based on pride.

So we know that all who believe are predestinated in Christ that they will have eternal life, sealed by the Spirit, and if they walk in tha Spirit, will be conformed to the use of God, that we may become separated, to be servants of the Gospel.

And so continuing the theme of Romans 8, the context of which is the works of the Spirit.

That while we are yet in the flesh, knowing the day of redemption will free us from that wretched state, that the Spirit helps heal our infirmities that led us to sin and conforms us to His will, so long as we walk after the Spirit, not feeding the flesh with the things of this world. That the Spirit within us acts also as an intercessor to bring our needs before the Father, so that His will be done in us.

And so, the good news;

*And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose.*

Who is called? Who is drawn to faith in God's promise?

**John 12:32-33**
*And I, if I be lifted up from the earth, will draw all men unto me. This he said, signifying what death he should die.*

All men. But few will answer this call, and seek to be transformed to fulfill His intended purpose for us. The harvest is great but the laborers few. Strait is the gate and narrow the way and few there be that find it. Every name of every person born of water upon this earth is in the book of life. But their names are stricken from it when they die in sin, unbelieving. (Or reprobates, twice-dead)

No where in the Bible do we see names added, only erased. God's foreknowledge, knowing of the end from the beginning, means He knows who will answer the call. It doesn't mean He selects them.

teachings.title: Jacob have I loved, Esau have I hated
teachings.summary: The hatred of Esau refers to the later wicked nation of Edom, not to Esau himself, who God blessed and who was saved by faith, against the Calvinist reading.
teachings.text:
He is Esau who is Edom. He is Esau the father of the Edomites.

We are given the genealogies of Esau, who is Edom, which God repeats for us several times, to drive home the point.

The primary target for this scripture were the Israelites in Moses' day, sharing their people's story and the story of the people of Mt Seir, who they are coming up against as we will see later in scripture. Cousins really. One with the blessing and the promise for the seed that is Christ to come.

Esau himself is often painted in a negative light, primarily due to a Calvinist reading of **Romans 9:13**:

*As it is written, Jacob have I loved, but Esau have I hated.*

Which is itself taken from the prophet **Malachi 1:3-4**

*And I hated Esau, and laid his mountains and his heritage waste for the dragons of the wilderness. Whereas Edom saith, We are impoverished, but we will return and build the desolate places; thus saith the Lord of hosts, They shall build, but I will throw down; and they shall call them, The border of wickedness, and, The people against whom the Lord hath indignation for ever. And your eyes shall see, and ye shall say, The Lord will be magnified from the border of Israel.*

Note, these are the Edomites generations later, being cursed by God. Not Esau, who is Edom.

And why were they cursed by God for destruction? In **Deuteronomy 2:1-5**, God orders the Israelites to tread carefully through the land of Seir so as not to worry the Edomites. That their land was promised Esau:

*Then we turned, and took our journey into the wilderness by the way of the Red sea, as the Lord spake unto me: and we compassed mount Seir many days.*

*And the Lord spake unto me, saying,*
*Ye have compassed this mountain long enough: turn you northward.*
*And command thou the people, saying, Ye are to pass through the coast of your brethren the children of Esau, which dwell in Seir; and they shall be afraid of you: take ye good heed unto yourselves therefore: Meddle not with them; for I will not give you of their land, no, not so much as a foot breadth; because I have given mount Seir unto Esau for a possession.*

We see at this point God is still allowing the nations of Edom, who is Esau to continue with His blessing of a promised land to their patriarch.

God loved Esau, despite his failings. He made a promise to him and kept it, even in those days, 400yrs later.

Esau was saved by the same faith as Jacob, and their fathers. But his descendents became wicked.

**Numbers 20:14-21**

*And Moses sent messengers from Kadesh unto the king of Edom, Thus saith thy brother Israel, Thou knowest all the travail that hath befallen us:*
*How our fathers went down into Egypt, and we have dwelt in Egypt a long time; and the Egyptians vexed us, and our fathers: And when we cried unto the Lord, he heard our voice, and sent an angel, and hath brought us forth out of Egypt: and, behold, we are in Kadesh, a city in the uttermost of thy border:*

*Let us pass, I pray thee, through thy country: we will not pass through the fields, or through the vineyards, neither will we drink of the water of the wells: we will go by the king's high way, we will not turn to the right hand nor to the left, until we have passed thy borders.*

*And Edom said unto him, Thou shalt not pass by me, lest I come out against thee with the sword. And the children of Israel said unto him, We will go by the high way: and if I and my cattle drink of thy water, then I will pay for it: I will only, without doing anything else, go through on my feet.*

*And he said, Thou shalt not go through. And Edom came out against him with much people, and with a strong hand. Thus Edom refused to give Israel passage through his border: wherefore Israel turned away from him.*

Later we see Edomites war with Israel, and eventually David conquers and takes them as servants, slaves.

**2 Samuel 8:13-14**

teachings.title: Predestinated in Christ, not chosen individuals
teachings.summary: In Ephesians 1 it is Christ who was predestinated and we are chosen and accepted only in Him, obtaining the inheritance after we hear and trust the gospel and are sealed, so Calvinism misplaces the focus.
teachings.text:
What an introduction. Paul lays so much doctrine in what is only the greeting of his letter to believers at Ephesus. It's fantastic, and dense and due to the extensive use of prepositional clauses, causes many believers and all natural men to struggle in understanding.

One aspect of understanding the Word is understanding God's use of conditional logic, if-then statements, often complex with multiple factors. This method of reasoning together with God is evident in this epistle.

Paul is an Apostle, *by* the will of God. He's writing to the saints, the faithful *in* Jesus Christ. He wishes grace and peace to the reader *from* God and Jesus. God has blessed us *with* all spiritual blessings.

Keeping this in mind, consider verse 4-6:

According as he hath chosen us *in him* (Jesus) before the foundation of the world, that we should be holy and without blame before him in love: Having predestinated us unto the adoption of children **by** Jesus Christ **t**o himself, *according to the good pleasure of his will, To the praise of the glory of his grace, wherein he* (God) *hath made us accepted* in the beloved *(*Jesus*).*

The error of Calvinism is to misapply the focus of predestination to those benefiting from it, rather than *by* whom, Jesus Christ.

God has chosen us *in Jesus*. Predestinated *by Christ.* Accepted *in the beloved,* His Son.

Jesus is the Son of God, beloved of the Father, the lamb slain before the foundation of the world. Jesus was predestinated to be the means *by which* we received grace.

We weren't chosen. He was. We are only adopted sons, because of Jesus *In whom we have redemption through his blood, the forgiveness of sins, according to the riches of his grace.*

Paul is lauding God the Father and the Son, Christ Jesus, he is not indicating that the believers are special boys, predestined, but that in Christ through God's grace, we are.

*In whom also we have obtained an inheritance, being predestinated according to the purpose of him who worketh all things after the counsel of his own will.*

We obtain the inheritance in Jesus who was predestinated according to the will of God.

And this isn't a question of perspective and interpretation, because Paul then makes our role in this process abundantly clear:

That we should be to the praise of his glory, who first trusted in Christ.

*In whom ye also trusted, after that ye heard the word of truth, the gospel of your salvation: in whom also after that ye believed, ye were sealed with that holy Spirit of promise, Which is the earnest of our inheritance until the redemption of the purchased possession, unto the praise of his glory.*

Follow that? We gain this inheritance IN Christ who we trusted when we heard the Gospel, and after hearing and believing, being sealed by the Holy Spirit. These are the conditional terms of our obtaining the inheritance, our salvation. Not God picking and choosing us, but God having predestinated Christ, that those *who first trusted* in Him are included in the inheritance.

It's an order of operations that is focused on God and His Son. Our part is in believing it to be true.

teachings.title: John 1: as many as received him
teachings.summary: John 1 shows Christ lights every man, that the world did not know Him, and that whoever receives Him by believing becomes a son of God, refuting limited atonement and irresistible grace.
teachings.text:
Next, the apostle John introduces us to John the Baptist, the voice crying out in the wilderness bearing witness to Christ.

John the apostle again turns to explain Jesus is the true light which "lighteth *every* man." (RIP limited atonement).

V10 states the matter plainly, the creator has come into the creation and the creation didn't even recognize Him, fallen as we are. Man doesn't recognize Christ (rip irresistible grace)

V11 lays the groundwork for replacement theology. The "chosen people" the Jews don't recognize Christ

V11 is the Gospel itself; the good news. "As many received him..." (that's an indeterminate number, meaning 'all who' (limited atonement BTFO, again), "...to them gave he power to become the sons of God" (the promise made by God), "even to them that believe on his name" (the means of obtaining the aforementioned power to be sons of God; BELIEVING, not works or any other means).

V13 Sons born (you have to be born again to be a son or daughter of God). Not by blood (dispensationalism, ded), not by our fleshly desire (none righteous), not by our works (the will of man) but of God.

V14 is the mystery of Christ made flesh revealed.
V15-17 John the BAPTIST (hint) tells us his ministry has been preaching the coming Christ and salvation by grace, not the law.

When JtB is questioned by the Pharisees he testifies that Jesus is the Christ come in answer to what was taught by all the prophets, the faith that saved OT saints was manifest.

About halfway through one chapter and the doctrines are just boom, boom, boom...

teachings.title: Romans 8: adopted after first believing
teachings.summary: Paul builds the case for conditional election: we are adopted as sons and joint heirs only after believing, and foreknowledge comes before predestination, which Calvinists reverse.
teachings.text:
Paul has for the past 7 chapters laid out the factual, Biblical case for *conditional election,* that **we must believe to be saved,** starting with the testimonial of God in creation, the lack of excuse by the unbelieving, the refusal to accept the knowledge of God of the reprobate, and the surety of our salvation of placing our faith in God's promise.

Here, tying together these themes, he speaks of the carnal mind that the saved still have, exhorting the saved by faith to live in the spirit, not the flesh, because in that righteousness given us is adoption into the promise; we become heirs of Christ, we call out to our Father. In verse 9, he makes it clear that this is a **conditional** state of being. You aren't adopted without first believing.

Then, Paul begins building onto this foundational theme of being adopted as sons in the spirit by explaining how God's foreknowledge that we (the saved) then be used to His purpose. (Note the order of operations in verse 29, Calvinists reverse it, and thus get none of it).

The glory of being joint heirs with Christ, in Christ. The hope, which is an earnest expectation for the thing we believe to come (not a long-shot wish as some use the term) being shared with all of creation, waiting for that kingdom to come. That we are blameless to charge by any because we are justified in our faith in Christ. That, in faith, none can stand before us as God gives us all things, according to His will.

Having laid out the first faith and its terms and rewards, Paul is making the case to the saved to understand what their faith has opened them up to, what God's gifts mean to us if we now walk in the spirit, quickened by the Holy Ghost, that all things are for good to us for loving God, if we simply trust further in the word of God, building faith upon faith.

teachings.title: Who first trusted in Christ
teachings.summary: Ephesians 1 does not teach unconditional election, because the chosen are those who first trusted in Christ, and the elect nation is spiritual Israel, not the Jews of the flesh.
teachings.text:
Here we see in what is considered the strongest case for special boyism undone with one conditional phrase, "who first trusted in Christ."

Ephesians 1 and Romans 8 are the go to chapters used by special boys to justify their being "chosen" for salvation, but both Ephesians 1 and Romans 8 precede Ephesians 2 and Romans 9, the nails in the coffin of dispensationalism, the idea that only the Israel of the flesh were "chosen."

Paul is establishing that the new covenant is for Israel of the spirit, and has to establish that in the same way (saved and unsaved) physical Israel was predestined by God to be used for His purpose, so too saved Gentiles representing spiritual Israel are similarly a chosen nation.

That God in His foreknowledge destined and shaped those who would be heirs to the promise to be His tools on earth. That knowing who would believe and who wouldn't allows Him to craft the believers to be of best use for His will, is almost a secondary point of this scripture.

He's establishing that the Jews who are persecuting saved Gentiles, claiming that Israel of the flesh are still God's special boys and Gentiles aren't heirs to that kingdom or adopted sons of God, are liars.

teachings.title: The whole testimony is about free will
teachings.summary: From Eden to Revelation scripture shows men choosing, and God in His foreknowledge elects to blessings those who have first believed.
teachings.text:
God wouldn't go through so much trouble establishing His testimony, asking that people believe His word, that He cannot lie and illustrating the choice of man, from Adam and Eve in the garden, to Cain and Abel' faith vs works, Noah and the ark, Abraham and Isaac (and Ishmael/the bond woman), Esau and Jacob, the Northern/Southern Kingdoms, Jonah, Job, Jesus in the garden, Jews choosing Barabbas, Paul's epistles describing all these divergent points, Peter's peculiar people, Revelation of Christ showing the choice to accept the beast, take the mark, be sorted like sheep and goats, and even the devil being freed for a season to convince some humans who have just lived a thousand years of peace under Christ to rise up and rebel one final time.

The entire testimony, the living Testament of Christ, is about free will, informed choice. And we are called to share that testimony with others to give them that information, and lead them to the same conclusion.

And God, in His foreknowledge of who would choose to accept His word on faith, has a destiny for us, a plan for us, and promises and blessings that we are elected to receive having FIRST believed.

teachings.title: Sovereign does not mean puppet master
teachings.summary: Lordship salvation and Calvinism grow from modern bibles and a false idea of sovereignty, while God's word says whosoever believeth shall not perish.
teachings.text:
One thing that greatly confuses many searching for truth, and leads them into the damnable heresy of Lordship salvation and reformed Calvinism is they use modern perverted bibles, that insert words and concepts that aren't in the text, and that are then manipulated to deceive the ignorant.

Few would argue that God isn't LORD of creation, but the concept of "sovereign" shifts this truth to a false doctrine that reduces God to simply a puppet master micromanaging all of reality.

But even if we were to use the dictionary definition of the word 'sovereign,' it doesn't carry that implication. A sovereign may pass orders and laws and render judgement and punish the disobedient, but he can't force anyone to obey all his dictates.

I would that any deceived by this doctrine to repent and believe the testimony of God, that the only way to salvation is to trust His word, that He so loved the world He gave His only begotten son that WHOSOEVER believe shall not perish but have everlasting life

teachings.title: Meddle not with them that are given to change
teachings.summary: Change for its own sake has led churches into apostasy, from Catholicism to modernism and the compromise of standards and music, and moving the landmarks of the fathers ends in sudden ruin.
teachings.text:
*My son, fear thou the Lord and the king: and meddle not with them that are given to change: For their calamity shall rise suddenly; and who knoweth the ruin of them both?*

The people who promote change as an end to itself, that we must "progress," to leave the old paths to strike out in the new, covet ideas of what they think could be, because they don't appreciate what is.

In Christianity, this has resulted in more tragedy and departure from the Biblical truth found in the fear of the Lord. Taking His word as the final authority.

Denominational control was a reaction to the fact that some churches fell into apostasy. This gave us the false religion of Catholicism.

In recent times, the 19th and 20th century were plagued by modernism and changing of God's word to justify it. Even in the past few decades, churches that had resisted change and kept the right gospel, began to compromise with the world to "keep up with the times." Dropping standards, adding carnal appeals in music, technology, dress, "worship," to attract younger crowds.

But the ruin of these changes comes suddenly. You can only go so far afield, and drift off the well-worn paths so far without finding yourself in sudden calamity. You can't move the landmarks of your fathers' and not become lost.

teachings.title: The Samaritans worshipped what they knew not
teachings.summary: The Samaritans who offered to help build the temple mixed the Lord with their own gods, worshipping what they knew not.
teachings.text:
Ezra continues to give background to the history of rebuilding the Temple, and here he writes about the period when, under Cyrus the Jews returned to Israel, and began work on the foundation.

And adversaries of Judah and Benjamin, the people who occupied the land of Israel after the Assyrian captivity, the mixed and displaced strangers that had become the Samaritans ask to help Zerubbabel and the people with the construction.

They say that they too worship the Lord, and had since the days of Esarhaddon, king of Assur, which is Assyria.

But, as we know they worship what they know not.

**2 Kings 17:20-34**
*And the Lord rejected all the seed of Israel, and afflicted them, and delivered them into the hand of spoilers, until he had cast them out of his sight. For he rent Israel from the house of David; and they made Jeroboam the son of Nebat king: and Jeroboam drave Israel from following the Lord, and made them sin a great sin. For the children of Israel walked in all the sins of Jeroboam which he did; they departed not from them; Until the Lord removed Israel out of his sight, as he had said by all his servants the prophets. So was Israel carried away out of their own land to Assyria unto this day. And the king of Assyria brought men from Babylon, and from Cuthah, and from Ava, and from Hamath, and from Sepharvaim, and placed them in the cities of Samaria instead of the children of Israel: and they possessed Samaria, and dwelt in the cities thereof. And so it was at the beginning of their dwelling there, that they feared not the Lord: therefore the Lord sent lions among them, which slew some of them. Wherefore they spake to the king of Assyria, saying, The nations which thou hast removed, and placed in the cities of Samaria, know not the manner of the God of the land: therefore he hath sent lions among them, and, behold, they slay them, because they know not the manner of the God of the land. Then the king of Assyria commanded, saying, Carry thither one of the priests whom ye brought from thence; and let them go and dwell there, and let him teach them the manner of the God of the land. Then one of the priests whom they had carried away from Samaria came and dwelt in Bethel, and taught them how they should fear the Lord. Howbeit every nation made gods of their own, and put them in the houses of the high places which the Samaritans had made, every nation in their cities wherein they dwelt. And the men of Babylon made Succothbenoth, and the men of Cuth made Nergal, and the men of Hamath made Ashima, And the Avites made Nibhaz and Tartak, and the Sepharvites burnt their children in fire to Adrammelech and Anammelech, the gods of Sepharvaim. So they feared the Lord, and made unto themselves of the lowest of them priests of the high places, which sacrificed for them in the houses of the high places. They feared the Lord, and served their own gods, after the manner of the nations whom they carried away from thence. Unto this day they do after the former manners: they fear not the Lord, neither do they after their statutes, or after their ordinances, or after the law and commandment which the Lord commanded the children of Jacob, whom he named Israel*...

They did not worship the Lord alone, or properly. They were worshiping in the high places, the mountains.

**John 4:19-23**
*The woman saith unto him, Sir, I perceive that thou art a prophet. Our fathers worshipped in this mountain; and ye say, that in Jerusalem is the place where men ought to worship. Jesus saith unto her, Woman, believe me, the hour cometh, when ye shall neither in this mountain, nor yet at Jerusalem, worship the Father. Ye worship ye know not what: we know what we worship: for salvation is of the Jews. But the hour cometh, and now is, when the true worshippers shall worship the Father in spirit and in truth: for the Father seeketh such to worship him.*

teachings.title: Ecumenism refused and persecution follows
teachings.summary: Zerubbabel rightly refused the Samaritans' ecumenical offer, and like them false religions, Rome included, use governments to stop true churches and soul winners.
teachings.text:
So these Samaritans were offering an ecumenical union to build the Lord's house, similar to if a group of Catholics sought to join with a NT Baptist Church. And naturally, Zerubbabel rejected their offer as tainted. Offended, these false religions begin to petition the government of Persia to stop the rebuilding effort.

**Ezra 4** documents the pre-520 BC efforts by Judah's enemies to undermine the temple rebuilding that began shortly after Cyrus's decree in 538 BC, and persisting throughout his reign, through his predecessor Cambyses's rule (530-522 BC), and into Darius I's early years, circa 522 BC, resulting in halted work until Darius's second year in 520, when Haggai and Zechariah pick up.

The chapter also mentions later similar oppositions during Ahasuerus's reign (likely Xerxes I, starting around 486 BC) with initial accusations, and under Artaxerxes I (465-424 BC) via detailed letters that enforced a cessation of Jerusalem's reconstruction as a threat. Ezra lists all these efforts as one long opposition campaign.

How relatable this is to our modern day efforts of soul-winning and building up the house of God. How frequently do false "Christian" leaders join together to get Bible-believing church's "in trouble" with the local government? To try to stop door to door evangelism, labeling it as solicitation. To try and get churches denounced and shut down for preaching against the sodomites.

When you look at the history of the Roman Catholic Church, it literally was formed by apostates working in conjunction with the government to shut down and martyr believers and good NT churches, to force them out. Declaring their pastors heretics. History is filled with these same types of people.

But God had promised in the 70th year of captivity to turn towards the people if they built His house. And Darius I blessed the construction, and it resumed for a while.

teachings.title: The woman in the ephah carried to Shinar
teachings.summary: Zechariah's woman of wickedness carried to Shinar pictures the spirit of the whore, Mystery Babylon of Revelation 17, delivered to her place.
teachings.text:
**Zechariah 5** begins a series of very symbolic visions for the prophet. The angelic guides explain their representation, though their ultimate meaning may be left open to interpretation.

The first is a vision of a roll, or scroll, a length of parchment flying in the sky, 20 cubits long and 10 wide.

The angel says that this scroll contains a curse against those that steal and those that swear, falsely in God's name, that they shall be cut off. That their house shall be consumed and the timber of it. I believe that this means the house, as in the family and the structure, both.

This is gone out to the world, not confined to Israel or Judah. God promises there is a recompense for their error. A curse for their sin. Thieves never prosper, and those that swear falsely are eventually done in by their own lies.

Then the angel shows Zechariah another vision; an ephah, or basically a measured container, according to Webster's 1832 "an ancient Hebrew dry measure equivalent to a bushel." And in the ephah, a woman representing wickedness, kept in by a lead lid weighing a talent. She is carried by two female angelic beings with wings like storks, to the land of Shinar, which is Babylon.

This is cryptic and while we can see what it represents in the text, it is difficult to determine what it means. I think it is the spirit of the whore, Mystery Babylon, being delivered to its place, where that same spirit will rest on empires and kings, who become drunk in her fornication, from **Revelation 17**;

*Come hither; I will shew unto thee the judgment of the great whore that sitteth upon many waters: With whom the kings of the earth have committed fornication, and the inhabitants of the earth have been made drunk with the wine of her fornication. So he carried me away in the spirit into the wilderness: and I saw a woman sit upon a scarlet coloured beast, full of names of blasphemy, having seven heads and ten horns. And the woman was arrayed in purple and scarlet colour, and decked with gold and precious stones and pearls, having a golden cup in her hand full of abominations and filthiness of her fornication: And upon her forehead was a name written,* Mystery, Babylon The Great, The Mother Of Harlots And Abominations Of The Earth*. And I saw the woman drunken with the blood of the saints, and with the blood of the martyrs of Jesus: and when I saw her, I wondered with great admiration.*

teachings.title: Nineveh the wellfavoured harlot
teachings.summary: Nineveh, the harlot selling nations through whoredoms and witchcrafts, shows the same spirit of Mystery Babylon that passed through the empires and remains today.
teachings.text:
The final prophecy against Nineveh by Nahum the prophet. The city is gone and there is no escape from the judgment.

That bloody city, the armies that laid waste to other nations, and had corpses piled about them, now it was their turn.

*Because of the multitude of the whoredoms of the wellfavoured harlot, the mistress of witchcrafts, that selleth nations through her whoredoms, and families through her witchcrafts*.

The comparison of Nineveh and the Assyrian empire to the whore of Babylon in Revelation seems obvious;

*Come hither; I will shew unto thee the judgment of the great whore that sitteth upon many waters: With whom the kings of the earth have committed fornication, and the inhabitants of the earth have been made drunk with the wine of her fornication.*

The adultery of the whore, leading nations from God and to worship her idols and false gods and goddesses, to become drunk on the wine of her fornication. To sell nations through her whoredoms and witchcraft.

Isn't that the spirit of Babylon? Wasn't it upon Assyria? And then upon Babylon herself, the Medes and the Persians. The Greeks and the Romans. And even to this day there is that spirit of rebellion and Idolatry, adultery and bloodshed. Abominations.

The prophet reminds Nineveh of the city of No, in Ethiopia. A mighty city between Egypt and Ethiopia, upon many waters, defended well by natural defenses. And the Assyrians cut it down.

Now they would feel the same wrath, as Nebuchadnezzar, the Chaldeans and the Medes, came to destroy their capital.

Again, the word of God mocks them in their tribulation. He says build up your defenses. Lay brick and mortar. It won't matter. *There is no healing of thy bruise; thy wound is grievous*.

And just as He promised, and as Nahum preached, Nineveh was destroyed.

teachings.title: Spiritual adultery provokes God's wrath
teachings.summary: What most provokes God's wrath is the spiritual adultery of those calling themselves His who serve idols, like the scarlet and purple sects of our day.
teachings.text:
One of the major themes of the prophets, aside from the promise of deliverance in the promise of the Lord, is the judgment of God upon those who chase after other gods. Who commit fornication with them, metaphorically. The whoredoms of the people, who He consistently compares to a woman caught in adultery, whose lovers have abandoned her in her downfall. That she is like a woman exposed, naked to the world, ashamed.

The Lord is longsuffering and merciful, His patience and grace are abundant and His love for us who are His is unending. But those who fall away to apostasy, Idolatry, faith in strange gods, while still calling themselves His, provokes Him to wrath. God's name is jealousy.

So, in our times where the largest sects calling themselves "Christian," are decked in scarlet and purple, clad in gold and jewels, and bowing and serving idols, putting faith in the creation over the Creator, lighting candles and incense to the "queen of heaven," it stirs God to wrath.

The abominations of the heathen, the shedding of innocent blood, violence, sexual perversions...all of these the Lord hates, but it is that adultery of those harlots that really stirs Him to wrath.

teachings.title: The Fall of Babylon the Great City
teachings.summary: Babylon is destroyed last in the wrath, and the seat of Babylon is always some nation embodying its spirit, which today looks like the United States.
teachings.text:
And so, as the vials and trumps come to an end, the three and a half years of wrath poured out, special judgment is given against that great city, Babylon.

This is prophetic in the OT of both the actual Babylonian empire, but also the future empire represented in night visions and dreams interpreted by Daniel, and preached by the other prophets, which as we see in scripture, all speak of God's wrath followed by the coming of Christ and His kingdom.

When Jesus said that to Him gave all the prophets witness, we can see just how true that is.

And as we near the end of the judgement of the earth, and draw near to Christ's reign, the beast is readying the armies of man to resist Jesus and His saints. The earth has seen plagues and destruction since the day of the Lord. The sun and moon darkening and the rapture of the saints. Man has been in constant torment and fear from locusts from Hell, waters turned bitter and turned to blood. Fire from the sky and earthquakes. Giant hail. A relentless pouring out of God's wrath.

And at the end of all this, the representation of Babylon, the nation at the heart of the one world empire, is utterly destroyed in the span of an hour. Saved for last, God allows the people of the earth to see His righteous judgement upon it for the blood of the martyrs and the drunkenness of its fornication and abominations.

It is difficult not to see the United States as this city, especially given the merchants lament at the destruction of a great consumer nation. I believe that there is always a seat of Babylon, a country that embodies its spirit. Rome. London. The United States.

It is possible that should God be even more longsuffering than we reckon, it could be Hong Kong or some other nation that becomes the center for the beast. Every man feels like *surely these must be the final days.* I can't even imagine how they felt in WW2 for example. And yet even more horrors and evil were to come.

But reading this chapter, and the way it is described, it's difficult not to see things falling into place, faster and faster now. The beginning of sorrows feels imminent. And we long for the day when the angels sing out "*Rejoice over her, thou heaven, and ye holy apostles and prophets; for God hath avenged you on her."*

teachings.title: Mystery Babylon, the mother of harlots
teachings.summary: The great whore on seven hills is Rome and its apostate church, with the false religions sprung from her as harlot daughters, drunk with the blood of the saints she martyred in a trail of blood, until the beast and his kingdom make war with the Lamb and are overcome.
teachings.text:
The Whore, Mystery Babylon the Great. Mother of harlots and abominations. Drunken with the blood of the saints she martyred. The golden cup filled of her filthy fornication and abominations.

*That great city which reigneth over the kings of the earth*.

Sitting upon 7 mountains.
Given power by kings to rule.
Decked in purple and scarlet, gold and precious stones and pearls.

Sitting upon many waters, which are peoples and multitudes and nations and tongues.

Who is this great whore? This mother of harlots? This city on 7 mountains, that sits on many waters? Who has martyred the saints of Jesus and committed fornication and blasphemy and other abominations against God?

The city on seven hills is Rome. Its whore, the false religion and apostate church of the Roman Catholics. The harlot daughters all the other false religions that have sprung from it. The Orthodox and the Protestant. All those calling themselves Christ's, professing themselves to be holy and true. But drunk in her fornications. Idolatry. Blasphemy. The abominations of her golden cup. The power of her political control, given by the kings that committed adultery with her. The murder of millions of believers, in a trail of blood, as this empire of miry clay and iron has conquered much of the earth.

In the end, the 7th empire as described by Daniel (we will look at Daniel 7 tomorrow, along with the destruction of Babylon), will give the beast power to reign and will promote the worship of the beast who was, is not and is again. The fatal wound and Satan bringing the antichrist back to life as the man of perdition, and installing him as the head of the final one world government and religion for a short space.

*These shall make war with the Lamb, and the Lamb shall overcome them: for he is Lord of lords, and King of kings: and they that are with him are called, and chosen, and faithful.*

teachings.title: The Spirit of Babylon Is Whoredom
teachings.summary: Babel was the first works-based one world religion, and its spirit of idolatry is spiritual whoredom, which gives the context for the whore of Babylon.
teachings.text:
The study today on Revelation 17 and the Whore of Babylon, as well as tomorrow and the fall of that wicked city, has a lot of context coming from scripture, and concepts regarding the faithfulness of God, the betrothal to His people and the eventual marriage of the Lamb.

God has given us His law regarding marriage as a picture of His relationship with the saved. He is a jealous God. He speaks against Idolatry and having other gods, the blasphemy of worshiping graven and molten images or other creatures in His stead as fornication, whoredoms. Harlotry. He draws parallel to actual whores, allowing the daughters of your land to commit fornication and it destroying a nation, with the destruction visited on those who forsake Him to chase after strange gods.

There are many chapters and verses, but those I provided should give you some ideas of this major theme throughout the Bible.

The spirit of Babel, which is Babylon, and the empires and kingdoms that followed it, is one of adultery. Fornication. Whoredoms.

The original sin of the first one-world religion and government, just years after the flood, was to blaspheme God by building a tower to Heaven. Working their way to righteousness, that they may become as gods.

The Tower of Babel being a symbol of all works-based false religion. It's destruction, a picture of the end times.

Just as Babylon the empire, and Nebuchadnezzar and his idol, are a picture of the beast and his abomination. Harlots, taking from God what is His. Leading man to fornication.

This spirit of Babylon and its whore of self-righteous works religion, bowing to idols, worshiping the created more than the creator, is fornication.

God's law says that a betrothed groom can only put away his intended bride for fornication. And that no man may then marry her that has been put away.

This is the context, fulfilled in the end times prophecy.

teachings.title: The Whore and the Bride
teachings.summary: The whore and the Lamb's bride are set in contrast: trusting idols, rites or works is spiritual adultery against a jealous God.
teachings.text:
There is an interesting contrast made in the opening verse of chapter 17, and a verse from chapter 21:

**Revelation 17:1**
*And there came one of the seven angels which had the seven vials, and talked with me, saying unto me, Come hither; I will shew unto thee the judgment of the great whore that sitteth upon many waters:*

Revelation 21:9
*And there came unto me one of the seven angels which had the seven vials full of the seven last plagues, and talked with me, saying, Come hither, I will shew thee the bride, the Lamb's wife.*

The whore represents the unsaved and the wicked. The saved as the Lamb's wife, a bride.

The contrast and context of faithfulness and purity is intentional. A parable for a God whose name is Jealous.

*For thou shalt worship no other god: for the LORD, whose name is Jealous, is a jealous God.*

As Jesus teaches in Matthew 5:28

*But I say unto you, That whosoever looketh on a woman to lust after her hath committed adultery with her already in his heart.*

The same is true for us spiritually. When we put other gods before Him, even in our hearts, or trust in something other than Him to be our Lord and savior, it is adultery.

To make your faith one of idols and rites and vain traditions, trusting in our works and institutions made of man over the Lord who bought you, it is whoremongering. It is fornication.

And all those who lead others to this, especially when they claim the name of Christ Jesus, are harlots. Whores. And they serve the beast.

teachings.title: Miry Clay Mingled with Iron
teachings.summary: The miry clay mixed with iron may be false believers, chiefly the Catholic Church and her harlot daughters seeking political power.
teachings.text:
Delving a little bit deeper, we see Daniel talking about the feet of clay mixed with iron in the statue described in the dream. Traditionally in scripture the clay often represents believers. But here it is called miry clay, contaminated so as to not bind, mixed with iron which is the power of the state, the remnant of the Roman Empire's power.

This may represent false believers. Those who profess to be Christian but are not and have another gospel, primarily the Catholic Church.

Revelation, as we will see in chapter 17, will describe the whore of Babylon and her harlot daughters. From the description it clearly is the Roman Catholic Church, her harlot daughters the Protestants and various evangelical sects that have splintered off from the whore over the millennia. These churches claiming to be of Christ but seeking political power in the world.

 Miry clay mingled with iron.

And these 10 kingdoms of the final empire will be who gives the antichrist his power to rule.

teachings.title: Christ the bridegroom and the whore of Babylon
teachings.summary: Scripture pictures God's people as a bride and idolatry as adultery and whoredom, which is why the Roman Catholic Church is shown as the whore of Babylon, mother of harlots.
teachings.text:
Throughout scripture, God's relationship to His people is likened unto a marriage, Christ Jesus as the bridegroom, believers the bride. And just as married couples are joined together, become of one flesh, and adultery an abomination, so too scripture refers to chasing after false gods and idols as adultery.

The fornication with which a man may put away his betrothed is a like symbol of God's putting away a people who have gone after strange gods. He also calls it whoredom.

Scripture says to suffer not a harlot of the daughters of Israel, and it is both literal and symbolic of the call by God to be faithful unto Him.

That is why the Roman Catholic Church, the Whore of Babylon, mother of harlots, is represented this way. The cup of her fornication. It's all relative in terms to the bride, the believers in Christ who remain faithful.

The institution of marriage itself is a parable by which God teaches us of fidelity, and what it means to be a jealous God. How the man is head of the house, one body and one flesh with his wife, just as Jesus is head of His body, made up of the saints.

The one world religion of works and many gods will be used by the beast to gain control, until they turn on the whore and install the antichrist in the temple, proclaiming himself as God, Christ returned.

teachings.title: Traditions not even in the Bible
teachings.summary: The Galatians at least followed something God once ordained, but the mystery religion of Babylon and her harlot daughters trusts in extra-biblical traditions of men.
teachings.text:
And not to damn the Galatians with faint praise, but at least they were being beguiled into obeying something that actually was ordained by God in the Old Testament, if done away with in Christ.

How many people calling themselves Christian are putting their faith in something that isn't even in the Bible? That has no actual examples in scripture? That are twisted from incoherent cherry picking?

You can *almost* see the errors of those trusting baptism to save them, a natural man reading of scripture could lead them to that I suppose.

Unsaved people might be persuaded to think that the Lord's supper is some kind of magic ritual bringing them an installment of grace. (I'm speaking kindly of those holding on to damnable heresy, that it might jostle some in to repentance. But that benefit of the doubt doesn't mean they aren't damned).

But the entirety of the Mystery Religion of Babylon, practiced by the whore and her harlot daughters, is extra-biblical, vain traditions of men. Repent and trust in Christ alone. Believe God's word alone.

teachings.title: Speaking in tongues was known languages
teachings.summary: Tongues at Pentecost were real foreign languages for spreading the gospel, and Paul's tongues of angels is a hypothetical, not a doctrine.
teachings.text:
Speaking in tongues is described in Acts as the miracle of the disciples present on Pentecost, going out to the crowds of the feast in Jerusalem, and giving the gospel to those gathered from every nation in their own tongues. Their languages.

Judeans and Samaritans, who knew Aramaic, Greek. Hebrew, suddenly were speaking Parthian, and Mede, and Elamite, and Mesopotamian, and Phrygian, and Pamphylian, Egyptian, and Libyan and Latin, and a host of other languages, of all the scattered Israelites and others, gathered there that day. Prophesying the word of God and preaching the risen Christ.

This gift of the Holy Ghost continued in the early church, as it grew and served as a sign that brought the gospel to every nation, tongue and kindred. The God who had divided the nations and confused the languages in Babel, uniting them through the miraculous gifts of speaking in, and as we see in Corinthians, understanding or interpretation. Allowing them to be understood and to understand, that the gospel would be preached.

Even today, absent miracles but by the same grace, the same gift is given many who are quick studies in understanding languages, and given to allow the furtherance of the Gospel, bringing many to Christ.

The men in the church of Corinth, blessed with the more suspense gift, were puffed up, showing off, in the church. This was not only causing contention within the church, but as Paul says, gave a bad report to those without, that they were all babbling madmen. He admonishes them in Chapter 13 to seek rather Charity, the unfeigned and gracious love of others. Their profit and welfare. Their edification. Not our own.

And in the case of being able to speak in a tongue foreign to others, it serves no one but the speaker.

*Though I speak with the tongues of men and of angels, and have not charity, I am become as sounding brass, or a tinkling cymbal...For he that speaketh in an unknown tongue speaketh not unto men, but unto God: for no man understandeth him; howbeit in the spirit he speaketh mysteries. But he that prophesieth speaketh unto men to edification, and exhortation, and comfort. He that speaketh in an unknown tongue edifieth himself; but he that prophesieth edifieth the church.*

This is the sum of what Paul is teaching. He uses the idea that *even if* he were to speak in the language of angels, if no one understands it, it is useless, even to the speaker. Paul is not saying that they *are* speaking the language of angels. It is a hypothetical exaggeration given for instruction.

That some make an entire doctrine from that goes to show that those who wrest with scripture do so to their own destruction, because in the same scripture lays the context and the truth.

teachings.title: Pentecostal tongues are faked babbling
teachings.summary: Pentecostal tongue speaking is pride-driven faked babbling that edifies no one, against what Paul teaches.
teachings.text:
Pride and wanting to seem more spiritual, more holy, more blessed by God, in the eyes of others, feeds the Pentecostal movement and its foolish doctrines of speaking in tongues, the inane babblings of fools.

Of all the spiritual gifts, it's the easiest to fake. And when everyone present is afraid to call it out, they not only enable and encourage it, they'll even have some "interpreters" sharing the delusion and claiming they can understand the other person.

Since it is not any recognizable language, and because the noises being made have no bearing of prophecy, because they're not preaching the word of God but their own infantile speech, edifying no one, It is in direct conflict with what Paul is teaching here in 1st Corinthians.

It's to no one's benefit but the speaker. There's no charity in it, only pride and dishonesty.

teachings.title: Known by their fruits: Pentecostal delusion
teachings.summary: The saved can be corrected by scripture, but Pentecostals and Charismatics double down, hold works salvation and other heresies, and are known by their fruits.
teachings.text:
It is always amazing to me that the strong delusion people are under when they twist a small portion of scripture to serve their heresies, manages to fool others and bring them into the same delusion.

*But the natural man receiveth, not the spiritual  things of God for they are spiritually discerned.* And because they seek after the error of Simon the sorcerer, they don't know the spiritual things of God. They're blinded to them.

In chapter 3, Paul had already chastened the church for being carnal in regards to these gifts; *For ye are yet carnal: for whereas there is among you envying, and strife, and divisions, are ye not carnal.* That's the attitude they had was not spiritual, after the manner of God. He calls them children. And not in an endearing way. And understand he's speaking to people who actually possess these gifts. People who are actually saved by the Gospel through faith by grace. How much worse are these that fake it in order to seem spiritual? How much worse are they who, not being saved, not understanding the gospel, having faith in themselves instead of faith in Christ Jesus?

Simon, the sorcerer was saved. He took rebuke when Peter gave it. We see in the second epistle to the Corinthians that they too were corrected by Paul's letter.

One of the signs of a saved person is their ability to be corrected from scripture, by the word of God, because the Spirit that inspired it and the Spirit that indwells us are in harmony, being one. God is not the author of confusion. But you'll find that regardless of what you show them, Pentecostals and Charismatics will refuse to repent of their belief. They will double down. They will accuse you of not being faithful for trying to pop the bubble of their delusion.

And ultimately if you scratch the surface with them at all on doctrine, They will usually admit to some forms of work salvation. Or some odd heresy like oneness/modalism. That baptism is necessary for salvation. And a host of other weird doctrines.

Since these movements are led by wicked people who are often seen grifting the elderly and the desperate, begging for money for fake faith healing, prayer cloths, and assortment of other con jobs, but yet are not bringing anyone to Christ, You can see how Jesus warning that we shall know them by their fruits is so valuable. We can know they are false teachers because of the number of souls they've misled on the basic simple gospel of God.

teachings.title: Pride turns the gifts into doctrine
teachings.summary: False churches made the list of gifts primary doctrine out of pride and covetousness, and gifted men can use knowledge, governance or preaching for their own prominence.
teachings.text:
So. Knowing this, the list of examples given by Paul becomes incidental to the overall message. But in some false churches, the list became primary doctrine, and this heresy took hold precisely because of these sins in the hearts of men.

Wanting to feel powerful, special, better than. Given over to jealousy and vainglory. Coveting the attention and respect of persons given to those who are talented in some of the more prominent and manifest ways.

And so you have churches that place the expression of "spiritual gifts," as a witness to the "faith" of the person holding them. Of how special God must think they are, and wanting that for themselves.

Now, knowledge and wisdom are given every man his measure, by walking in the Spirit and study of the word, and from that the skill of preaching and teaching. And some will be puffed up, taking the gift of intelligence and time, studying to be approved by men, rather than God.

They use their knowledge to gain respect and power of others. And they guard dispensing it, rather than giving it freely as it was given them. They make themselves feel superior to others, and often seek to control those that they impress, rather than edifying others with humility and longsuffering. Their heart isn't right.

And some take their gifts for governance; organizational talents and judgement, and in pride make it about themselves, and their own power and prominence, not in glory to God.

And many take their ability to prophesy, preaching with great oration, and using that to gain a following and preeminence among the brethren.

The more comely parts thinking themselves better than the less comely but equally important parts.

And the less comely, envying and resenting the comely.

teachings.title: False prophets claiming God told me
teachings.summary: The less gifted who covet prominence turn to obscure doctrines and claimed visions and revelations, attention-seeking lies that lead others astray.
teachings.text:
If a man with wisdom and skill in leadership and teaching can be subverted by their own sin into taking advantage, imagine what deviltry the less skilled can of invent.

Lacking knowledge or wisdom, not diligently seeking the things of God to improve it, because that requires humility and self-discipline, they may focus on obscure doctrines, picked up third hand, that fascinate others and allow them to be beguiled. They become like a gnostic "master," dispensing this wisdom of men and the doctrines of devils, to lead astray silly women (and silly men). They are like Simon, and want to be considered special, and that is their avenue to achieve it.

These sometimes are the type that subvert whole houses. Unsaved vipers and apostates, who become false teachers. But they often are just pathetic saved people, who can't appreciate the gifts given them and the opportunity to serve others, because of their insecurities and own hangups.

This same impulse directs others to take the gift of prophecy, and not being great orators or filled with real knowledge and wisdom, they instead lean on the more sensational aspect of being a prophet; "seeing the future." Having "visions and dreams of what is to come," or extrabiblical revelations, claiming "God told me..."

It is attention seeking nonsense. But it is easy and many with itching ears want to believe. And the opportunity to manipulate others into validating your self-worth becomes more important truth, or serving God. Many may start as a lie, impulsively told, and then rationalized away as they experience the positive attention they coveted. Some are under delusion, given by God that they may be revealed a liar.

teachings.title: Faith healers are reprobate
teachings.summary: God still heals through prayer, but faith healers who fake miracles for money blaspheme the Holy Ghost and bring a bad report on God's power.
teachings.text:
The working of miracles, particularly healing, is another. God works through the fervent and effectual prayer of believers, often to heal the sick or bring about a miraculous outcome to a seemingly desperate situation.

In the case of the Apostles, those who had seen Christ risen, and been gifted accordingly to perform signs and wonders, the laying on of hands and the responsibility of growing the early church, the gift of healing was more than the hope of faith, but the power itself. And to those that were given it, like those around Samaria that Simon witnessed, worked miracles that the power of the gospel be made manifest, before the sealing of scripture.

And so, the evidence of miracles in our lives, or those that we are told about by others, is real. I have witnessed healing and recovery, miraculous events by my own reckoning, impossible becoming possible with the only explanation being the grace of God. Usually subtle. Sometimes not, but hardly ever "flashy." Rarely so definitive that the skeptic could be convinced, but to the believers, it adds to our faith. To some on the fence, it may help convict them in the Spirit.

But for the unscrupulous, those wishing to gain that prominence by the "gifts of the Holy Ghost," healing becomes an opportunity. Taking advantage of the desperate and brokenhearted. Performing flashy "miracles" of "healing," for filthy lucre's sake. To gain power over others with false hope.

I believe that these "faith healers" are all Reprobate. I believe they are blaspheming the holy Spirit when they claim they are performing miracles by His power. I think it is as wicked as those who claim to be mediums, talking to the dead to take advantage of mourning souls.

And it is incredibly easy to fake. Whether by the placebo effect, plants in the audience, the gullibility of the crowd. Those wanting to be part of something miraculous.

And sometimes, it might be through devils.

And when the frauds are exposed, it brings a bad report of the genuine power of God among the heathen. It shakes the faith of some and becomes a stumbling block to others.

teachings.title: Nadab and Abihu offered strange fire
teachings.summary: Nadab and Abihu died for adding their own works to God's commanded worship, the same error as those who follow traditions and church fathers over scripture.
teachings.text:
Over the course of 9 chapters we have seen the detailed instructions from the Lord to Moses, telling the Levitical priesthood of Aaron and his eldest two sons with great specificity, what they were to do regarding purification and sacrifice, where and how and when, and to what portion was God's, the blood, the burnt offering, the wave and the heave offerings, all of it.

And despite these clear and explicit teachings of the word of God, the first thing the newly anointed sons of Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, do is add their own works to it.

They light incense with a "strange fire," that is not the fire the Lord provided within the Tabernacle, but fire they made themselves. Their intentions seem to be good; they offered this strange fire before the Lord. They were seeking to praise Him, perhaps. Glorifying God with their own invention of religious expression, which the Lord commanded them not.

*And there went out fire from the Lord, and devoured them, and they died before the Lord.*

Aaron, chosen to be the first high priest of the Levitical priesthood, honored by his sons being chosen with him, to lead the congregation and perform the propitiations and oblations, to instruct the people in the ways of salvation through Christ by their adherence to the commands of God, in sanctification, showing the judgment of God that all the people may glorify Him. And he watches his sons burn to death, seeking their own righteousness.

The error of Cain is a natural impulse for man. To add our own works or to place new and strange ways of worship upon the things of God that His word instructs, is something we see throughout the Bible. And we see God's judgement upon those who seek their own sanctification, their own means of being holy. Who add to His word. Who brings their own works to the table of the Lord.

And yet, it continues.

Just as Judaizers and those teaching strange doctrines of men were creeping in unawares to the early New Testament churches. Just as heretics and apostates twisted the word of God, bringing another gospel, so too did *Nadab and Abihu*.

Those who claim that the "church fathers" were correct when they deviated from scripture and that there were hidden traditions, passed down from apostles, are the same as those who Jude wrote about in his epistle;

*Woe unto them! for they have gone in the way of Cain, and ran greedily after the error of Balaam for reward, and perished in the gainsaying of Core.*

They bring strange fire before the Lord.

teachings.title: Tongues were real languages, not babbling
teachings.summary: The gift of tongues was the Spirit-given ability to speak and understand other languages to spread the gospel, not the unintelligible babbling and floor-flopping of Pentecostals.
teachings.text:
One note I would have to this, regarding speaking in tongues and the understanding of tongues, regarding the Charismatics and Pentecostals; the gift of languages given by the Holy Ghost in those times was to the understanding by people of other languages. Not babbling and shouting nonsense that no one can understand. Partakers of the gift could be understood by those who didn't speak Greek or Hebrew or whatever the one blessed with the gift spoke, and interpreters could understand foreign tongues.

And this gift was for the spreading of the Gospel to the ends of the earth in those days. Not to make a show of it in a church, flopping on the floor like a fish.

teachings.title: One gospel: all are 1 Corinthians 15 Christians
teachings.summary: He refutes the teaching that Paul preached a different gospel from Jesus and Peter, showing 1 Corinthians 15 is the same gospel of the same risen Christ for all.
teachings.text:
**1 Corinthians 15:1-11**
*Moreover, brethren, I declare unto you the gospel which I preached unto you, which also ye have received, and wherein ye stand; By which also ye are saved, if ye keep in memory what I preached unto you, unless ye have believed in vain. For I delivered unto you first of all that which I also received, how that Christ died for our sins according to the scriptures; And that he was buried, and that he rose again the third day according to the scriptures: And that he was seen of Cephas, then of the twelve: After that, he was seen of above five hundred brethren at once; of whom the greater part remain unto this present, but some are fallen asleep. After that, he was seen of James; then of all the apostles. And last of all he was seen of me also, as of one born out of due time. For I am the least of the apostles, that am not meet to be called an apostle, because I persecuted the church of God. But by the grace of God I am what I am: and his grace which was bestowed upon me was not in vain; but I laboured more abundantly than they all: yet not I, but the grace of God which was with me. Therefore whether it were I or they, so we preach, and so ye believed.*

There is a weird, Judaizing movement of Dispensationalists that has been very active online lately, teaching the cursed, damnable heresy that there are multiple Gospels, and that the Gospel given by Paul is different than that of Jesus or Peter.

It is wicked as Hell.

They use this beautiful rendition of the Gospel in **1 Corinthians 15**, which was received by Paul, to claim it is a different Gospel than what was testified by Peter. But a simple reading of the entire epistle puts this foolish notion to rest. They are ministers sharing the same good news, of the same risen Christ. As believed by Peter, the other Apostles, James, the 500 brethren, and Paul on the road to Damascus.

The same risen Christ that those in Corinth had believed on. There is no other foundation. *But unto them which are called, both Jews and Greeks, Christ the power of God. And the wisdom of God.*

*For we are laborers together.* Giving the same Gospel that Peter gave to the Gentile Cornelius and his house. That Paul preached in Corinth, where he *reasoned in the synagogue every sabbath, and persuaded the Jews and the Greeks.*

If you run into someone claiming to be a "1 Corinthians 15 Christian" gently correct them that all Christians, from Pentecost on, from Jerusalem and throughout the world, are "1 Corinthians 15 Christians," be they Jew or Gentile.

If they push back, rebuke. If they refuse. Shake the dust, they oppose themselves.

teachings.title: Bullingerism, a false gospel
teachings.summary: He traces the Grace Movement to Bullinger and O'Hair and refutes its claim of different gospels in the Gospels, early Acts and Paul's epistles.
teachings.text:
The "Grace Movement," or Hyperdispensationalism, Bullingerism, etc, teaches a false gospel heresy that there's not only a difference between OT and NT salvation, Jews saved by works before Christ, and Gentiles by faith afterwards, but that there was a difference between the salvation taught in the Gospels, in the early  Acts, and the later Acts/Paul's epistles.

It was the late 19th/early 20th century creation of men like Bullinger in England and "J.C. O'Hair" in the U.S. and partially invented as a response to the rise of Pentecostalism in the 1800s, where the Pentecostalists insisted apostles and the gifts of the holy Ghost given to the first generation of the church continued in them.

But rather than simply debunking that by using the scriptures that define an apostle as a witness to the risen Christ, Bullingerians "discovered" a new doctrine, the "dispensation of the mystery" and that Paul's teaching of the death, burial and resurrection of Jesus was somehow different than the teaching of believing on the death, burial and resurrection of Jesus being taught to Jews by the Apostles, taught throughout Judea. To whom all the prophets gave witness. Which Jesus Himself charged the Apostles and disciples to preach to every creature.

It is a foolish and easily debunked heresy of a false gospel that requires one to "rightly divide the word" in a way that ignores Biblical accounts and clear scripture.

These false teachers claimed new revelation, that they'd been shown this truth by the Spirit, and that all of the Christians of that day who opposed them were in fact the false teachers, gate keeping this "hidden truth" from being discovered, of the "mystery" revealed to Paul.

My main understanding comes from interaction with its postulates, and searching scriptures to see if what they were saying was true.

It isn't, and so obviously false and another gospel, that it's almost impossible as a saved Christian to understand how they could believe what they do without being given over to strong delusion.

It also serves as a sort of mirror to the heresy of the "Hebrew Roots" movement that claims Christians should adopt OT laws and customs. Hyperdispensationalists teach, for example, that water baptism plays no part whatsoever in Christian tradition, after Paul received his "mystery."

It is also a strange cousin to those who deny Paul's writing, and say that the Apostle was a false prophet. That he taught a different gospel than Jesus, an equally absurd and easily exposed heresy. The Bullingerists and the Paul-deniers agree in principle, differing only in if he was of God or not.

teachings.title: The mystery: Gentiles fellow heirs
teachings.summary: He teaches the mystery revealed to Paul is that Gentiles are fellow heirs of the same body by the same gospel, preached to Abraham from the beginning.
teachings.text:
**Galatians 3** plays a foundational role in this hyperdispensationalist "Grace movement," as it's the main source for their teaching that Paul had a new mystery revealed unto him by Jesus, and it was a different gospel for the Gentile. But that's not what this says at all, in fact, as God often does in His word, He presents the idea of an unknown, a mystery, a dark saying, and then provides the answer key to understanding it. God is not the author of confusion.

Here, in verse 6, we have the answer to the mystery Paul is talking about; that the Gentiles should be fellow heirs with the believing Jews. Partakers of the Fathers promise in Christ, by the Gospel. Partakers and heirs OF THE SAME BODY. By the same Gospel. And that Gospel is identical to the one given by Jesus in **John 3:16**. Salvation by grace through faith. Eternal life for all who believe on His name.

Further Paul expounds that this mystery, of Christ going to the Gentiles that all nations be blessed, was always the plan, from the foundation of the world, and as explained in **Galatians 3:8**;
