*And the scripture, foreseeing that God would justify the heathen through faith, preached before the gospel unto Abraham, saying, In thee shall all nations be blessed.*

**Genesis 22:18**
*and in thy seed shall all the nations of the earth be blessed; because thou hast obeyed my voice.*

teachings.title: The Scofield Bible's heresies
teachings.summary: The Scofield study Bible twisted scripture to teach Zionism, dispensationalism and the kingdom given to the Jews, and to accommodate false science.
teachings.text:
**Jeremiah 4**, a clear prophecy of the destruction of Jerusalem coming from Babylon, has the distinction of being the "proof text" for the first of many heresies found in the wicked Scofield study Bible.

Written at the turn of the 20th century, but with roots back to Darby, Scofield took scripture and turned it on its head to embrace Zionism, dispensationalism, teach the wicked doctrines of the "failure of Christ church," and the Kingdom being given to the Jews.

He also sought to take the then-current trends in popular science, falsely so-called, that had been developed by antichrists to shake faith in God and His creation, and square them with the Bible so that Christians would accept things like Darwinism and dinosaurs. Scofield first published in 1909, and just a decade later was the infamous Scopes Monkey trial, that saw Modernists clashing with Fundamentalists over evolution, among many other things.

teachings.title: Scofield's gap theory from Jeremiah 4
teachings.summary: Scofield invented the gap theory between Genesis 1:1 and 1:2 from Jeremiah 4, so if he added to the first verse, none of his notes should be trusted.
teachings.text:
Scofield used his notes, interrupting the text of Scripture itself, column notes and foot notes, to add commentary and invent doctrine out of thin air.

Even today, a century later, this toxic corruption has infiltrated a majority of evangelical and many Baptist churches. Just as Judaizers had already taken root in Protestant sects and their seminaries, Scofield was the foot in the door to Bible colleges and KJVO churches.

But the heresies of C. I. Scofield were evident in the first chapter of the first book in the opening verses of the Bible.

In Genesis 1, he interrupts God's creation, to invent the idea that between verse 1;  *In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth.*

And verse 2 *And the earth was without form, and void; and darkness was upon the face of the deep. And the Spirit of God moved upon the face of the waters.*

That there was a span of an earlier creation, that millions or billions of years passed. That there was a "gap," between the initial creation, and the ultimate creation, and that this was proved by the vision of Jeremiah in chapter 4:23-26.

He claims that this passage "clearly indicates" that the earth had undergone a "cataclysmic change as a result of divine judgement." That we could see evidence of this pre-Eden, pre-Adamic destruction. That Jeremiah was seeing a vision of this past event. That this would match the geologists of the era, and their theories of the earth being billions of years old. That the earth wasn't made fully formed and stocked with life, but that God had made it before as habitations for angels, who fell, and was destroyed and left void and without form until he renewed creation for Eden.

The Gap theory was very popular for a time in American Evangelical circles, but is almost universally rejected today by believing Christians, despite their continued use of the Scofield, and acceptance of other heresy he taught.

But if he is inventing things in the first verse of the first chapter. Why do they trust anything else he wrote?

teachings.title: Dispensationalism is wicked
teachings.summary: Christians fall for dispensationalism by trusting study Bible notes and videos instead of reading the word, which teaches the law could not save and there is no other gospel for one people.
teachings.text:
Saved Christians who fall for the lie of Dispensationalism do so because they don't read the word of God themselves. They are led astray by wolves in sheep's clothing. They are brought to heresy by study Bibles' footnotes and column notes, twisting scripture and hobbling the power of the word. By charts and YT videos, and appeals after the flesh, and false promises of blessings for blessing a people who reject God and His salvation in His Son.

How can the law serve as a schoolmaster if your teachers say it had the power to save? That God's covenants don't expire, while those it was with no longer consent to the terms? If there is another gospel for one people that doesn't apply to the rest?

It is wicked.

teachings.title: Satan attacks the hope of His coming
teachings.summary: Satan pushes preterism, amillennialism, pre-trib rapture and doubts about Heaven, Hell and the preserved word to rob believers of hope and roots, leaving them withered in tribulation.
teachings.text:
It is the second coming and the rapture of the saints, the resurrection, the promise of being heirs to the Kingdom of Heaven, that Satan attacks with lies, so as to undermine that hope in those who he was unable to keep from salvation. To make those who believed unfruitful. Easily offended in persecution. To render them hopeless, and thus unable to do God's will and save more souls. To make their faith dead, being alone, as they withdraw like the Pharisees who believed on Jesus, but kept quiet for fear of the Jews.

To this end, Satan pushes lies such as the resurrection is past, that it is metaphorical, that the millennium reign is allegory, or already taking place. That the rapture isn't real, the lie that the gathering doesn't appear in scripture, or that it will occur before facing tribulation, so as to make believers be caught unawares.

He attacks the idea of Heaven being our inheritance, of Hell being eternal or real.

Preterism, amillennialism, post millennialism, pre-trib rapture, dispensationalism, "church ages," and other heresy, all designed to undermine our hope and leave us with *no root in ourselves,* on shifting sand. Not established, and so withering when the sun gets to hot.

Too many Christians believe the lie that God's word isn't preserved, that it's too difficult to understand, that they need others to explain every jot and tittle, never spending time in the word themselves. Never growing roots.

These shallow Christians are often carnal, worldly, carried away by the cares of this world. Afraid, angry, unable to show mercy, unable to be fruitful. Having no charity. Substituting the pure religion of being undefiled before God; visiting the fatherless and widows in their affliction, being unspotted from the world, soul winning...they instead cling to meaningless trappings of denomination, the church they attend, the rites and rituals they keep, making big shows of prayer, superficial expressions designed to justify them before man.

And so absent the roots, and not having faith in every Word of God being pure, they are unprepared for tribulations and divisions, and are left hopeless. Withered.

Don't fall into that trap! Don't let Satan snare you. Study to be approved unto God. Prove all things. Comparing scripture with scripture. Grow roots and be established that you may be unmoving in tribulation.

teachings.title: I shall go to him: babies are not born condemned
teachings.summary: David's words about going to his dead child show he did not believe babies are born guilty and condemned, refuting the doctrine of original sin built on Psalm 51:5.
teachings.text:
David continues his confession;

*Behold, I was shapen in iniquity; and in sin did my mother conceive me.*

He uses hyperbolic language to say that he is a sinner, born of a sinner, in his appeal for mercy.

There is much made of this passage, and all manner of doctrines that have been spun out of it. The primary being "original sin" as the idea that babies are born guilty, and condemned.

But the very account being mentioned show that David did not believe any such thing.

**2 Samuel 12:21–23**
*Then said his servants unto him, What thing is this that thou hast done? thou didst fast and weep for the child, while it was alive; but when the child was dead, thou didst rise and eat bread. And he said, While the child was yet alive, I fasted and wept: for I said, Who can tell whether GOD will be gracious to me, that the child may live? But now he is dead, wherefore should I fast? can I bring him back again? I shall go to him, but he shall not return to me*.

David, who knew he was redeemed by God, saved by faith, under the grace of the Lord, states plainly that he will go to be with his dead child in the end. That Heaven is their home.

While Psalms are dripping with doctrine, we should still always compare scripture with scripture, and gain understanding by the totality of the Bible, rather than out of context proof texts.

teachings.title: The fathers have eaten sour grapes
teachings.summary: Ezekiel 18 teaches against original sin: each man is judged for his own sin, and each generation must get right regardless of its fathers.
teachings.text:
This prophecy of Ezekiel is an often cited chapter regarding the doctrine of "original sin," which it clearly teaches against. But it is also cited by workies as to why turning from sin is part of salvation. But as always, we need to look at the context.

First, the parable among the children of Israel in Judah, that the fathers ate sour grapes, but the children's teeth are on edge, has to be understood. And it is something many of us are guilty of saying.

The judgment against the people had come, and Babylon was bringing them into captivity, and slaying many. So the younger generation was blaming the sins of the older generation for their troubles. That their fathers had eaten the sour grapes but they were the ones with the taste in their mouth. That God's judgment was unfair, and they were being punished for the sins of the father.

We often blame Boomers for ruining the country they inherited, and it is true. They set up high places and committed adultery and violence and rejected the God of their fathers. But many who complain the loudest about this are themselves living the same way, or worse.

Revival is on us, today and our present generation. As it says in verse 14, *Now, lo, if he beget a son, that seeth all his father's sins which he hath done, and considereth, and doeth not such like*...he shall surely live.

It is up to us to get right, regardless of the hole dug by our parents. This is true regardless of the age we live in. And if we haven't, there's always time for turning from our own sins, and walking in righteousness, through Christ.

The Lord has no pleasure in the deaths of the wicked, but rejoices in those who turn to Him and live.

The word of the Lord shuts down the idea of original sin condemning us. The sins and the righteousness of each generation are their own. A man isn't judged by the sins of their father or his righteousness, but by theirs. And vice versa.

We aren't condemned by Adam's sin, but by our own. We have his nature, being sons. But we all make our own way.

But the Lord challenged the people saying He is unfair, because in fact they did as their fathers.

teachings.title: We do not inherit sin
teachings.summary: He teaches Ezekiel 18:20 refutes using Psalm 51:5 for original sin, so infants who die are not condemned and go to Heaven.
teachings.text:
**Psalm 51**:1-
*Have mercy upon me, O God, according to thy lovingkindness: according unto the multitude of thy tender mercies blot out my transgressions. Wash me throughly from mine iniquity, and cleanse me from my sin. For I acknowledge my transgressions: and my sin is ever before me. Against thee, thee only, have I sinned, and done this evil in thy sight: that thou mightest be justified when thou speakest, and be clear when thou judgest. Behold, I was shapen in iniquity; and in sin did my mother conceive me.*

*Behold, thou desirest truth in the inward parts: and in the hidden part thou shalt make me to know wisdom. Purge me with hyssop, and I shall be clean: wash me, and I shall be whiter than snow. Make me to hear joy and gladness; that the bones which thou hast broken may rejoice. Hide thy face from my sins, and blot out all mine iniquities.*

The heretical dogma of "original sin," the false idea that we are born already guilty of sin inherited from our parents, passed on from Adam, is usually defended by using **Psalm 51:5** as a proof text.

**Ezekiel 18:20** contradicts this reading;
*The soul that sinneth, it shall die. The son shall not bear the iniquity of the father, neither shall the father bear the iniquity of the son: the righteousness of the righteous shall be upon him, and the wickedness of the wicked shall be upon him.*

We do not inherit sin. Sins that are imputed upon us are our own. We do not bear another's iniquity.

David's lamenting of his own sins, his sorrowful repentance in poetic hyperbole, isn't introducing a doctrine of original sin, Ezekiel's plain language that flatly states we do not carry the sin of our fathers, is not trumped by a hyperliteral reading of a Psalm.

Infants who die are not condemned by inherited sin. Because babies who die go to Heaven.

teachings.title: Alive without the law once
teachings.summary: He shows original sin relies on corrupt versions like the NIV and leads to infant baptism and limbo, while Romans 7:9 shows we die spiritually when we knowingly sin.
teachings.text:
I will note too that in order to wrest **Psalm 51:5** to say that babies are born sinning and carrying sin generationally, they use corrupt versions of the Bible like the NIV;

Surely I was sinful at birth, sinful from the time my mother conceived me.

Just like most other heresies, they need to twist and rend meaning that's not there to create proof texts.

And like most other heresies, they then need to build on their error to make it fit with other verses that clearly contradict their interpretation.

Sinning from birth, where a baby has no understanding of right and wrong, no sinful needs, only to eat, sleep and grow, no need to covet, is an absurdity. But if you accept this absurd doctrine, then you have to deal with the untimely deaths of infants. Miscarriages and still births. Young toddlers dying in their cribs.

If they are born sinning, and carrying the guilt of sin their parents committed, then those babies by necessity are damned.

And if infants without the law or understanding of right from wrong are sent to Hell for eternity, then that cruelty would offend people, especially mothers.

So, to square this seeming injustice with a perfectly just God, the invention of baby baptism, "Limbo," the extension of grace from Christ's sacrifice for sin extended to children to some arbitrary "age of accountability," and other strange doctrines were formed. Even going so far as to extend Calvinistic predestination to the infants, so that either some babies are elect, and others damned (James White), or by God's grace and mercy, all children who die young also happen to be elect (Reformers who know how evil White sounds).

The simple answer is found in **Romans 7:9**

*For I was alive without the law once: but when the commandment came, sin revived, and I died.*

The simple understanding that, at some point innocence ends, at the understanding of the law, knowing right from wrong, and we choose sin. And when we do, our spirit dies.

God is just. We must choose salvation in Christ, because we all inevitably choose sin. But those who have no capacity for either choice are not slain in the spirit, or in need of having it quickened again.

Infants are in the same state as Adam in the garden, before breaking the one commandment of God. Their needs cared for by others. Incapable of sin until they can willingly transgress the law of God. And afterwards, like Adam. They fall, and learn the knowledge of good and evil. They die to sin, spiritually.

There is no hard and fast rule of what age this happens. There are some who as soon as they gain understanding, choose evil. This could be as young as a toddler. It could be as a tween. It may be that a developmentally delayed or retarded person never fully gains this understanding, while others do and get saved or become wicked.

teachings.title: God judges the heart, not ignorance
teachings.summary: God does not impute sin to those without understanding, as with manslaughter and meat offered to idols, because sin comes from the heart.
teachings.text:
Rather than extrapolate out doctrines of men and vain philosophies to explain the incongruity of the wisdom of men with the wisdom of God, we should just accept what we know, and rightly judge. Babies go to Heaven, and God doesn't impute sin on people who have no understanding of their actions being transgressions of the law.

We see this in His law regarding accidental murder, manslaughter. God does not hold the blood against a person who by accident or negligence kills another, and provides sanctuary in the cities of the Levites, instructing those that judge them to not input the sin to them.

We see this in Paul's instruction to the Corinthians, regarding eating meat sacrificed to idols;

*If any of them that believe not bid you to a feast, and ye be disposed to go; whatsoever is set before you, eat, asking no question for conscience sake.*

What you don't know isn't a sin, and it's ok to not even ask. Just as you cannot be tricked into sinning. Our heart condemns us, not our actions. God doesn't unfairly judge us.

As Jesus says, in response to the hypocrisy of the Pharisees judging the disciples for eating without washing their hands; *Not that which goeth into the mouth defileth a man; but that which cometh out of the mouth, this defileth a man...But those things which proceed out of the mouth come forth from the heart; and they defile the man. For out of the heart proceed evil thoughts, murders, adulteries, fornications, thefts, false witness, blasphemies: These are the things which defile a man: but to eat with unwashen hands defileth not a man.*

Just as lust of the heart is the sin of adultery. Just as coveting begins in the heart, and our intention.

**Jeremiah 17:9-10**
*The heart is deceitful above all things, and desperately wicked: who can know it? I the LORD search the heart, I try the reins, even to give every man according to his ways, and according to the fruit of his doings.*

teachings.title: No doctrine on a parable alone
teachings.summary: Fools misuse parables, and no doctrine should stand on a parable alone, as with Abraham's bosom, since Lazarus was carried to Abraham in heaven, not to a paradise compartment in hell.
teachings.text:
Just as the lame struggle to walk, the fool will misuse parables to their own purposes, drawing wrong conclusions and clouding understanding, rather than gaining wisdom.

While God uses parables throughout the Bible, Jesus teaching almost exclusively in parable to the hard-hearted Jews, so many have been used to create false doctrine. Proper application of parables should lay primarily on any explanation given in the text, (Jesus would often expound to the Apostles their meaning) but for those without clear teaching, the context should then be drawn by comparing scripture with scripture. No doctrine should stand alone on a parable.

The most obvious example is the false doctrine of "Abraham's bosom,' taken from **Luke 16's** tale of the rich man and Lazarus. Jesus is using their example to convey a message of urgency to the Jews, to repent and believe the gospel before its too late. To say that the prophets and Moses gave witness to His day, harken to them and believe. That those who don't are Hell-bound, no matter how rich they are. That those with dull ears and blind eyes will not believe, even if one were to raise from the dead.

But that the faithful, even the afflicted and poor in this world, who call upon the name of the Lord, are carried by angels into Heaven, honored and seated with Abraham, the father of faith. To be comforted forever.

The eisegesis and natural man logic required to turn this simple (and I believe, true) story into a doctrine that says that there is a place in Hell that's actually a compartment containing paradise, called "Abraham's bosom," and that that's where Old Testament saints went, is absurd.

The embrace of Abraham is specifically to show how even the lowly beggar, covered in sores, whose life was misery and rejection, someone lower than the dogs without the rich man's gate, rejected by the respecters of persons Jesus is addressing, is given an honor that Jews would be envious of. To sit down with Abraham, in the paradise that is God's heavenly kingdom.

As vs 9 says; *As a thorn goeth up into the hand of a drunkard, so is a parable in the mouths of fools.*

teachings.title: He led captivity captive
teachings.summary: Ephesians 4 says Christ rose with the keys of death and Hell and so led captivity captive, and gives no hint of freeing saints from a holding room in Hell.
teachings.text:
**Ephesians 4**
*4 There is one body, and one Spirit, even as ye are called in one hope of your calling;*

*5 One Lord, one faith, one baptism,*

*6 One God and Father of all, who is above all, and through all, and in you all.*

*7 But unto every one of us is given grace according to the measure of the gift of Christ.*

*8 Wherefore he saith, When he ascended up on high, he led captivity captive, and gave gifts unto men.*

*9 (Now that he ascended, what is it but that he also descended first into the lower parts of the earth?*

*10 He that descended is the same also that ascended up far above all heavens, that he might fill all things.)*

The letter to the Ephesians, Paul is writing regarding spiritual gifts and the like, and references **Psalm 68**, regarding the gifts given to men by God. Quoting verse 18, which says God ascended up on high, leading captivity captive, Paul takes the time to parenthetically mention that Jesus, who conquered Hell and Death when He was  risen from Hell, had first descended. Note the order of things. The line about captivity captive isn't part of that parenthetical point.

It doesn't say Jesus freed saints from some holding room in Hell. It doesn't even hint at it.

We are all captives of sin, and the wages of sin are death. But by rising from the dead with the keys to death and Hell, Jesus led captivity captive. Amen.

**Revelation 1:18**
*I am he that liveth, and was dead; and, behold, I am alive for evermore, Amen; and have the keys of hell and of death.*

teachings.title: The Harrowing of Hell is a Catholic fable
teachings.summary: The Catholic Harrowing of Hell misuses 1 Peter 4:6, which in context means the dead in Hell were shown their disobedience by Christ's resurrection, as those mocking Noah were destroyed in the flood.
teachings.text:
There is a false doctrine, invented by Catholics (among dozens of others), called the "Harrowing of Hell." In it, they say that Jesus didn't go to Hell for 3 days and 3 nights to be the burnt sin offering (a holocaust), for the whole world as the sole propitiation for our sins, as the Bible teaches. Instead they claim Jesus went to Hell on a Saturday to give the Gospel to Old Testament saints and various heathens who "lived a righteous life," or were "seekers of truth" like Virgil and Plato and other pagans, so they could go with Him to Heaven.

It is an incredibly natural man thing to believe, and it's no wonder that its origin comes from the false "Gospel of Nicodemus," supposedly written by the unsaved Pharisee in the Gospel of John who couldn't understand salvation and being born again, despite being a leader of the people, as Jesus pointed out.

*Art thou a master of Israel, and knowest not these things? Verily, verily, I say unto thee, We speak that we do know, and testify that we have seen; and ye receive not our witness. If I have told you earthly things, and ye believe not, how shall ye believe, if I tell you of heavenly things?*

But to give it some anchor in scripture, they pull **1 Peter 4:6** to claim it. The verse states "*For for this cause was the gospel preached also to them that are dead..."* Which relates back to the previous chapter:

**1 Peter 3**
*8 Finally, be ye all of one mind, having compassion one of another, love as brethren, be pitiful, be courteous:*

*9 Not rendering evil for evil, or railing for railing: but contrariwise blessing; knowing that ye are thereunto called, that ye should inherit a blessing.*

*10 For he that will love life, and see good days, let him refrain his tongue from evil, and his lips that they speak no guile:*

*11 Let him eschew evil, and do good; let him seek peace, and ensue it.*

*12 For the eyes of the Lord are over the righteous, and his ears are open unto their prayers: but the face of the Lord is against them that do evil.*

*13 And who is he that will harm you, if ye be followers of that which is good?*

*14 But and if ye suffer for righteousness' sake, happy are ye: and be not afraid of their terror, neither be troubled;*

*15 But sanctify the Lord God in your hearts: and be ready always to give an answer to every man that asketh you a reason of the hope that is in you with meekness and fear:*

*16 Having a good conscience; that, whereas they speak evil of you, as of evildoers, they may be ashamed that falsely accuse your good conversation in Christ.*

*17 For it is better, if the will of God be so, that ye suffer for well doing, than for evil doing.*

*18 For Christ also hath once suffered for sins, the just for the unjust, that he might bring us to God, being put to death in the flesh, but quickened by the Spirit:*

*19 By which also he went and preached unto the spirits in prison;*

*20 Which sometime were disobedient, when once the longsuffering of God waited in the days of Noah, while the ark was a preparing, wherein few, that is, eight souls were saved by water.*

*21 The like figure whereunto even baptism doth also now save us (not the putting away of the filth of the flesh, but the answer of a good conscience toward God,) by the resurrection of Jesus Christ:*

*22 Who is gone into heaven, and is on the right hand of God; angels and authorities and powers being made subject unto him.*

Jesus triumph over death and Hell and the eternal destruction of those in prison, Hell, is a like image to the people destroyed in the flood, the dead in sin, and the quick are those with eternal life in Christ, by the resurrection of Jesus, like Noah and the other 7, saved by water, (which is also a figure of baptism, which is *an answer of a good conscience toward God,* not how we are saved, but that we are saved).

The people in Hell were shown their disobedience by the resurrection of Jesus, just as they mocked Noah and were destroyed by the flood, they mocked God and were thrown into Hell to witness Jesus triumph.

teachings.title: Angels are not sons of God
teachings.summary: Scripture says God never called angels His sons and they do not marry, which refutes the doctrine of angel-human hybrids in Genesis 6.
teachings.text:
But what of angels, the creations of God who serve divine purpose? The hosts of heaven? Are they sons of God?

The Bible definitively says no**;**

*For unto which of the angels said he at any time, Thou art my Son, this day have I begotten thee? And again, I will be to him a Father, and he shall be to me a Son?*

*And of the angels he saith, Who maketh his angels spirits, and his ministers a flame of fire.*

...*For unto the angels hath he not put in subjection the world to come, whereof we speak.But one in a certain place testified, saying, What is man, that thou art mindful of him? or the son of man that thou visitest him? Thou madest him a little lower than the angels; thou crownedst him with glory and honour, and didst set him over the works of thy hands.*

And so we see that angels, while higher created beings than man, are in no way the sons of God, for they are below man in our dominion as sons of God. They aren't heirs to the promise. They are not partakers with Christ, they but serve God and His heirs, or rebel and tempt and accuse.

*Are they not all ministering spirits, sent forth to minister for them who shall be heirs of salvation?*

And all angels are spirit, not flesh, and not made in the image and likeness of God. Jesus, describing their limitations as He spoke of our glorified bodies in the resurrection; *For in the resurrection they neither marry, nor are given in marriage, but are as the angels of God in heaven*.

*The children of this world marry, and are given in marriage: But they which shall be accounted worthy to obtain that world, and the resurrection from the dead, neither marry, nor are given in marriage: Neither can they die any more: for they are equal unto the angels; and are the children of God, being the children of the resurrection.*

And so, mindful of what the Bible says (and does not say), we can draw doctrine that counters the claim of half-human hybrids made of spiritual things copulating with daughters of men. Angels are servants of God, ministers to us that are saved in Christ. That we are His children, His sons. What love He has for us! Amen.

teachings.title: Wise as serpents, harmless as doves
teachings.summary: Uses Matthew 10:16, Matthew 18:16-17 and 2 Timothy 2:16-18 to say grace without discernment is a vulnerability wolves exploit.
teachings.text:
**Matthew 10:16**
*Behold, I send you forth as sheep in the midst of wolves: be ye therefore wise as serpents, and harmless as doves.*

Many Christians often fall into the trap of being harmless as doves, while failing to be wise as serpents. 

We tend to feel the need to show Grace and to try to bridge peace and avoid conflict in every situation. To be as sheep in both mind and spirit. 

But the wolves take advantage of this. 

Jesus says to be as wise as serpents. To understand the context and nature of those who come into our lives and exert a negative influence. 

Part of the problem is that we don't attempt to discern the intents of the heart of the person who we are dealing with. Sometimes they'll say something that has a grain of truth, and in the interest of fairness and to seem reasonable, we will validate their premise. But their premise may be in bad faith. They may not be seeking a dialogue and to come to an understanding. Their intent is to throw bombs. Sow discord. To validate slander in the interest of promoting their own agenda. 

Even those who come in, in error, weak in the faith, maybe confused or wrong on some doctrinal point, or turned around by something they've heard that you know is wrong, we are warned against giving them space to stay in error and to spread it. 

**Romans 14:1**
*Him that is weak in the faith receive ye, but not to doubtful disputations.*

Yes we should cater to those who are ignorant, or convicted about something that isn't explicitly taught in the Bible, and we should attempt to correct them in love. 

But when they come in with doubtful disputations, that is creating turmoil and breaking the unity of the brotherhood of saints? Him we should not receive. 

Part of the problem often stems from the fact that we can't imagine how evil people might behave. We cut them slack. We give them grace based on our own conscience's sake, and show them kindness and mercy that only encourages and emboldens them. 

If they're simply in error, and too prideful or ignorant to accept rebuke, after you've admonished them kindly, shake the dust. 

**Titus 3:10**
*A man that is an heretick after the first and second admonition reject;*

This is especially true at the door when you are out soul winning. It does no one any good to get bogged down in the doubtful disputation. 

Defending yourself against a false accusation built on bad faith premises does nothing but legitimize the other person's point. 

If someone accused you of being incestuous with your mother, your reaction should not be "I am not!" it should be "You're wicked!" You don't defend yourself from slander by reasoning with the slanderer. You identify them for what they're doing, and rebuke them. 

But the issue becomes entertaining these sowers of division in a house of God or in a space of fellowship. Not throwing them out at the first sign of their behavior. 

What that does is allow their contention to grow, and to draw others in to deal with it. 

Further you encourage those sheep who aren't as wise as serpents, to compromise with the truth in order to bring peace to the situation. To try to smooth things over. To debate the slander as a point with merit. 

This only encourages wolves and keeps the confused and weak-in-the-faith brother, in error. 

God hates those who sow division. 

**Proverbs 6:14–19**
*Frowardness is in his heart, he deviseth mischief continually; he soweth discord. Therefore shall his calamity come suddenly; suddenly shall he be broken without remedy. These six things doth the LORD hate: yea, seven are an abomination unto him: A proud look, a lying tongue, and hands that shed innocent blood, An heart that deviseth wicked imaginations, feet that be swift in running to mischief, A false witness that speaketh lies, and he that soweth discord among brethren.*

We as Christians have absolutely no obligation to give them a platform to do the things that God hates, but rather to expel them and turn them over to Satan. 

If they are saved believers, God will deal with it. But the Bible says we are to treat them as heathen.

**Matthew 18:16–17**
*But if he will not hear thee, then take with thee one or two more, that in the mouth of two or three witnesses every word may be established. And if he shall neglect to hear them, tell it unto the church: but if he neglect to hear the church, let him be unto thee as an heathen man and a publican*.

You should not allow someone free rein to spew lies and indignities, to overthrow the faith of some.

Grace without discernment isn't biblical peace; it is a vulnerability that wolves exploit. 

**2 Timothy 2:16–18**
*But shun profane and vain babblings: for they will increase unto more ungodliness. And their word will eat as doth a canker: of whom is Hymenaeus and Philetus; Who concerning the truth have erred, saying that the resurrection is past already; and overthrow the faith of some.*

It doesn't matter if the vain babblings are denying the future resurrection of saints, slandering men of God and their works, discouraging the first love of the faith, soul-winning, or teaching a false gospel that says men are made elect by their genealogy. 

It increases ungodliness among the brethren and overthrows the faith of some.

teachings.title: What worship means in scripture
teachings.summary: Shows from the Hebrew shachah, translated worship, bow and obeisance, that Catholics change the meaning of worship to excuse idolatry.
teachings.text:
When a Catholic tells you you don't understand what "worship means" they are actually changing the meaning of the word to obfuscate their idolatry. 

The Hebrew term (שָׁחָה / shachah) is used 172 times in the Old Testament - translated as “worship” 99 times, “bow” 31, “bow down” 18, “obeisance” 9, “reverence” 5, “fall down” 3.

Defined as to depress/prostrate oneself (especially in homage to a superior, royalty, or God) i.e., to bow, kneel, or fall down in respect and deference.

The primary Greek term (proskuneō) accounts for the great majority of NT occurrences of “worship” (60 times) and is defined as "to fall upon the knees, touch the ground with the forehead/kneel or prostrate oneself" in homage or obeisance (whether to express respect or make supplication).

**Exodus 20:4–5**
*Thou shalt not make unto thee any graven image, or any likeness of any thing that is in heaven above, or that is in the earth beneath, or that is in the water under the earth: Thou shalt not bow down thyself to them, nor serve them: for I the LORD thy God am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation of them that hate me*

The term is explicitly rendered as "bow" in the 2nd Commandment, and carries with it no qualifiers or anything indicating that the "level of honor" given when bowing and making supplication to an image or idol has any bearing when considering the commandment. 

There is no question that bowing before an image or idol, regardless of what it is meant to represent, is strictly forbidden. 

**Deuteronomy 5:7–10**
*Thou shalt have none other gods before me. Thou shalt not make thee any graven image, or any likeness of any thing that is in heaven above, or that is in the earth beneath, or that is in the waters beneath the earth: Thou shalt not bow down thyself unto them, nor serve them: for I the LORD thy God am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation of them that hate me, And shewing mercy unto thousands of them that love me and keep my commandments.*

There is no mention of special religious worship for images of God, versus images of men, where it is allowed. 

Jeroboam created a new religion for Israel, with images of golden calves that were meant to represent the Lord God of Israel, and God destroyed them for it:

**1 Kings 12:28–32**
*Whereupon the king took counsel, and made two calves of gold, and said unto them, It is too much for you to go up to Jerusalem: behold thy gods, O Israel, which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt. And he set the one in Bethel, and the other put he in Dan. And this thing became a sin: for the people went to worship before the one, even unto Dan. And he made an house of high places, and made priests of the lowest of the people, which were not of the sons of Levi. And Jeroboam ordained a feast in the eighth month, on the fifteenth day of the month, like unto the feast that is in Judah, and he offered upon the altar. So did he in Bethel, sacrificing unto the calves that he had made: and he placed in Bethel the priests of the high places which he had made.*

And because of this false religion of idolatry, God judged Israel 

**1 Kings 15:30**
*Because of the sins of Jeroboam which he sinned, and which he made Israel sin, by his provocation wherewith he provoked the LORD God of Israel to anger.*

It is no wonder that every nation that becomes majority Catholic is judged by God, and is either wiped out with famine, war, disease or invasion and ethnic replacement.

teachings.title: Mary needed a Saviour too
teachings.summary: Applies Romans 4 to Mary, saying she was redeemed by her Lord and Saviour and that the Catholic view of a sinless Mary denies the gospel of justifying the ungodly.
teachings.text:
What shall we say then that Mary our sister in Christ, as pertaining to the flesh, hath found? For if Mary were justified by works, she hath whereof to glory; but not before God.

They don't believe the gospel. That Jesus justifies the ungodly, and His righteousness is given. A new man created by the baptism of the Spirit. And our sins and iniquity He remembers no more. 

So Mary has to be born sinless somehow, and fully obedient to the law her whole life, just as Jesus was. They can't comprehend Mary being redeemed by her Lord and Savior.

teachings.title: Responsibility, not free will, against Calvinism
teachings.summary: Says the argument against Calvinism is responsibility, noting that God always provides an escape according to 1 Corinthians 10:13.
teachings.text:
Free will isn't the argument against Calvinism. Responsibility is.

No one has unlimited, absolutely free, will. Everyone is influenced and penned in by their past choices, other people's choices, trauma and bad habits and all the dark ripples of sin that all combine to make limited the number of choices we have. 

But God always provides an escape. 

**1 Corinthians 10:13** 
*There hath no temptation taken you but such as is common to man: but God is faithful, who will not suffer you to be tempted above that ye are able; but will with the temptation also make a way to escape, that ye may be able to bear it.*

When we are tested, we have a choice to do the right thing, based on God's standards. And it's harder to do the right thing, because of sin. 

But we are responsible. And able to respond. So we have no excuse, except to deal with what's in front of you, in the Spirit. Even when it is hard.

It is by God's grace that He offered us His word, His commandments, His wisdom and prudence. We don't deserve a way out of the repercussions of sin. He not only forgives us, but provides us an escape. Both spiritually, in Christ but in this life, by His word. That's amazing grace.

teachings.title: Original sin and babies
teachings.summary: Says original sin is not biblical and that the idea that babies are born guilty was created to keep people in the Roman Catholic church.
teachings.text:
Remember, original sin is not biblical. And the idea that babies are born guilty, and if they die they go to hell, was created to keep people going to the Roman Catholic apostate Church. 

Protestants continued to varying degrees supporting this. Even going so far to say that babies that die who aren't elect go to hell.

teachings.title: Reformed theology and unconditional election
teachings.summary: Argues that Calvinist election rests on a quality in the elect, contrary to the gospel of grace, and warns that Reformed teaching is creeping into Baptist churches.
teachings.text:
Notice that the underlying false gospel of the Reformed theology Calvinist, assumes they are selected based on God's will, because of a personal quality they possess. This is antithetical to the gospel of grace, which is the love of God for all men, manifest in the life, death and resurrection of His Son, Christ Jesus. 

It places a condition on their so-called "unconditional election." They say things like this in pride, trying to sound humble. 

They make themselves their own christs. Jesus isn't even necessary in the equation, because God would have chosen them anyway.

Reformed theology is the most dangerous apostasy creeping in to Baptist and evangelical churches today. It has been there, but is suddenly increasing in scope, with reports of solid IFB churches being subverted by online ministries and pastors creeping in, denying their doctrine is Reformed, while they sow seeds of it from the pulpit. 

Beware these wolves. They appeal to believer's pride to act as the soil their corrupt seed is planted in. The thorns and thistles these tares produce become the next generation in the church.

teachings.title: Baptism for the dead in 1 Corinthians 15
teachings.summary: Explains that 1 Corinthians 15:29 is part of Paul's argument for the resurrection, not a recommendation of the Mormon practice of baptism for the dead.
teachings.text:
1 Corinthians 15:12-32 
***Now if Christ be preached that he rose from the dead**, how say some among you that there is no resurrection of the dead? **But if there be no resurrection of the dead, then is Christ not risen: And if Christ be not risen, then is our preaching vain, and your faith is also vain.** *

***Yea, and we are found false witnesses of God; because we have testified of God that he raised up Christ: whom he raised not up, if so be that the dead rise not.** **For if the dead rise not, then is not Christ raised: And if Christ be not raised, your faith is vain; ye are yet in your sins. Then they also which are fallen asleep in Christ are perished**.

**If in this life only we have hope in Christ, we are of all men most miserable. But now is Christ risen from the dead,** and become the firstfruits of them that slept. **For since by man came death, by man came also the resurrection of the dead**. For as in Adam all die, even so in Christ shall all be made alive. But every man in his own order: Christ the firstfruits; afterward they that are Christ's at his coming. Then cometh the end, when he shall have delivered up the kingdom to God, even the Father; when he shall have put down all rule and all authority and power. For he must reign, till he hath put all enemies under his feet. The last enemy that shall be destroyed is death. For he hath put all things under his feet. But when he saith all things are put under him, it is manifest that he is excepted, which did put all things under him. And when all things shall be subdued unto him, then shall the Son also himself be subject unto him that put all things under him, that God may be all in all. **Else what shall they do which are baptized for the dead, if the dead rise not at all? why are they then baptized for the dead?** And why stand we in jeopardy every hour? I protest by your rejoicing which I have in Christ Jesus our Lord, I die daily. If after the manner of men I have fought with beasts at Ephesus, **what advantageth it me, if the dead rise not? let us eat and drink; for to morrow we die.***

There is a wicked heresy among Mormons, especially, that there is a practice called "the baptism for the dead."

They take the verse *Else what shall they do which are baptized for the dead, if the dead rise not at all? why are they then baptized for the dead?* and create an entire ceremony where they go to graveyards, find names of people that weren't Mormon, and do an elaborate ritual where a member gets baptized in a pool in their Masonic temples, in the name of the dead person. They teach this will guarantee that spirit will enter the afterlife, and gives them points towards becoming gods. 

This is obviously wicked.

But many Christian denominations, even good Baptist pastors and preachers, misunderstand this verse, and while they will teach against the Mormon practice, they say it actually was some sort of pagan practice in Corinth that the church was caught up in. 

That's wrong. 

In this chapter, Paul is addressing the real problem among Corinthians, that they had some denying the resurrection. Not only the resurrection of believers, but of Christ Jesus. 

Paul then begins a series of rhetorical and logical arguments that lays out the hypothetical implications of the idea that Jesus didn't rise from the dead. 

If there be no resurrection of the dead, then Christ is not risen. If Christ is not risen, then the preaching of the gospel is in vain. Their faith is in vain. Paul and other ministers of the Gospel are liars. We would still be in our sins of Christ didn't rise from the dead. Those who are dead in Christ, fallen asleep, are actually perished. 

We would be most miserable. 

Paul then explains the truth, that by Adam death came into the world, but in the resurrection, Christ conquered death. 

He then says *Else what shall they do which are baptized for the dead, if the dead rise not at all?* If Jesus didn't rise up, He is dead. Why are we baptized in His name, an ordinance that pictures the death, burial and resurrection of Christ, in the name of a dead man?

Why would Paul stand in jeopardy every hour? Why risk his life to deliver the gospel? What advantage do we have as Christians if we do not have the resurrection? Eat drink and be merry, for tomorrow we die!

We see that, in context, it is an extension of the same argument. It isn't a recommendation for a practice invented in the fever dreams of Salt Lake City. It isn't a practice of the NT churches. It is not a pagan practice. 

It is simply the argument against those who doubt Jesus Christ rose from the dead, and the implications of that damned heresy.

While it's easy to laugh at the Mormons and profane idea of baptizing for the dead, which obviously has no efficacy or biblical support, it's important to note how evil this is. 

They will literally go and find relatives names or even total strangers and take it upon themselves to baptize in their name and claim that those people are now Mormons. It's as ghoulish as the Catholics trying to claim Charlie Kirk. 

It's a wicked process and evil minds come up with things like this. 

The LDS Church teaches that performing baptisms for the dead allows this "saving ordinance" to be offered on behalf of those who have died without accepting or knowing Jesus Christ or his teachings during their mortal lives.

Of course water baptism does not save anyone. But this is where that heresy leads. Believers baptism is the only biblical form of baptism that is taught. And it's an outward sign to others of what's in someone's heart.

teachings.title: The one test of a false teacher
teachings.summary: Says the one criterion the Bible gives for a false believer or teacher is whether they add works to the gospel, not behavior after being saved.
teachings.text:
The one criteria the Bible gives for identifying a false believer or false teacher is do they add works to the gospel. 

Not behavior after being saved. Not by how good they are. Not if they turn over a new leaf. Not if they clean up their life. Not by how righteous they act, what church they go to, or any other thing, but what they trusted in.

teachings.title: Ruckmanism: serpent seed, the Gap Theory and the KJV
teachings.summary: Rejects Peter Ruckman's teachings, such as serpent seed, UFOs and Jews saved by works, while holding the KJV as God's preserved word without correcting it from the Greek. Goes through his errors one by one: serpent seed, demons, UFOs, Jesus able to sin, "advanced revelation" in the KJV, and the Gap Theory from Scofield.
teachings.text:
Ruckman taught another gospel. It is wicked and accursed and all his other teachings that flowed from it were wicked and blasphemous and did not come from the KJV Bible. UFOs and new Adams on alien planets and the kingdom given to unbelieving Jews who were saved by works....all of it is evil. The divorces and the fruit of his ministry, wicked preachers who teach "Serpent Seed" and other wicked doctrine only adds to it. 

I don't care if you think he was right about the KJV (it's a perverted twisting of sound doctrine IMO), it cannot overcome his insane teachings. 

Imagine being correct that the KJV is the only Bible today we need and then being so spiritually blind that you pull damnable heresy from your own vain imagination instead of the rock of the word you supposedly champion. 

Good natured disagreement on the topic between brothers is fine, and there are many great pastors today who hold similar views on the providential nature of the beautiful Authorized Version. And while some could nitpick their opinions, God bless them for their standards and doctrines. Their fruit is a consistent gospel and soul-winning flocks, amen.

Lots of good pastors out there are wrong on one secondary doctrine or opinion. Hard not to be when Bible colleges and seminaries are out there, teaching for commandments the doctrines of men (especially around the Jews and the end times). 

But praise God those things shake out in the wash. Meanwhile, we all share an every word Bible, the blood of Jesus Christ and a great commission. Amen.

And I thank God Pastor Hyles stopped a bad habit he apparently had, of using the Greek to "correct" the King James. 

His moderate position bridges the gap between two extremes and his defense of the Bible his momma gave him is the sweetest KJVO testimony you'd ever need.

I can understand why someone who holds a similar (though not necessarily identical, or even more extreme) view on the inspiration behind the KJV would not like to be labeled a "Ruckmanite" as an argument-ending ad hominem. It means guilt by association with things that no sane believer would want to be linked with, and isn't fair. 

Serpent Seed and UFOs aren't being argued. In good faith, that label shouldn't be used unless they explicitly claim the whole mantel of Ruckman, or doctrines outside the stated topic of the wonderful Authorized Version.

Ruckman taught that Satan had sexual relations with Eve, resulting in the birth of Cain, a doctrine known as the serpent seed or dual-seed theory. This is detailed in his works, such as The Ruckman Reference Bible (first edition, p. 9) and The Book of Genesis (1969, p. 101-102, 118), where he suggests Genesis 3:15 implies Satan's seed, referencing 1 John 3:12 and John 8:44. He claimed this was "implied" rather than explicitly stated, but it lacks biblical foundation, contradicting Genesis 4:1, which explicitly states Adam fathered Cain. 

Cain was given by God the choice to correct his works-based sacrifice. He chose not to, and slew his brother and reprobated himself. By making him into a literal child of Satan, it removes the entire point of free will and faith given in the story. 

But if you teach that Adam and Eve were saved by works, that the Israelites were saved by works, and that the Millennium Kingdom will see a return to salvation by works, as the unbelieving Jews inheritance of the Kingdom hinges upon it, there's little constraining you to getting your doctrine solely from the inspired KJV, no matter how hard you protest for the Authorized Version.

Abortion is murder, life doesn't begin at the first breath. The blood of the innocent is upon the nation that tolerates and encourages the murder of babies, in the womb or out. 

Saved Christians cannot be possessed by demons or devils, and absolutely no one has any Bible-based reason to claim they know what demons look like (He described demons as small, winged creatures resembling flies or mosquitoes (Demons and Christians, 1976) and admitted to his own personal demon possession.)

Eve did not have sex with the snake, and the apple wasn't an allegory for it. (And Adam, biting the same apple implies some disgusting abominations.) Cain was Adam's son according to the word of God. Also, Adam did not have water for blood according to any version of scripture, despite what Ruckman taught. 

Ruckman believed UFOs were real, involving aliens with different blood types (e.g., black aliens with green blood, grey aliens with clear blood) and tied them to end-times events. He claimed the U.S. government collaborated with aliens, kidnapping citizens for experiments (Black Is Beautiful, 1996, pp. 230, 244, 291, 295-297, 310-311). He also suggested demons transport humans to other planets to “replenish” them (The Unknown Bible, 1984, p. 592).  
 
Ruckman insisted that Jesus could have sinned. This is more of sophistry and foolishness than the other strange doctrines he held. Jesus being tempted at all points as we are, yet without sin is the biblical doctrine. 

"Oh yeah, but He could have if He wants to!" is just dumb.

Ruckman held that biblical inspiration pertains to speaking, not writing, again a weird and unnecessary assertion that ignores the sundry times and diverse manner God has spoken to us. 

Ruckman claimed the KJV. provides “advanced revelation” superior to the original Hebrew and Greek texts. Some would argue this position with examples from the text. 

He did not. He claimed advanced revelation from the KJV taught him that the antichrist is a 10-ft. tall alien with a bad right arm, a bad right eye, landing in St. Peter’s Square in a flying saucer 600 feet in diameter and 60 feet thick, and implanting the mark of the beast with his "huge black lips."

He claimed that the KJV translators were being given an advanced prophecy in **Numbers 33:52**

*Then ye shall drive out all the inhabitants of the land from before you, and destroy all their **pictures**, and destroy all their molten images, and quite pluck down all their high places*

That choosing to use "pictures" for images, they were warning us about TV and photography being evil, without them even knowing it. Bizarre. 

In The Christian’s Handbook of Manuscript Evidence, Ruckman cited the rendering "churches" in **Acts 19:37**, when the Greek refers to "temples," as an advanced revelation, suggesting deeper spiritual insight not found in the Greek. What that insight is isn't immediately clear. Since it was regarding the building where an assembly gathers to worship (here a pagan assembly at that), church is the Modern English choice they used. Ok. What deeper meaning is there? Shrug.

He claimed typos and mistakes in the 1611 were of the Spirit, and not of the printers. He claimed that Easter was a pagan celebration, and ignored the 1611 containing a table to help Christians find the right date for Easter (Pascha) forever. Minds blown. 

Ultimately, he did what false teachers do. Bait the hook with some truth, and then reel folks in with absolute insane nonsense. 

Sheep's clothing. Appearance of righteousness. Etc. 

It is this legacy that has done more damage to the cause of KJV onlyism in modern English speaking nations, by tainting that truth, than anyone who says the Antioch manuscripts and Masoretic Text used by the translators are equal to the KJV in inspiration, preservation and power. 

Hope this helps explain my position.

This was going to just be a comment in the chat, but it's worthy of a post. "The Gap Theory" heresy.

Peter Ruckman taught the Gap Theory, asserting a time gap between Genesis 1:1 and 1:2, during which a pre-Adamic world, possibly involving Lucifer’s fall, was destroyed and left “without form, and void.” He discussed this in The Bible Babel (1964, p. 31) and The Book of Genesis (1970, pp. 11-16), citing support from heretic Clarence Larkin’s Dispensational Truth. The claim is that the geological record and "science" had to be reconciled to the Biblical 6 day creation. That since modern science had "debunked the Bible," they needed to make up absolute nonsense to square scripture to "reality."  

The Gap Theory stems from Scofield, and his first note in his incredibly destructive reference Bible. 

**Genesis 1:2**
*And the earth was without form, and void; and darkness was upon the face of the deep. And the Spirit of God moved upon the face of the waters*. 
 
Scofield’s Margin Note (Genesis 1:2): “The earth was without form, and void: Jer. 4:23-26; Isa. 24:1; 45:18 clearly indicate that the earth had undergone a cataclysmic change as the result of a divine judgment. The face of the earth bears everywhere the marks of such a catastrophe. There are no indications that it was the result of the original creation, but rather a judgment which ended the primal order. The Hebrew words tohu and bohu (without form, and void) imply a waste and empty state, not necessarily the original condition of the earth.”

I recently heard a Baptist pastor say "Let me tell you about the Gap FACT!" 

Let me tell you a BIBLE FACT, The earth is 6,284 years old, give or take a year. God created it in 6 days, by His Word, Christ Jesus, resting on the 7th. And that creation was good. Amen. 

I don't have time for modernists who reject the clear teaching of the KJV to use the words of unsaved charlatans like CI Scofield to get the world's approval. To make God's word fit into the world's ideas. 

How about the world conform to the word of God? How about that?

teachings.title: Demon possession and Catholic exorcisms
teachings.summary: Gives the Baptist view that demon possession affects the unsaved, doubts Catholic exorcisms, and cautions against dismissing all possession as mental illness.
teachings.text:
I think that 99.9% of Catholic "exorcisms" are fraudulent. Like entirely performative and made up. The same way so many of their "apparitions" and "mold on the window looks like Mary!" Or "this inanimate object bleeding! (It's an old magic trick)" are.

In Baptist circles, generally shared doctrine on demonic possession is that it only affects unsaved people (the Spirit within the saved prevents this) and that it often is the result of sin/occult practices inviting them in. This leads to those cases brought forward to either be prayed over, fasting, etc, or outright saying it isn't their problem. But deliverance ministries are pretty often called in and successful (there are many fraudulent, false gospel people calling themselves Deliverance Ministries, but legitimate practitioners exist, and many pastors either know a guy or know of a guy). 

It usually is a quiet affair, and not turned into a show of Latin and special FX nonsense. And the goal is to get the person cleaned AND saved. 

The problem with any false gospel form of exorcism is obviously this:

**Matthew 12:43-45**
*When the unclean spirit is gone out of a man, he walketh through dry places, seeking rest, and findeth none. Then he saith, I will return into my house from whence I came out; and when he is come, he findeth it empty, swept, and garnished. Then goeth he, and taketh with himself seven other spirits more wicked than himself, and they enter in and dwell there: and the last state of that man is worse than the first. Even so shall it be also unto this wicked generation*.

And finally, because saved Christians tend not to be anywhere near as superstitious as Catholics, there's a modern tendency to dismiss what is demonic possession as just mental illness or addiction or whatever. And so they don't even address it. 

Meanwhile, Catholics will turn to a supernatural explanation, even when it is just like drug induced psychosis. Basically two ends of a spectrum if you see what I mean.

teachings.title: The Septuagint myth
teachings.summary: Argues the Letter of Aristeas is a forgery, that no Greek Old Testament existed before Christ beyond fragments, that Matthew 5:18 shows Hebrew scripture in use, and that the LXX of Vaticanus and Sinaiticus is a 4th-century revision; answers objections.
teachings.text:
**The Septuagint Myth: Debunking the 2nd Century BC Narrative**

The traditional narrative of the Septuagint (LXX), a supposed 2nd-century BC Greek translation of the Old Testament (OT), is a historical fraud that cannot withstand scrutiny.

The claim—rooted in the pseudepigraphic Letter of Aristeas—that 72 Jewish translators from all 12 tribes, commissioned by Ptolemy II, produced a unified Greek OT is not only implausible but contradicted by manuscript evidence, textual analysis, and biblical context. 

As a defender of God’s preserved word in the Hebrew Masoretic Text (MT) and Byzantine Majority Text, I argue that the LXX, as known today in 4th-century AD manuscripts like Codex Vaticanus and Codex Sinaiticus, is a Roman Catholic fabrication, revised to align with New Testament (NT) quotations and shaped by the apostate Catholic Church’s agenda to alter scripture.

Below, I synthesize my case, grounded in the King James Bible (KJV), exposing the LXX myth and its unreliable minority text foundations.

**The Letter of Aristeas: A Forgery**

The Letter of Aristeas, dated to the 2nd century BC, claims Ptolemy II (285–246 BC) commissioned 72 translators—six from each of Israel’s 12 tribes—to translate the Torah into Greek for the Library of Alexandria. This story is a fabrication. 

No Egyptian records corroborate Ptolemy’s commission, and the letter’s miraculous account of identical translations reeks of legend, not history. 

The involvement of scribes from the 10 northern tribes, dispersed by Assyria in 722 BC (2 Kings 17:6), is anachronistic nonsense, as these tribes were effectively lost. Even non-Levite scribes translating sacred texts stretches credulity, given the Levites’ exclusive role in preserving scripture (Deuteronomy 31:25–26). The Letter is a pseudepigraphic attempt to legitimize Greek texts for Hellenistic Jews, not a historical record.

**Scant Manuscript Evidence**

Manuscript evidence demolishes the idea of a 2nd-century BC Septuagint. Only 1.7–2.6% of the OT survives in Greek from BC sources, per fragments like 4Q120 (Leviticus, 1st century BC) and Papyrus Fouad 266 (Deuteronomy, 2nd–1st century BC). These scraps, covering parts of the Torah and Minor Prophets, are far from a complete OT. 

No unified Greek OT manuscript exists from the 1st century AD, when the NT was written. The earliest complete LXX texts—Codex Vaticanus and Codex Sinaiticus—date to the 4th century AD, over 500 years after the supposed translation. These minority texts, riddled with thousands of variants (e.g., 6,000–7,000 NT differences), lack the reliability of the harmonious MT, which aligns closely with the Dead Sea Scrolls (DSS, 250 BC–70 AD). 

The DSS, with over 200 Hebrew manuscripts, confirm the MT’s stability, while Greek fragments show textual diversity, suggesting ad hoc translations, not a standardized Septuagint.

**Hebrew Primacy in the NT Era**

The NT assumes a Hebrew textual context, not a Greek one. 

In Matthew 5:18 (KJV), Jesus declares, “Till heaven and earth pass, one jot or one tittle shall in no wise pass from the law.” “Jot” (Hebrew yod, smallest letter) and “tittle” (scribal stroke) refer to Hebrew script, meaningless in Greek. This underscores that Hebrew scrolls, not a Greek LXX, were read in 1st-century Judean synagogues (Luke 4:16–20). The DSS, overwhelmingly Hebrew, and rabbinic practices (e.g., Mishnah, Megillah 4:4) confirm Hebrew’s primacy. 

While Greek was spoken, NT writers like Paul, fluent in Hebrew, likely translated Hebrew texts into Greek for their audience, not quoted a non-existent Septuagint. Similarities between NT quotations (e.g., Isaiah 7:14, “virgin” in Matthew 1:23) and later LXX texts (e.g., parthenos) result from natural translation of Hebrew terms like almah (virgin or young maiden), not reliance on a unified Greek OT.

**Almah and Translation Integrity**

The claim that NT writers quoted an LXX misreading of almah in Isaiah 7:14 (KJV: “a virgin shall conceive”) is baseless.

Almah, used seven times in the OT (e.g., Genesis 24:43, Rebekah as virgin), denotes a young, unmarried woman, often implying virginity in context (Song of Solomon 6:8). The NT’s parthenos (Matthew 1:23) accurately renders almah’s meaning, reflecting the miraculous sign of a virgin birth. Similarities with 4th-century LXX texts are due to shared translation choices, not NT dependence on a 2nd-century BC Septuagint. Like KJV translators, who used English terms (e.g., “charity” for agape) to convey meaning, NT writers rendered Hebrew into Greek, preserving sense over literalism. This explains overlaps without requiring a mythical LXX.

**4th-Century Revision**

The LXX, as preserved in Vaticanus and Sinaiticus, is a 4th-century AD Roman Catholic product, revised to align with NT quotations. These minority texts, produced in Christian scriptoria, show deliberate harmonization. 

For example, Isaiah 7:14’s parthenos in Vaticanus matches Matthew 1:23, supporting the virgin birth, while the MT’s almah is ambiguous. Origen’s Hexapla (240 AD) and the Lucianic recension (300 AD) demonstrate Catholic scribes editing Greek OT texts, often to reflect NT theology. 

The Catholic Church, an apostate institution of the 4th century, sponsored this revisionism, as seen in Jerome’s Vulgate (382–405 AD), which included the Apocrypha despite early fathers like Melito and Jerome questioning their canonicity. 

The Apocrypha’s inclusion, absent from the Jewish MT and warned against by Athanasius, reflects Catholic tampering, not divine preservation.

**Unreliable Minority Texts**

Vaticanus and Sinaiticus, the backbone of the LXX, are unreliable. 

Their 4th-century dating, largely affirmed by Catholic-controlled scholarship (e.g., Vatican Library for Vaticanus), faces providential questions. Sinaiticus’ authenticity is further doubted due to 19th-century forgery claims by Constantine Simonides, who alleged creating it in 1839–1840. While paleography supports their antiquity, their 6,000–7,000 NT variants contrast with the Byzantine Majority Text’s harmony, which underpins the KJV. Westcott and Hort, 19th-century heretics with liberal biases, championed these texts to undermine the Textus Receptus, driven by profit and unorthodox agendas. Their work, like Catholic dating, cannot be trusted against the MT’s fidelity, confirmed by the DSS.

**Objections Answered**

**Objection:** BC Greek fragments (e.g., 4Q120) prove a 2nd-century BC Septuagint.

**Response:** These fragments, covering only 1.7–2.6% of the OT, are disparate, not a unified text. They reflect localized translations, not a Ptolemaic commission.

**Objection:** NT quotations (50–80% LXX-like) suggest a pre-Christian Septuagint.

**Response:** Similarities stem from NT writers translating Hebrew texts, like almah to parthenos. Vaticanus/Sinaiticus were later harmonized to match NT, not quoted in the 1st century.

**Objection:** Jewish use (e.g., Philo) and early papyri show an early LXX.

**Response:** Philo cited individual Greek translations, not a standardized Septuagint. Papyri (e.g., Chester Beatty, 2nd–3rd century AD) are Christian, postdating the NT and reflecting revision, not a 2nd-century BC text.

**Objection:** Catholic scholarship is ecumenical, not controlling dating.

**Response:** The Catholic Church’s history of altering scripture (Vulgate, Apocrypha) and control of Vaticanus taint its credibility. Its apostate status by the 4th century undermines its role as a neutral arbiter.

**Conclusion**

The 2nd-century BC Septuagint is a myth, unsupported by manuscripts, contradicted by Hebrew primacy in the NT (Matthew 5:18), and exposed as a 4th-century AD revision in unreliable minority texts like Vaticanus and Sinaiticus. The Letter of Aristeas is a forgery, BC fragments are negligible, and NT-LXX similarities reflect translation, not a unified Greek OT. The Catholic Church’s apostate influence, from the Vulgate to Apocrypha inclusion, and the dubious scholarship of Westcott and Hort, confirm the LXX’s corruption.

God’s preserved word lies in the MT and the Byzantine Majority Text, faithfully rendered in the KJV. Let us reject the LXX myth and uphold the true scriptures.

teachings.title: Original sin, infant baptism and grace
teachings.summary: Argues that teaching original sin leads to baptizing babies as a work for grace, and that anything added to grace makes grace no more grace.
teachings.text:
The false teachings of "Original sin" are the root of most damnable heresy. The false teachings of it immediately stir the maternal to ask "What about my baby??!!" From there it becomes about works and cult-control

As soon as you are water baptizing babies because moms are freaked out about being told that if their kids die, they might go to Hell (Or maybe limbo,) you've put faith in a rite and a priest and a church. Not Jesus. And not a just God.

And the churches that teach this damnable heresy have convinced you to do a work for grace that's not in the Bible. 

From that point on, their people have accepted a lie, and so they will be invested in maintaining the lie, even when there is no scripture teaching it, at all. Even when they are shown why the handful of out of context scripture that they are told actually teaches baptism of babies is wrong. Spiritual blindness because of fear and pride.

Doing something to "receive grace" makes grace no more grace. 

Grace is the unearned and unmerited favor of God. Work, laboring, receives a wage, not grace. Anything that adds anything to create merit or to be deserving in any way, means you are going to receive your just wages. 

Death and Hell.

teachings.title: Calvinism and election
teachings.summary: Says Calvinism makes election rest on foreknowledge or God's sovereign will rather than grace, reads Romans 9 as about nations, and cites Ephesians 1:4-5 for predestination in Christ.
teachings.text:
Even so, Calvinism falls into the same heresy, making the election not of grace, but of foreknowledge and predestination, God choosing who is saved based on His "sovereign will." That they are elect because of something God saw in them. Some merit.

They also use **Romans 9**, which was written about nations of people, the very scripture dispensationalism uses to justify its own heresy towards Jews, except changing the election from a physical nation to another innate quality; their usefulness to God. 

**Romans 9:10-13**
*And not only this; but when Rebecca also had conceived by one, even by our father Isaac; (For the children being not yet born, neither having done any good or evil, that the purpose of God according to election might stand, not of works, but of him that calleth;) It was said unto her, The elder shall serve the younger. As it is written, Jacob have I loved, but Esau have I hated*.

Again, Paul is writing about nations, not individuals, and drawing the comparison between the children of promise through Isaac, and the inheritance of that promise through Jacob rather than Esau. 

Paul goes from **Genesis**, the first book of the Old Testament, through **Malachi**, the last to make his point, and that point is not that God pre-ordains who will be saved and who is condemned.

Rather God pre-ordains that His promise will be kept, and those that partake in the conditions for that promise, are heirs to it. In this case, the election of grace through faith in His word. 

**Romans 9:22-24 **
*What if God, willing to shew his wrath, and to make his power known, endured with much longsuffering the vessels of wrath fitted to destruction: And that he might make known the riches of his glory on the vessels of mercy, which he had afore prepared unto glory, Even us, whom he hath called, not of the Jews only, but also of the Gentiles?*

God predestined that those who believe on His promise will be given the gifts of that promise, being longsuffering towards the unregenerate Jews, that His mercy may be shown to all who believe, in Christ. 

For all men are called; The Bible says:

**John 12:32**
*And I, if I be lifted up from the earth, will draw all men unto me.*

And again:

**2 Timothy 1:9**
*Who hath saved us, and called us with an holy calling, not according to our works, but according to his own purpose and grace, which was given us in Christ Jesus before the world began.*

And:
**2 Peter 3:9**
*The Lord is not slack concerning his promise, as some men count slackness; but is longsuffering to us-ward, not willing that any should perish, but that all should come to repentance.
*
All are drawn, all are called. God's will is that no man perish. It is to His purpose that we avail ourselves of the grace given the whole world, whom He loves. *That while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us. *

But by making the election not of grace, but sovereign will, and not to all men, but the select few, they make the promise of God to no effect. That whosoever believes isn't whosoever, but the preselected few, drawn by irresistible grace and unconditional election. 

"Unconditional election," is an oxymoron, used as a fig leaf to say "actually, we aren't special boys. We are randomly chosen, basically." An election without conditions is not an election, not a choosing, but is a random decision. It is a false humility used to hide their pride. 

They don't believe in grace, but in their own worthiness. Even if they say they don't know why they are special, only that they are. 

**Ephesians 1:4-5**
*According as he hath chosen us **in him** before the foundation of the world, that we should be holy and without blame before him in love: Having predestinated us to be adopted his sons by Jesus Christ to himself, according to the good pleasure of his will.*

All who trust Christ are predestined in Him. That election of grace given the whole world, is predestined in Jesus according to the will of the Father. It is Christ Who was chosen before the foundation of the world. Not the special boys who believe themselves to be their own little christs, making grace no more grace.

teachings.title: The sons of God are believers, never angels
teachings.summary: Shows from John 1:12, Hebrews 1:5 and Matthew 22:30 that the sons of God in Genesis 6 and Job are believers by faith, not angels, and that the giants were already in the earth; answers the common objections.
teachings.text:
**"Sons of God" Are Always Believers, Never Angels:**

**1. The Bible Defines "Sons of God" as Believers Through Faith**

The Bible makes it clear how one becomes a "son of God": through faith in the Lord. John 1:12 states, "But as many as received him, to them gave he power to become the sons of God, even to them that believe on his name." This is the foundation—sonship is granted to humans who believe in Christ. Romans 8:14 adds, "For as many as are led by the Spirit of God, they are the sons of God," and Galatians 3:26 confirms, "For ye are all the children of God by faith in Christ Jesus." From the start, "sons of God" are believers, not angels or any other beings.

**2. This Definition Applies Across All Scripture, Rooted in Christ’s Eternal Work.**

Jesus is "the Lamb slain from the foundation of the world" (Revelation 13:8), meaning His redemptive work exists outside time, which itself is a creation. Old Testament believers, like Abraham, "rejoiced to see my day: and he saw it, and was glad" (John 8:56), and Moses "esteemed the reproach of Christ greater riches than the treasures in Egypt" (Hebrews 11:26). Even in Seth’s day, "then began men to call upon the name of the Lord" (Genesis 4:26). These men were "sons of God" by faith in God’s promise—Christ—long before the cross, because sonship transcends time.

**3. "Sons of God" in Genesis 6 Are Believing Humans, Not Angels**

In Genesis 6:2, "the sons of God saw the daughters of men that they were fair; and they took them wives of all which they chose." These are believers from Seth’s line, who called on the Lord, marrying ungodly women, leading to wickedness. Genesis 6:4 says, "There were giants in the earth in those days; and also after that, when the sons of God came in unto the daughters of men, and they bare children to them, the same became mighty men which were of old, men of renown." 

The "giants" (Nephilim) were already there before these marriages, not produced by them—proving the "sons of God" aren’t angels making hybrids. God blames "the wickedness of man" for the Flood (Genesis 6:5), not angels or their offspring. Angels can’t marry—Matthew 22:30 says, "in the resurrection they neither marry, nor are given in marriage, but are as the angels of God in heaven." The idea of angels as "sons of God" here is absurd; they’re not sons, and they don’t marry. Humans, made in God’s image (Genesis 1:26-27), are the focus.

**4. "Sons of God" in Job Are Believers in Heaven, Not Angels**

Job 1:6 and 2:1 say, "the sons of God came to present themselves before the Lord, and Satan came also among them." They’re in heaven, so they must be believers—only the redeemed go there (Hebrews 12:22-23). Satan’s "among them" but not one of them; he’s the accuser, not a son. Hebrews 1:5 proves angels aren’t sons: "For unto which of the angels said he at any time, Thou art my Son, this day have I begotten thee?" The repetition in Job 2:1 changes nothing—same believers, same contrast with Satan.

**5. Job 38:7 Ties "Sons of God" to Christ’s Triumph, Not Creation**

Job 38:6-7 asks, "Who laid the corner stone thereof; When the morning stars sang together, and all the sons of God shouted for joy?" The "corner stone" is Jesus (Ephesians 2:20), and this is His triumph at the cross, not the earth’s creation. "Morning stars" are angels, distinct from "sons of God," who are believers rejoicing in Christ’s day, like Abraham did (John 8:56). This happens outside time, reflecting Christ’s eternal victory, not a pre-human event.

**6. Angels Are Never Called "Sons of God" in Scripture.**

Hebrews 1:5 is decisive—God never calls angels "sons." They’re not made in His image (Genesis 1:26-27 applies to man), nor do they become sons through faith. "Morning stars" in Job 38:7 are angels, but "sons of God" stay believers. Satan, an angel, is among but not of the sons in Job, proving the distinction.

**But "Genesis 6’s ‘Sons of God’ Must Be Angels Because of the Nephilim!"**
