Some say the "sons of God" in Genesis 6:2-4 are angels, producing Nephilim as hybrids. But Genesis 6:4 says the "giants" were "in the earth in those days" before "the sons of God came in unto the daughters of men"—they’re not the offspring, just there already. The children born after became "mighty men," not hybrids. 

God blames "the wickedness of man" (Genesis 6:5), not angels. Angels don’t marry (Matthew 22:30), and sonship comes through faith (John 1:12), not angelic nature. These are believers gone astray, not angels.

**But "Job 1:6 and 2:1’s Heavenly Setting Implies Angels!"**

The heavenly scene suggests angels to some, but only believers enter God’s presence as sons (Hebrews 12:23). Satan’s there as an accuser, not a son—Hebrews 1:5 excludes angels from sonship. These are redeemed humans, like Abraham, in heaven by faith, not angels.

**But "Job 38:7’s ‘Sons of God’ Shout at Creation, Before Humans Existed!"**

If this is creation, how can humans shout? It’s not creation—it’s Christ’s triumph as the "corner stone" (Ephesians 2:20), seen outside time. Believers like Abraham rejoiced in it (John 8:56). "Morning stars" are angels; "sons of God" are the faithful, praising Christ eternally.

**But "The Majority View Says ‘Sons of God’ Are Angels!"**

The majority’s wrong—scripture trumps tradition. Hebrews 1:5 says angels aren’t sons, and Genesis 6 blames man, not angels. Faith defines sonship (John 1:12), not angelic status. The Bible’s clear when you stick to its words.

From Genesis to Job, "sons of God" are believers—humans who call on the Lord by faith in Christ, the eternal Lamb (Revelation 13:8). Angels, like Satan or "morning stars," are never sons; they don’t marry, aren’t in God’s image, and don’t gain sonship. Every reference fits: Genesis 6’s wayward believers (with giants pre-existing), Job 1 and 2’s heavenly redeemed, Job 38’s timeless praisers of Christ. The KJV leaves no room for doubt—sonship is human, through faith, forever tied to Jesus.

God is not the author of confusion. If your interpretation of scripture causes a contradiction, creates a question that cannot be answered by comparing scripture to scripture, then it's wrong.

teachings.title: Every believer a priest, not a priest class
teachings.summary: Sets 1 Peter 2:9 and Hebrews 4:14-16 against sacerdotalism, showing Christ is our only High Priest and every saved believer is part of the priesthood.
teachings.text:
Catholicism is a godless, hopeless false gospel

**1 Peter 2:9-10**
*But ye are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation, a peculiar people; that ye should shew forth the praises of him who hath called you out of darkness into his marvellous light; Which in time past were not a people, but are now the people of God: which had not obtained mercy, but now have obtained mercy.*

**Hebrews 4:14-16**
*Seeing then that we have a great high priest, that is passed into the heavens, Jesus the Son of God, let us hold fast our profession.For we have not an high priest which cannot be touched with the feeling of our infirmities; but was in all points tempted like as we are, yet without sin. Let us therefore come boldly unto the throne of grace, that we may obtain mercy, and find grace to help in time of need.*

**1 Timothy 2:5**
*For there is one God, and one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus*

**1 John 5:11-15**
*And this is the record, that God hath given to us eternal life, and this life is in his Son.He that hath the Son hath life; and he that hath not the Son of God hath not life.These things have I written unto you that believe on the name of the Son of God; that ye may know that ye have eternal life, and that ye may believe on the name of the Son of God. And this is the confidence that we have in him, that, if we ask any thing according to his will, he heareth us: And if we know that he hear us, whatsoever we ask, we know that we have the petitions that we desired of him.*

Sacerdotalism is the heretical teaching that a priest class are essential mediators between God and humanity. That none come to the Father themselves, through Christ, Who is our High Priest, Who is our only mediator, but that we need men to act as intermediaries. 

Catholicism again spoils God to give to men the divine roles and responsibilities. 

As for priests, every saved believer is of the priesthood of Christ. Giving the gospel that others become part of that holy priesthood of believers. A peculiar people. Separated unto the gospel of God.

teachings.title: Calvinism makes grace no more grace
teachings.summary: Argues that election by a chosen purpose introduces merit, so the TULIP doctrines undo grace and are self-refuting.
teachings.text:
Rebuking a Calvinist, and it occurred to me that they make grace no more grace. If grace is entirely unmerited, but God "chooses" someone for His own purpose, that introduces merit. That person then has a predetermined purpose, and value, or God wouldn't have chosen them. Thus they are needed and inherently that's merit.

Even if you introduce the concept of limited free will, the Calvinist who doesn't hold to irresistible grace, and says "if not me, then He could use someone else," they are simply making a pool of merit, shared across a group. 

To make irresistible grace work in a limited atonement system, you'd have to then deny their other doctrine of God's sovereignty, and say it's random. Which of course isn't what election is. No one is elected by random. There are candidates, considered for their qualities, and chosen. A sovereign god, who micromanaged creation, couldn't leave it up to chance anyway. 

Calvinism, especially the TULIP doctrines, are self-refuting.

teachings.title: What the Bible says an idol is
teachings.summary: Defines an idol as any image or representation made by hands for religious service, whether of God, Christ crucified, angels or creatures.
teachings.text:
God says not to make idols. Not to bow before them or serve them. To not offer any kind of sacrifice to one, or to pray to them or to the spirit they believe it represents, for deliverance or favor. Not to light incense or candles to one.

According to the Bible, an idol is any image or representation, made by hands, representing either the living God in any form, including Christ crucified, or any representation of the creation, such as the goats of heaven, angels, a man, woman, or animal, used in religious services.

teachings.title: Was Mary good?
teachings.summary: Answers that Mary, like every believer, was made good only in Christ and called God her Saviour in Luke 1.
teachings.text:
Was Mary good?

I'm not good, either. 
But in Christ I am made good in Him, and saved by so sweet a Savior!

Just like my sister Mary. 

**Luke 1:46-47**
*And Mary said, My soul doth magnify the Lord, And my spirit hath rejoiced in God my Saviour.*

teachings.title: Praying to saints is superstition
teachings.summary: Says Catholic prayers to saints treat them as house gods or demigods and amount to a spell no less superstitious than pagan practice.
teachings.text:
Catholics will say they don't pray for the power of the saints to be given to them. But they always vacillate between "intercession" and actually having the spirit they claim to be praying to, to work a miracle themselves. They treat these idols and spirits as house gods or demigods. It is wicked as Hell

Note the casual blasphemy that a man was as perfect, complete in righteousness, as Christ, and that God gave this demigod a magic ability to find lost items, through an incantation. A spell basically, that invokes this magic power for the caster. 

It is no less superstitious and profane than common pagans, witches and sorcery.

teachings.title: Matthew 23 and the Catholic catechism
teachings.summary: Reads Jesus' woes on the scribes and Pharisees as describing Catholic and related false religion, noting that their dogmas keep people from believing the gospel.
teachings.text:
It's the most wicked of all their damnable heresies and doctrines of devils. 

Calling faith "sin." 

*For they bind heavy burdens and grievous to be borne, and lay them on men's shoulders; but they themselves will not move them with one of their fingers.

But woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye shut up the kingdom of heaven against men: for ye neither go in yourselves, neither suffer ye them that are entering to go in.

Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye compass sea and land to make one proselyte, and when he is made, ye make him twofold more the child of hell than yourselves.*

In **Matthew 23**, as Jesus preaches hard against the Jewish religious leaders who perverted the law and led their charges to perdition, He points out their pride in their fathers and their tradition, despite their fathers being the same that killed the prophets of God:

*Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! because** ye build the tombs of the prophets, and garnish the sepulchres of the righteous, And say, If we had been in the days of our fathers, we would not have been partakers with them in the blood of the prophets.** 

Wherefore ye be witnesses unto yourselves, **that ye are the children of them which killed the prophets.***

***Fill ye up then the measure of your fathers**.

**Ye serpents, ye generation of vipers, how can ye escape the damnation of hell?** 

Wherefore, behold, I send unto you prophets, and wise men, and scribes: and some of them ye shall kill and crucify; and some of them shall ye scourge in your synagogues, and persecute them from city to city: That upon you may come all the righteous blood shed upon the earth, from the blood of righteous Abel unto the blood of Zacharias son of Barachias, whom ye slew between the temple and the altar.*

A scathing indictment of the Jews, and the unbelieving Israelites that came before them, but it is also damning the Roman Catholic Church that came after, and those that swear by its "fathers" today.

Those who build up the tombs of the martyrs, the early saints whom the apostate church murdered by the millions. Who now change history and claim a false succession, robbing Peter, betraying Paul. 

Jesus sent among them prophets and holy men and scribes, those made righteous by faith, not by denomination and sacraments and rites, and they crucified them and burned them at the stake, flayed them and put whole churches to the sword. Often burning copies of God's word on the same pyre as the people found with them. 

They claim a lineage with men who persecuted the faithful from city to city, who slew the elect for a millennium, and then the harlot daughters of that protested their whore mother picked up where she left off, and slew Christians all the more.  

***Fill ye up then the measure of your fathers.*** 

Embrace your tradition. Vipers. Hypocrites. Serpents.

teachings.title: The Shroud of Turin
teachings.summary: Gives the history of the Shroud of Turin as a denounced forgery and points to 1 Corinthians 11:14 against its long-haired image.
teachings.text:
It shouldn't have to be said, but no, the so-called "shroud of Turin" is not "authentic," and has not been proved to be the "burial shroud of Jesus."

It was labeled a forgery by the Catholic Church at the time of its "discovery," when it was first presented to the public in the 1350s. The shroud was denounced as a forgery by the bishop of Troyes, Pierre d’Arcis, in 1389. 

Previous attempts to verify its authenticity have repeatedly come up short, and in fact seemingly confirmed it was a recent relic, made over a thousand years after Christ. Chemical analysis found the stains made with colored pigments in a gelatin medium. Historical analysis of the weave pattern used in creating the shroud wasn't in use during the time period of the 1st century, or the area of the Levant and Asia Minor, but was common in 14th century Europe. 

Anatomy analysis of the image shows that the proportions are wrong. The head too small, arms too long and site of wounds incorrect for "blood" patterns present. 

The new technique, "x-ray dating," does not accurately measure the cloth in a way that proves anything about its dated origin, especially given the fire damage, preservation and restoration it has undergone over the past centuries. True dating is next to impossible. 

Believers in the hoax point to this verse:

**Matthew 27:59-60**
*And when Joseph had taken the body, he wrapped it in a clean linen cloth, And laid it in his own new tomb, which he had hewn out in the rock: and he rolled a great stone to the door of the sepulchre, and departed.*

But they miss key context, that while His body was indeed wrapped in linen, Jesus head was covered with a separate piece of cloth:

**John 20:6-7**
*Then cometh Simon Peter following him, and went into the sepulchre, and seeth the linen clothes lie, And the napkin, that was about his head, not lying with the linen clothes, but wrapped together in a place by itself*.

Further;

**Isaiah 52:14**
*As many were astonied at thee; his visage was so marred more than any man, and his form more than the sons of men*

And of course;

**1 Corinthians 11:14**
*Doth not even nature itself teach you, that, if a man have long hair, it is a shame unto him?*

So no, that image going around isn't Jesus.

This idea that Mary remained a virgin was not taught by Tertullian, Irenaeus, Origen, and was considered only theoretically possible by a neutral Basil.

And it clearly states in scripture:

**Matthew 1:24-25**
*Then Joseph being raised from sleep did as the angel of the Lord had bidden him, and took unto him his wife: **And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son:** and he called his name Jesus.*

That the gospel of God is a series of transactions and works instead of a loving relationship between Him and His children.

**Acts 8:26-39**
*And the angel of the Lord spake unto Philip, saying, Arise, and go toward the south unto the way that goeth down from Jerusalem unto Gaza, which is desert. And he arose and went: and, behold, a man of Ethiopia, an eunuch of great authority under Candace queen of the Ethiopians, who had the charge of all her treasure, and had come to Jerusalem for to worship, Was returning, and sitting in his chariot read Esaias the prophet.

Then the Spirit said unto Philip, Go near, and join thyself to this chariot. And Philip ran thither to him, and heard him read the prophet Esaias, and said, Understandest thou what thou readest? And he said, How can I, except some man should guide me? And he desired Philip that he would come up and sit with him. The place of the scripture which he read was this, **He was led as a sheep to the slaughter; and like a lamb dumb before his shearer, so opened he not his mouth: In his humiliation his judgment was taken away: and who shall declare his generation? for his life is taken from the earth.**

And the eunuch answered Philip, and said, I pray thee, of whom speaketh the prophet this? of himself, or of some other man? Then Philip opened his mouth, and began at the same scripture, and preached unto him Jesus.

And as they went on their way, they came unto a certain water: and the eunuch said, See, here is water; what doth hinder me to be baptized?

And Philip said, If thou believest with all thine heart, thou mayest. And he answered and said, I believe that Jesus Christ is the Son of God. And he commanded the chariot to stand still: and they went down both into the water, both Philip and the eunuch; and he baptized him. And when they were come up out of the water, the Spirit of the Lord caught away Philip, that the eunuch saw him no more: and he went on his way rejoicing.*

The most comprehensive example of soul winning and the baptism of believers in the New Testament is given here, in **Acts 8**. We are shown that an unsaved person searching for truth will have opportunity to be given what he seeks. That saved believers will come I their life to preach the word of God. That a saved Christian must lead them through scripture to faith. That faith comes by hearing the word of God. 

And, importantly, we learn what is required to be water baptized, as an ordinance to testify of their found faith, that you *believe that Jesus Christ is the Son of God*.

The only examples given are all of adults. And all are believers first, the water baptism being an answer to their good conscience before God, as Peter writes. For he that biddeth him God speed is partaker of his evil deeds.

So then what are the dangers of not doing that?
Look to yourselves, that we lose not those things which we have wrought, but that we receive a full reward.

Is this epistle about salvation or about tolerating false prophets and in doing so, being partakers of their evil and undoing works and losing rewards (the payment God gives the saved for their work Romans 4)? 

Look to yourselves, that we lose not those things which we have wrought, but that we receive a full reward.

teachings.title: Tradition against the commandment of God
teachings.summary: Quotes Matthew 15:3-8 and says Jesus supported the death penalty for cursing father or mother.
teachings.text:
**Matthew 15:3–8**
*But he answered and said unto them, Why do ye also transgress the commandment of God by your tradition? For God commanded, saying, Honour thy father and mother: and, He that curseth father or mother, let him die the death. But ye say, Whosoever shall say to his father or his mother, It is a gift, by whatsoever thou mightest be profited by me; And honour not his father or his mother, he shall be free. Thus have ye made the commandment of God of none effect by your tradition. Ye hypocrites, well did Esaias prophesy of you, saying, This people draweth nigh unto me with their mouth, and honoureth me with their lips; but their heart is far from me.*

If you're against the death penalty for murders while Jesus was for it for those that curse their parents, you ain't right.

teachings.title: Believers cannot apostasize
teachings.summary: Argues from Romans 1, 1 John 2 and Hebrews 6 that the saved cannot fall away or believe a strong delusion, and that apostates never believed.
teachings.text:
**Romans 1:18–23**
*For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men, who hold the truth in unrighteousness; Because that which may be known of God is manifest in them; for God hath shewed it unto them. For the invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made, even his eternal power and Godhead; so that they are without excuse: Because that, when they knew God, they glorified him not as God, neither were thankful; but became vain in their imaginations, and their foolish heart was darkened. Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools, And changed the glory of the uncorruptible God into an image made like to corruptible man, and to birds, and fourfooted beasts, and creeping things.*

That which may be known of God is made manifest by His wrath revealed from Heaven. Man has no excuse. 

Many have this understanding, the law written in their hearts and the conviction of the Spirit, and the wonder of creation and even the example of mercy towards the saved believer...and still don't repent towards the gospel, perishing in their sins. 

But these people being described know the truth of God and hold it in unrighteousness. They do not wish to retain God in their knowledge. They reject the truth for a lie. They worship themselves and the created over the Creator. And God gives them up to a reprobate (rejected) mind. 

For those that not only had the manifest truth of God, but a clear articulation of the gospel of grace and reconciliation through faith in Christ Jesus, understand it, and even profess to assent to it, and then reject it? They are worse off than those that simply never hear or consider it. 
These have forsaken the right way;

**2 Peter 2:17**
*These are wells without water, clouds that are carried with a tempest; to whom the mist of darkness is reserved for ever.*

The apostates are reprobate, twice-dead. Not only dead and hellbound in the next world, but conscience seared and accursed in this one. 
**2 Peter 2:21**
*For it had been better for them not to have known the way of righteousness, than, after they have known it, to turn from the holy commandment delivered unto them.*

But we who have trusted the truth in our hearts have a more sure hope. We have the Spirit of truth to defend us from the spirit of error. Jesus said it is impossible to fool the elect. 

But for the fallen away, God gives them strong delusions as punishment for their rejection of the truth. 

2 **Thessalonians 2:10–12**
*And with all deceivableness of unrighteousness in them that perish; because they received not the love of the truth, that they might be saved. And for this cause God shall send them strong delusion, that they should believe a lie: That they all might be damned who believed not the truth, but had pleasure in unrighteousness*.

But praise God this is not possible for a believer. We are kept from falling by the power of God. By the witness of the Spirit. By the perfect work of Christ, knowing we have not believed in vain. 

**Jude 1:24–25**
*Now unto him that is able to keep you from falling, and to present you faultless before the presence of his glory with exceeding joy, To the only wise God our Saviour, be glory and majesty, dominion and power, both now and ever. Amen.*

Regarding the lie that those who are saved CAN fall away, can believe a strong delusion, can be fooled, the Bible teaches this is not possible.

**1 John 2:18–27**
*Little children, it is the last time: and as ye have heard that antichrist shall come, even now are there many antichrists; whereby we know that it is the last time. **They went out from us, but they were not of us; for if they had been of us, they would no doubt have continued with us: but they went out, that they might be made manifest that they were not all of us**. **But ye have an unction from the Holy One, and ye know all things. I have not written unto you because ye know not the truth, but because ye know it,** and that no lie is of the truth. 

Who is a liar but he that denieth that Jesus is the Christ? He is antichrist, that denieth the Father and the Son. Whosoever denieth the Son, the same hath not the Father: he that acknowledgeth the Son hath the Father also. 

Let that therefore abide in you, which ye have heard from the beginning. **If that which ye have heard from the beginning shall remain in you, ye also shall continue in the Son, and in the Father**. And this is the promise that he hath promised us, even eternal life. These things have I written unto you concerning them that seduce you. **But the anointing which ye have received of him abideth in you, and ye need not that any man teach you: but as the same anointing teacheth you of all things, and is truth, and is no lie**, and even as it hath taught you, ye shall abide in him.*

John continues;

**1 John 4:1–6**
*Beloved, believe not every spirit, but try the spirits whether they are of God: because many false prophets are gone out into the world. Hereby know ye the Spirit of God: Every spirit that confesseth that Jesus Christ is come in the flesh is of God: And every spirit that confesseth not that Jesus Christ is come in the flesh is not of God: and this is that spirit of antichrist, whereof ye have heard that it should come; and even now already is it in the world. **Ye are of God, little children, and have overcome them: because greater is he that is in you, than he that is in the world.** They are of the world: therefore speak they of the world, and **the world heareth them**. We are of God: **he that knoweth God heareth us; he that is not of God heareth not us.** **Hereby know we the spirit of truth, and the spirit of error.***

This is the unction of the holy Spirit. This Spirit of truth. That we hear those of God and reject those heard of the world by their false teaching. 

**John 10:1–5**
*Verily, verily, I say unto you, He that entereth not by the door into the sheepfold, but climbeth up some other way, the same is a thief and a robber. But he that entereth in by the door is the shepherd of the sheep. To him the porter openeth; and the sheep hear his voice: and he calleth his own sheep by name, and leadeth them out. And when he putteth forth his own sheep, he goeth before them, and the sheep follow him: for they know his voice. *

***And a stranger will they not follow, but will flee from him: for they know not the voice of strangers.***

We who are saved WILL NOT FOLLOW the stranger. We hear Jesus' voice. This is the promise of God.

**John 10:26–30**
*But ye believe not, because ye are not of my sheep, as I said unto you. My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me: And I give unto them eternal life; and they shall never perish, neither shall any man pluck them out of my hand. My Father, which gave them me, is greater than all; and no man is able to pluck them out of my Father’s hand. I and my Father are one.*

It is impossible for a saved child of God to fall away into apostasy. The trust in a false way, after knowing and assenting to the truth in their hearts. And it is impossible for an apostate to ever be saved once they've rejected the truth.

**Hebrews 6:4–6**
*For it is impossible for those who were once enlightened, and have tasted of the heavenly gift, and were made partakers of the Holy Ghost, And have tasted the good word of God, and the powers of the world to come, If they shall fall away, to renew them again unto repentance; seeing they crucify to themselves the Son of God afresh, and put him to an open shame.*

Anyone teaching that saved believers can reject the truth, believe a lie, have strong delusion, and apostasize, is wrong. It's heresy. It is not possible. 

Just as it is not possible for one who went out from us, who held the truth in unrighteousness and didn't wish to retain God in their knowledge, to ever come to the knowledge of the truth.

The Bible warns repeatedly against false prophets, false teachers who try to lead away people with itching ears by their vain jangling. Creeping unawares in order to spy out our liberty, and to make merchandise of us. 

Just like Satan, they try to make you doubt God's word in order to get you to sin. Or to believe foolishness. A saved believer can be led away into believing some heresies that are couched in the truth. 

These heresies are not necessarily apostasy. In order for it to be apostasy, it has to change the truth of God into a lie. 

Not all heresies are damnable. Not all heresies force someone to become apostates by their adopting them as a school of thought or a systematic that they apply to or over their existing faith. 

Nor does a heart that is no longer perfect towards God, but has added other elements of worship into their true faith, make someone an apostate. Yes they are not right and yes they are backslidden and yes they will face the chastening of God, but they have not lost their salvation. Theologians call adding falsehoods or heresies to true faith syncretism.

Solomon was guilty of this. He never rejected the Lord God or the temple he was given to build or the covenant and sacrifices that represented the Christ to come. But his heart was turned away to other gods by the love of his wives, partaking in their idolatry in addition to the truth he held in his heart. 

This applies to saved believers who use terms like repent of your sins, or who believe in some of the elements of Calvinism and predestination. Or who get caught up in other false doctrines, or never fully abandon the religion that they were won out of.

It may apply to someone who trusted in Christ at the door when a soul winner came and presented the gospel to them, but out of habit and loyalty and family ties they continue on going to a Catholic Church for example. 

Naaman was a Syrian general who asked the Lord for forgiveness for entering an idol's temple with his king, after believing on the truth of God. 

**2 Kings 5:18**
*In this thing the LORD pardon thy servant, that when my master goeth into the house of Rimmon to worship there, and he leaneth on my hand, and I bow myself in the house of Rimmon: when I bow down myself in the house of Rimmon, the LORD pardon thy servant in this thing.*

He had full knowledge of what he was doing and understood that it was wrong. I would assume Solomon did too, knowing the punishment he received through his son and the divided Kingdom for his spiritual adultery. 

But there are thousands and thousands of saved believers who after trusting in God, and the blood of Christ, neglect to walk in the Spirit, and read the Bible and learn God's ways. Those who simply went back to their Catholic church or their Mormon church or whatever apostate cult they were in, and while it may prick them in the heart they might not recognize why. 

But what they'll never do is trust in the false gospel of that church. Just as Naaman never trusted in the false gods of his people ever again.

And I think it's curious that this current heresy - that a saved believer could apostasize and could believe a false gospel in their heart, or reject the truth of God utterly, has been creeping up over the past few years. 

It's a twist on Arianism, which holds that a saved believer can become apostate and lose salvation. By adding the assurance of salvation to it, it allows them to lead away babes in Christ or people who aren't fully trusting the truth, and give them cover to chase after delusions. 

A believer they lead away with this vein jangling won't lose their salvation obviously. They also won't come to believe a lie ultimately because they can't. But they'll introduce doubt and they'll give a bad testimony and when the false teacher can get baby Christians to slander men of God, soul-winning efforts, the teaching of Truth, they ultimately hurt the cause of Christ.

But a nominal Christian, someone who has not fully believed unto salvation, it allows them to continue in whatever lie they are holding on to to avoid repentance. 

And it softens them up to be led away by whatever other strange doctrine the false teacher decides to impart upon their proselytes. He makes them twofold more the child of Hell than themselves.

These false teachers are attempting to have it both ways. They use the comforting banner of "Once Saved, Always Saved" as a Trojan horse to smuggle in a license for total apostasy, claiming a person can completely deny Christ, turn to paganism, or become an atheist, and that God will simply override their will and force them to believe in the end.

This teaching collapses under the weight of Scripture for several critical reasons. 

It redefines Faith as a meaningless past transaction, that purchased salvation, Rather than treating belief as a state of being. It becomes a transient action in their minds, rather than the reality their heart would live in if they believe the truth. 

Of course we reject Calvinism, so there is no forcing of faith or salvation onto someone who has utterly rejected it. The Bible says they're ever learning and never able to come to the knowledge of the truth. Jesus says depart for me I never knew you. 

It invents a class of people that the Bible doesn't say exists. There is a binary of those who believe and those who are condemned already because they have not believed. There is no third option. 

They purposefully overlook the power of the Holy Spirit and His purpose, to seal the believer, guide us to all truth and show the spirit of error. 

While that doesn't rise to the level of blaspheming the Holy Spirit, in my opinion, it sure does come close.

teachings.title: Pray to God against them that persecute us
teachings.summary: Believers may pray as David did for deliverance and against enemies who seek their hurt, asking God to send His angels to defend them, but must pray only to God and never to angels as false teachers lead people to do.
teachings.text:
**Psalm 35** is a model of prayer that carries with it both the plea for deliverance, and imprecatory, or negative prayers against enemies who seek our hurt.

In David's case, we understand that he was falsely accused, had enemies trying to literally kill him and destroy him.

We may not have the threat against our lives, but we can relate.

The Lord is our Judge of judges. We go boldly before the throne of grace, asking anything, that we may plead our cause. Asking God to get involved in our lives, to fight our fights.

We have such an awesome advocate in Christ Jesus and a Father Whose mercy and judgement is righteous and true. It is foolishness not to go before Him in prayer, knowing that He seeks our prosperity. Not the riches and accumulations of things, as the false teachers preach, but our overall benefit and success spiritually, that we may do His will.

So, of course when we have enemies in this life that seek our hurt, it would be natural that we get God involved.

*Draw out also the spear, and stop the way against them that persecute me*. That is to form a flank before us, a hedge of protection, like a wall of men, spear extended. A host to shield us from the advances against us. To show us and comfort us with the truth that He is our salvation.

Let our enemies be confounded and confused. Let them be scattered as the chaff. Let the angel of the Lord be our guardian. His children have guardian angels;

**Hebrews 1:14**
*Are they not all ministering spirits, sent forth to minister for them who shall be heirs of salvation?*

We can call upon Him to give them direction to not only shield us, but it persecute them that seek to do us harm.

But we shouldn't misunderstand that these ministering spirits are ours to control, or to plea to them. Many pray directly to angels, or archangels, which is wicked.

**Revelation 22:8–9**
*And I John saw these things, and heard them. And when I had heard and seen, I fell down to worship before the feet of the angel which shewed me these things. Then saith he unto me, See thou do it not: for I am thy fellowservant, and of thy brethren the prophets, and of them which keep the sayings of this book: worship God.*

We pray, as David did, to the Living God. He directs His hosts.

The Bible says that false teachers will mislead people into worshiping angels.

**Colossians 2:18**
*Let no man beguile you of your reward in a voluntary humility and worshipping of angels, intruding into those things which he hath not seen, vainly puffed up by his fleshly mind*.

Pray directly to God in all things. Pray for Him to dispatch His angels to defend us and attack our enemies, as David demonstrates here.

teachings.title: Righteousness from the God of our salvation
teachings.summary: Believers are made clean by God's imputed righteousness received by faith, not by their own works, and Roman Catholicism's denial of imputation at the Council of Trent is a lie.
teachings.text:
**Psalm 24** is a meditation on the truth of the Christ, the Lord, King of Hosts. Creator of all things, and the truth of the way of righteousness for those that trust in Him.

The gospel message of the Psalms, sung in the Temple, performed by the chief musicians and the congregation is the inspired doctrines of God, and the focus is entirely Jesus.

They may have looked through a glass darkly, but the concepts of Christ are hammered home, in verse after verse, chorus and stanzas of praise for the name of God, the Holy One, the Lord.

Here in the 24th Psalm, David asks *Who shall ascend into the hill of the LORD? or who shall stand in his holy place?*

Those with clean hands and pure hearts, who hasn't put their trust in vanity or lying lips, but who trusted the God of their salvation.

*He shall receive the blessing from the LORD, and righteousness from the God of his salvation.*

We are made clean of our sins, our hearts purified by the imputed righteousness of God. We receive these blessings by grace through faith, and access to the Kingdom, not by our own righteousness but by submitting to the righteousness that is God's.

**Romans 4:5–8**
*But to him that worketh not, but believeth on him that justifieth the ungodly, his faith is counted for righteousness. Even as David also describeth the blessedness of the man, unto whom God imputeth righteousness without works, Saying, Blessed are they whose iniquities are forgiven, and whose sins are covered. Blessed is the man to whom the Lord will not impute sin.*

There are false religions that deny the imputation of righteousness by faith in Christ. They say that imputation is not taught in scripture. This is a lie.

**2 Corinthians 5:21**
*For he hath made him to be sin for us, who knew no sin; that we might be made the righteousness of God in him.*

Our righteousness is as a filthy rag, our works could never justify us before a holy and perfect God. But these men believing vanity, and swearing deceitfully, teach that man needs to establish their own righteousness through works of the law, and many are misled by this lie.

**Romans 10:2–4**
*For I bear them record that they have a zeal of God, but not according to knowledge. For they being ignorant of God’s righteousness, and going about to establish their own righteousness, have not submitted themselves unto the righteousness of God. For Christ is the end of the law for righteousness to every one that believeth.*

Roman Catholicism rejects the idea that we are made righteous by receiving righteousness from the God of our salvation. The Council of Trent (Canon 11 on Justification) anathematized the idea that people are justified “by the sole imputation of the justice of Christ, or by the sole remission of sins” and that righteousness is "infused" by works, sacraments and "grace transforming a person," so that their own righteousness is established, rather than submitting to the righteousness of God.

But let God be true, and every man a liar. The generation of them that seek His face shall not be ashamed. All who come to the saving knowledge of Christ are made pure, in Him. Righteous, in Him.

**Titus 3:5–7**
*Not by works of righteousness which we have done, but according to his mercy he saved us, by the washing of regeneration, and renewing of the Holy Ghost; Which he shed on us abundantly through Jesus Christ our Saviour; That being justified by his grace, we should be made heirs according to the hope of eternal life.*

The truth of imputed righteousness of God being given the believer is found throughout scripture. And thank God for His grace and mercy. That our sins are washed clean, justified by the blood, and remembered no more.

teachings.title: The reprobate doctrine and the repent-of-sins gospel
teachings.summary: Says those who preach repent-of-your-sins make reprobates into saints, and asks who the dogs, swine, tares and goats in Christ's teaching are.
teachings.text:
If you don't understand what's being taught here, the process of hardening and eventually being given over to that hard heart, I don't know what to tell you. 

Your argument is with God.

People who preach a false "repent-of-your-sins" Gospel, always make Sodomites, who claim to have turned from their sin, into saints. They put them above all other men, because to them it's the ultimate proof of their false gospel. 

Their rationale "If turning from being a filthy sodomite, the worst sin, if that  doesn't get you saved, then nothing will!"

They'll claim it's evidence of the power of Christ to change lives. But it's really self-serving. They want to put their faith in the repentance of a homo, because it validates the faith they have in their own turning from sin. 

And no matter how many times it bites them in the ass, where the person they are putting up on a pedestal it turns out to be a false teacher, or a degenerate, or worse, They hold out hope for the next queer who makes merchandise of them by paying lip service to Jesus. 

And many of these vipers become false teachers, given authority over the faith. And they bring in damnable heresy, just as the Bible says they will. 

A large portion of the New Testament is devoted entirely to exposing this behavior and explaining it. 

Jesus teaches about false teachers. We encounter them in Acts. Paul writes against them repeatedly. Peter, Jude, and John talk about it. In the letters from Jesus to the seven local churches in Asia, he talks about it. In Revelation, in the end times, there's literally a false prophet leading a false religion in the name of the beast. 

We're told that they creep in unaware. Wolves and sheep's clothing. Leading away silly women and people with itching ears, bringing with them accursed false gospels. Reprobate concerning the faith. Ever learning and never coming to the knowledge of the truth. Impossible to bring them again to repentance to believe on the Lord Jesus Christ. Because they believed in vain. Cuz they continued not in the sayings. They went out from us because they were not of us.

Jesus tells us to not give that which is Holy to dogs, not to cast pearls before swine... That they'll turn and rend you. 

Who do people think the dogs are? Who are the swine in this teaching of Christ? What do people who don't understand the reprobate doctrine and who don't think sodomites are accursed, what do they think this is talking about?

Who are the thistles and briars? Who are the tares? Who are those compassing sea and land to make their follows twofold more the child of Hell than themselves? Who are the goats? Who are the sheep who don't hear His voice? 

WHO DO PEOPLE THINK THESE TEACHINGS ARE ABOUT?

God's word: "Hey, there are false prophets who will try and infiltrate your churches, and lead away people, watch out for them. This is how they got that way, and this is what they do. Biblical fundamentalism is how you protect yourself from them. Love you." 

And people refuse to believe Him.

teachings.title: One gospel in all ages
teachings.summary: Says there has always been one gospel, salvation by calling on the Lord and believing His word by grace through faith, and quotes Galatians 1:8-9.
teachings.text:
There was, is and will always be one gospel. The same in all ages. Salvation by calling upon the name of the Lord, believing His Word. By grace through faith.

**Galatians 1:8-9**
*But though we, or an angel from heaven, preach any other gospel unto you than that which we have preached unto you, let him be accursed. As we said before, so say I now again, If any man preach any other gospel unto you than that ye have received, let him be accursed.*

teachings.title: Nephilim and serpent seed are not biblical
teachings.summary: Says Nephilim, serpent seed and similar teachings about angels and demons are not biblical and quotes Colossians 2:18.
teachings.text:
Reminder that "Nephilim," "serpent seed" and other false doctrines about angels and demons that men use to make merchandise of simple people are not Biblical, and hurt the cause of Christ. 

***Let no man beguile you of your reward in a voluntary humility and worshipping of angels, intruding into those things which he hath not seen, vainly puffed up by his fleshly mind***

teachings.title: Soul winning guards against false teachers
teachings.summary: Says saved people who never go soul winning look for things to validate faith and are more open to false teachers, with 2 Peter 2:1-3.
teachings.text:
I think saved people who never go soul-winning tend to need something to validate their faith, because they don't see the power in the word in action. 

It makes them more likely to be taken advantage of.  

**2 Peter 2:1-3**
*But there were false prophets also among the people, even as there shall be false teachers among you, who privily shall bring in damnable heresies, even denying the Lord that bought them, and bring upon themselves swift destruction. And many shall follow their pernicious ways; by reason of whom the way of truth shall be evil spoken of. And through covetousness shall they with feigned words make merchandise of you: whose judgment now of a long time lingereth not, and their damnation slumbereth not.*

Faith grows by obedience, not by paying influencers and "archeologists," or any number of "holy land" scams people get taken in by.

teachings.title: Honour thy parents, not the tradition of men
teachings.summary: Jesus upheld the commandment to honor father and mother against the Pharisees' Corban tradition, and a generation that abandoned its parents to the state and its children to schools has broken God's multigenerational family order and reaped suffering.
teachings.text:
**Matthew 15:1-9**
*Then came to Jesus scribes and Pharisees, which were of Jerusalem, saying, Why do thy disciples transgress the tradition of the elders? for they wash not their hands when they eat bread. But he answered and said unto them, Why do ye also transgress the commandment of God by your tradition? For God commanded, saying, Honour thy father and mother: and, He that curseth father or mother, let him die the death. But ye say, Whosoever shall say to his father or his mother, It is a gift, by whatsoever thou mightest be profited by me; And honour not his father or his mother, he shall be free. Thus have ye made the commandment of God of none effect by your tradition. Ye hypocrites, well did Esaias prophesy of you, saying, This people draweth nigh unto me with their mouth, and honoureth me with their lips; but their heart is far from me. But in vain they do worship me, teaching for doctrines the commandments of men.*

Here Jesus reinforces the concept of honoring your father and mother, referencing the honor due them, and placing the command against cursing your parents as the direct counterpoint to the 5th Commandment.

**Leviticus 20:9**
*For every one that curseth his father or his mother shall be surely put to death: he hath cursed his father or his mother; his blood shall be upon him.*

The promise of a long life upon the earth for those that honor their parents, versus the death that those who fail to, who rob their parents, deserve.

The doctrine of the Pharisees held that a son who pledged his wealth to the temple, while yet holding on to it for his own use, could declare it as a gift, and exempt the person from their duty to their father and mother.

**Mark 7:11**
*But ye say, If a man shall say to his father or mother, It is Corban, that is to say, a gift, by whatsoever thou mightest be profited by me; he shall be free.*

This commandment of men made God's law to no effect. Creating a holier than thou excuse.

The curse of God upon a people who dishonor their parents, leading them to destruction, Is something that we have seen in modern times.

The baby boomer generation was the first to abandon the care and support of their parents to the state. To nursing homes. To their health insurance and Medicare. Food stamps. They also abandoned care of their children to schools and day cares. They broke the generational cycle God had put into place and we have all suffered for it.

They took the inheritance of their parents and squandered it while bragging that they're spending their grandchildren's inheritance on frivolous things.

It's fitting that many have broken relationships with their now dead parents, and their children and grandchildren. And sadly, they spend their final days alone in the same nursing homes they consigned their own parents to.

God put in place a system of family, of fathers in a hierarchy, wives in respectful submission to their husband, children under both, and honor due to the elders, to the widow indeed. A multi-generational family where children are arrows in the quiver of the father. Where each generation provides something to the unit, and stability to society.

But those that have broken this tradition the same is a companion of the destroyer. They've brought only suffering and death.

teachings.title: Jesus' brothers and sisters
teachings.summary: Argues from the Greek adelphos that the KJV is correct in saying Jesus had siblings through Mary.
teachings.text:
The Greek ἀδελφός (adelphos, "brother") & ἀδελφή (adelphē, "sister") literally mean "from the same womb" (ἀ- + δελφύς "womb"). NT uses ἀνεψιός (anepsios) for "cousin" (Col 4:10).  God inspired the "same-womb" words deliberately for brothers & sisters, not cousins.

The KJV is correct. Jesus had siblings through Mary.

teachings.title: Augustine, Pelagius and the persecution of separated Christians
teachings.summary: Shows how Augustine built original sin and irresistible grace against a Pelagian strawman, and how the same false witness was used against Cathars, Waldensians, Paulicians, Lollards, Anabaptists and Baptists who lived separated lives; all that will live godly shall suffer persecution.
teachings.text:
God's gospel is simple: grace through faith in Christ's finished work, which not only saves us from Hell and gives us eternal life in Jesus, the Spirit indwelling us, quickening our spirit, sealing us unto redemption, but God also graciously empowers us to choose obedience, His paths, His commandments, allowing us to strive for maturity in Him, and live separated lives as the New Testament demands. 

But over the centuries, and even today, that simplicity has been complicated, twisted, and poisoned by human systems that shift blame from personal choice to inherited inability or divine decree, and make grace no more grace. Leading men to destruction, and to pridefully destroy those that remind them of their error. 

Augustine's doctrines of Manichaean gnostic determinism, which he championed (including his novel theory of "original sin" as inherited corruption, "prevenient/irresistible grace" as the sole cause of good, and redefining predestination as preordainment) were advanced by redefining orthodoxy against a constructed "Pelagian" strawman opposite, and attributing to Pelagius heresies which were not held by the ascetic monk in Britain.

This approach functioned as a Hegelian dialectic: Augustine pitted his views against an exaggerated opposite to legitimize them as the necessary middle ground. By securing Pelagius's condemnation through imperial and ecclesiastical pressure, Augustine's theology gained dominance in the emerging Roman Catholic Church, influenced by political patrons in the late Empire.
This pressure of being made anathema and labeled a heretic served to make others who held the Eastern, Greek traditions of New Testament Christianity and understanding fearful of being similarly labeled. The writings of Pelagius and others who held his actual beliefs were either destroyed or allowed to fall into obscurity due to this fear, and so the lack of an extensive record lends even more credibility to Augustine's false doctrines.

Regarding original sin, Augustine's formulation—where Adam's sin transmits inherited guilt and an inevitable inclination to evil from birth—was not a settled orthodox doctrine in the earlier churches.

Pre-Augustinian Christian asceticism generally viewed human nature as inclined toward goodness, if incapable of being good outside of grace entered into by faith. That man is capable of moral progress in Christ, with sin arising from personal choices, habits, or imitation of bad examples rather than a deterministic corruption inherited biologically or legally.

Despite the smears, Pelagius explicitly affirmed God's grace and the Spirit's work as essential: grace opens the heart, reveals truth, exposes snares, enlightens with heavenly gifts, and forgives sins gratuitously. In his Letter to Demetrias and other texts, he described virtue as resulting from cooperation—human consent and effort partnering with divine aid to battle sin and imitate Christ's example of holy living. This was not sinless perfection by fleshly will alone (he acknowledged ongoing weakness and the need for maturity, or perfection in Christ), nor salvation by Old Testament law-keeping (which he recognized all fall short of), but pursuit of Christ's new commandment: loving God fully, with all your heart and loving your neighbor as yourself, all enabled by grace in the regenerated life of the believer.

Pelagius wasn't claiming sinless perfection or denying God's grace and human weakness/sin, we see a view of grace-enabled free agency and moral responsibility that was orthodox into the late 4th/early 5th-century Christian theology, particularly in the ascetic context—before Augustine's influence shifted the boundaries, and changed the conversation to say men are beyond responsibility, and can only be as "good" as God predetermined they be.

In the predominantly Greek, Antioch tradition, they had grown to see the natural end result of following the New Testament was living simply, loving others, being charitable, not given to drink, gluttony, fornication, adultery, coveting, etc. To put others' profit above your own.

This contrasted with late empire libertine culture in Rome, and the gnostic influence from Alexandria, which saw excess, and to the ascetic mind, sinful living being supported by the religious leaders there.

Augustine, from North Africa with roots in Alexandrian thought, a deep Manichaean past, and limited Greek proficiency, which introduced interpretive errors and conclusions, because he lacked the ability to understand the Greek texts. So Augustine diverged from earlier traditions, and his heresies have over time become foundational for many supposed Christians.

Pelagius's outspoken criticism of Roman hedonism and clerical hypocrisy made him unpopular among those Augustine later influenced to support his theology and anathematize his critic.

This reevaluation of the false charges of "Pelagianism," isn't meant to idealize Pelagius but recognize that the traditional "heretic" label stems more from polemical and political wrangling by Augustine and others, than from his actual teachings. In that context, we should reconsider how Augustine's legacy shaped Western Christianity—often at the expense of biblical exegesis and understanding of choice, responsibility, and grace-empowered obedience. That the simplicity of the Gospel and simplicity of life we should strive for, has been complicated by systematics of men. That the separated life and sanctification believers should strive for has been abandoned by many professing Christians. And that the teachings on lack of responsibility, or "inability to respond," has allowed those influenced by Augustine to fall well short of the potential given us by grace through faith, and the example of Christ we should actually be striving for.

The pattern is clear once you see it. Groups that actually try to live the separated, simple, holy life the New Testament calls for—loving God with all the heart, loving neighbor as self, putting others first, avoiding the flesh’s excesses—have always drawn persecution from the powers that be.

Look at the Cathars (the "pure ones"): extreme ascetics who rejected Roman wealth, hierarchy, sacraments, and papal authority in favor of purity and spiritual living. Rome branded them dualist heretics with false charges and launched a full crusade to wipe them out, massacring thousands in genocidal campaigns like the siege of Béziers in 1209, where "Kill them all, God will know His own" became the motto. Their crime? Living too separated from the corruption they saw in the Church, exposing the hypocrisy just like Pelagius did.

The Waldensians ("poor men of Lyon") did the same in a more biblical way: lay preaching, poverty, charity, vernacular Scripture (KJV-like emphasis on the Word for all), no oaths or excess, and rejection of papal authority and indulgences. They wanted apostolic simplicity. Rome excommunicated them, hunted them with crusades and Inquisition, burning them at stakes, drowning families, and slaughtering villages in the Alps—murderous false witness calling them heretics for rejecting infant baptism, purgatory, and clerical pomp. Why? Because their separated life exposed clerical hypocrisy, echoing the smears Augustine used on Pelagius.

This false witness—strawmanning true believers as heretics to justify murder—didn't stop with Augustine and Rome. It continued through the Reformers: Luther labeled Anabaptists "fanatics" and supported their execution; Calvin had Servetus burned and drowned Anabaptists in Geneva for rebaptism; Zwingli oversaw the drowning of believers in Zurich rivers; Anglicans imprisoned and executed Puritans and early Baptists for nonconformity. Even "Bloody Mary" (Queen Mary I of England) burned hundreds of Protestants at the stake during her reign (1553–1558), including men, women, and children who rejected papal authority and held to Scripture alone—false witness and torture to enforce high-church conformity.

Add in the Paulicians: 7th-century ascetics rejecting icons, hierarchy, sacraments, and papal-like authority, emphasizing Scripture and simple faith—they were massacred by Byzantine emperors and labeled Manichaean heretics (ironic, given Augustine's past). The Bogomils followed, dualistic but ascetic, persecuted by Orthodox and Catholic alike with burnings and exiles. Petrobrusians and Henricians (12th century) preached against infant baptism and corruption, only to be burned alive. Arnoldists rejected clerical wealth—hunted down. And the Lollards, followers of Wycliffe, pushed Bible in English, poverty, holy living, and rejection of papal authority—branded heretics, burned at stakes under English law, their bones dug up and scattered.

Even quasi-Augustinian sects like the Puritans and Plymouth Brethren, who pursued disciplined, world-denying holiness—plain living, strict Sabbath, moral rigor—faced hostility. Puritans fled England under Anglican pressure, facing starvation and native attacks; Brethren separated from established bodies and were often mocked or marginalized, even as they carried some Calvinist errors.

Rome and high-church Protestant systems alike use political power to silence those who live too close to Christ’s example. The simple gospel—grace through faith enabling obedience, choice, and separated living—threatens any institution that has grown fat on compromise. 

When believers start striving for the real thing, the powers that profit from laxity always push back with false witness and murder. History proves it: purity draws fire, leaving a trail of blood from NT martyrs through these groups to the burnings under Bloody Mary and beyond.

Augustine’s legacy perverted the gospel and weakened responsibility which excused the excess and rationalized the evil done to separated Christians with standards; the faithful who keep trying to live Biblical lives and are persecuted for it. The pattern hasn’t changed.

The Bible says, *Yea, and all that will live godly in Christ Jesus shall suffer persecution.* Jesus warns again and again that Christians will be hated for His name. That we will suffer persecution. Paul, Peter, John and Jude all write about scoffers, mockers, persecution for the faith, and the patience of the saints who endure it. 

We count ourselves blessed that in America, today, we aren't facing any real persecution. That we are free to worship, pray, read and own the Bible, go soul-winning...all without facing the same challenges our spiritual forefathers faced. Partly because our system of government was influenced by those fleeing persecution and sectarian violence. This gave us some protection against politically connected apostates coming against us for Godly living. 

But, another reason why Bible believing Christians today, including you and I, aren't facing the same level of persecution those 1st century NT Churches faced, or the various Christians throughout the last 2,000 years have faced, is because of our own lack of separation. Because we compromise. Because we shirk standards and give in to the flesh, and aren't as perfect, or mature, as we could be. Worldly. Carnal. 

Maybe we would have the crowns of glory given martyrs if we chose to live more like Christ and followed His example, the way these earlier Christians did.

**Luke 6:22-23**
*Blessed are ye, when men shall hate you, and when they shall separate you from their company, and shall reproach you, and cast out your name as evil, for the Son of man's sake. Rejoice ye in that day, and leap for joy: for, behold, your reward is great in heaven: for in the like manner did their fathers unto the prophets.*

teachings.title: No Mid-Acts dispensation
teachings.summary: Uses Acts 15:8-11 to show Peter and Paul preached the same gospel, and that all men from Adam through today have been saved by grace through faith.
teachings.text:
**Acts 15:8-11**
*And God, which knoweth the hearts, bare them witness, giving them the Holy Ghost, even as he did unto us; And put no difference between us and them, purifying their hearts by faith. Now therefore why tempt ye God, to put a yoke upon the neck of the disciples, which neither our fathers nor we were able to bear? But we believe that through the grace of the *Lord* Jesus Christ we shall be saved, even as they.*

"Mid-Acts" Dispensationalism holds that by chapter 15, a different gospel is made known unto Gentiles, that the Jews keeping the law of Moses still, despite believing, were under a dispensation of the law still. That the Gospel of Grace was given to Paul to preach to the Gentiles. That these verses "prove it."

A plain reading of the text shows that Peter held the same Gospel of Grace, and that it is not given by works of the law, but by the grace of the LORD (made distinct in the text, using the same capitalized distinction reserved for YHWH. A divine Lord, absolute authority, Greek is *Kyrios*).

*We believe that through the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ we shall be saved, even as they*. This sentence refutes any of the idea that Jews had a different gospel or standard, or that Peter's preaching to the circumcision was any different than Paul's ministry to the Gentiles. 

There is no "Mid-Acts Dispensation." All men, from Adam through today have been saved by the grace of God the Father, through faith in His deliverance, which is by His Son, Jesus Christ.

teachings.title: Job and the hedge of protection
teachings.summary: Job shows that both wealth and affliction are to God's glory, refuting both the idea that only the wicked prosper and the prosperity gospel, while Satan, the god of this world, works only within what God allows.
teachings.text:
Now God knows who Satan is and what he does and His pointing out Job is deliberate, and in so many ways this is done for our admonition, upon whom the end of the world has come.

If a man as upright and perfect in his ways can be sorely tempted by the persecution of Satan against him, If the hedge of protection may be lifted, to show the glory of God for such a man as job, how can we expect the small tragedies that befall us as believers to be any less to His glory?

If the Book of Job was one chapter, the lesson is present and clear. But as we'll see, there is so many more lessons to learn than simple perseverance in faith.

Satan of course credits the hedge of protection God has placed around Job and his family and the blessings of the holdings that he's acquired which are gifts of God, as the only reason Job's faith is so strong. He says to God that if He put forth His hand now and touched all that he had, Job would curse Him to his face.

I have seen an error among people similar to this, that says only the wicked prosper. Job shows this isn't the case and that wealth in itself is not a bad thing, but that all we have is a gift of God.

Then there's the prosperity Gospel types, who falsely say that if you're not successful and you're not succeeding, that you're not right with God.

But here we humbly learn that whether we are blessed or cursed, all is to His glory. As Paul writes:

**Philippians 4:12**
*I know both how to be abased, and I know how to abound: every where and in all things I am instructed both to be full and to be hungry, both to abound and to suffer need*.

Whether you're in good times or bad times or the mix most of us find ourselves in, it's all to the glory of God. His grace is sufficient.

Now the Lord says to Satan, *behold all that he hath is in thy power* but bars him from doing harm to Job physically.

The prime interpretation of this is that God has granted Satan special permission to afflict Job, And that is a fair reading of the text, especially in light of the hedge of protection Satan says God has placed about Job. But, as I've mentioned, the Bible says that Satan is the god of this world, That he is the prince of the power of the air, ruler of this world. Not as God, but as having influence and power over the things of this Earth.

So is the Lord reminding Satan, or enabling him? It's difficult to say. But we should keep it in mind always.

**Ephesians 6:12**
*For we wrestle not against flesh and blood, but against principalities, against powers, against the rulers of the darkness of this world, against spiritual wickedness in high places.*

But regardless, Satan is given the power to affect all that Job has, if not his person. And in one day, he does his worst.

First we see that his sons and his daughters were eating and drinking wine and in the eldest brother's house, this detail is given before the rest, creating tension in the reader.

Then the messengers begin to arrive. One tells of the oxen and asses killed by marauding Sabeans, who are from the south, where modern Yemen is.

Then another arrives to say that the fire of God reigned from Heaven on the sheep in the servants and consumed them.

When God gave permission to Satan to do what he will, he gave him access to the fire of God that rains from Heaven.

**Revelation 13:11-13**
*And I beheld another beast coming up out of the earth; and he had two horns like a lamb, and he spake as a dragon. And he exerciseth all the power of the first beast before him, and causeth the earth and them which dwell therein to worship the first beast, whose deadly wound was healed. And he doeth great wonders, so that he maketh fire come down from heaven on the earth in the sight of men*

The false prophet of the Antichrist will have this power and ability, And it will cause the unsaved to worship the beast and his image.

teachings.title: The preserved word against critical text claims
teachings.summary: Says denying that God preserved His word, with critical text claims, opens the door to cults like Mormonism, and thanks God for the preserved King James Bible.
teachings.text:
The false doctrine that the Bible isn't preserved by God, and that it contains errors that "Critical Textism" addresses by "favoring the oldest and best" sources (an assertion), leads to things like Mormonism being able to say it's corrupt, so anything goes. 

Thank God for the King James Bible. His inspired word, preserved perfectly, without error.

teachings.title: Against continual believism
teachings.summary: Answers the teaching that belief must be maintained until death, using John 3, Galatians 4, 1 Corinthians 15 and Hebrews 6 to show that vain faith means never having believed.
teachings.text:
**John 3:16-18**
*For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that **whosoever believeth** in him should not perish, but have everlasting life. For God sent not his Son into the world to condemn the world; but that the world through him might be saved. **He that believeth** on him is not condemned: but **he that believeth not** is condemned already, **because he hath not believed** in the name of the only begotten Son of God.*

Calvinism falsely teaches that election is unconditional, that grace is irresistible and that belief is conferred on people by force of God's sovereign will. That they are chosen to have faith thrust upon them. (Some Calvinists will say at that point, there's a choice, but generally, they reject free will).

Saved Christians understand that there is one condition for salvation, and that condition is to believe on Christ. To believe in the name of the only begotten Son. He that believes that the Father so loved the world He gave His Son, Who while we were yet sinners, died for us, and rose again that we may have eternal life in His name. 

This is Biblical repentance. **Acts 19:3-5** defines it for us. 

*And he said unto them, Unto what then were ye baptized? And they said, Unto John's baptism. Then said Paul, John verily baptized with **the baptism of repentance**, saying unto the people, **that they should believe on him which should come after him, that is, on Christ Jesus.** When they heard this, they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.*

Repentance towards the truth, the Gospel of God, is to believe on Christ Jesus. And believe means to trust. 

Ephesians 1:12-14
*That we should be to the praise of his glory, **who first trusted in Christ**. In whom **ye also trusted**, **after that ye heard the word of truth, the gospel of your salvation:** in whom also **after that ye believed, ye were sealed with that holy Spirit of promise**, Which is the earnest of our inheritance until the redemption of the purchased possession, unto the praise of his glory.*

Repent>believe>trust is all one thing, the Bible says. This is the condition by which one is saved. 

"But what if I stop believing?" What if you stopped trusting that the Gospel is true? What if you repent again to something else? How? There is no biblical mechanism given where this happens, where a saved believer stops believing.

There are examples given for those who backslide, who lose the joy of their salvation, who walk in the flesh, who are carnal Christians, who don't feed the Spirit, and become castaways to the calling of God. Chastened, prodigal, all of these things are given us as examples for what may happen in the Christian life of saved believers. 

But there is only one doctrine given for those that claimed to have believed and then repented to believe, to trust on something else. That they never fully believed. That they believed in vain. That it is impossible to renew them again unto repentance. 

Paul, upon hearing the church at Galatia had those among its members who were being beguiled into adopting the law to be saved, who had repented of the faith he taught them to believe something else - he wrote to them and harshly questioned if they actually were saved. 

**Galatians 3:1-7**
*O foolish Galatians, who hath bewitched you, **that ye should not obey the truth,** before whose eyes Jesus Christ hath been evidently set forth, crucified among you? **This only would I learn of you, Received ye the Spirit by the works of the law, or by the hearing of faith?** Are ye so foolish? having begun in the Spirit, are ye now made perfect by the flesh? Have ye suffered so many things **in vain?** if it be yet in vain. He therefore that ministereth to you the Spirit, and worketh miracles among you, doeth he it by the works of the law, or by the hearing of faith? Even as Abraham believed God, and it was accounted to him for righteousness. Know ye therefore that they which are of faith, the same are the children of Abraham.*

Note that Paul doesn't say "Well you did believe, so you're still saved," and then try and get them to change their mind again. He accuses them of not believing at all. 

**Galatians 4:4-11, 14-20**
*But when the fulness of the time was come, God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law, To redeem them that were under the law, that we might receive the adoption of sons. And because ye are sons, God hath sent forth the Spirit of his Son into your hearts, crying, Abba, Father. Wherefore thou art no more a servant, but a son; and if a son, then an heir of God through Christ. Howbeit then, when ye knew not God, ye did service unto them which by nature are no gods. But now, after that ye have known God, or rather are known of God, how turn ye again to the weak and beggarly elements, whereunto ye desire again to be in bondage? Ye observe days, and months, and times, and years. I am afraid of you, lest I have bestowed upon you labour in vain.*..*Am I therefore become your enemy, because I tell you the truth? They zealously affect you, but not well; yea, they would exclude you, that ye might affect them. But it is good to be zealously affected always in a good thing, and not only when I am present with you. My little children, of whom I travail in birth again until Christ be formed in you, I desire to be present with you now, and to change my voice; for I stand in doubt of you.
*
According to this new group of people claiming "Heresy!" Paul was a heretic to be marked and avoided. 

Also John then, according to these foolish men, would be a heretic, for teaching that if one goes out from the doctrine of the truth, it was to make manifest that they never believed.

**1 Corinthians 15:12-14**
*Now if Christ be preached that he rose from the dead, how say some among you that there is no resurrection of the dead? But if there be no resurrection of the dead, then is Christ not risen: And if Christ be not risen, then is our preaching vain, and your faith is also vain.*

Faith in vain is defined for us again here, where those that had heard the truth preached, that included the resurrection of the dead, now were saying the resurrection of Christ wasn't true. Paul says that this means their faith was in vain. Empty. Having no effect. Vanity is defined again and again in scripture to mean one thing, a belief or action that has no power towards salvation in God. Vain works, vain idols, vain beliefs. *All is vanity, sayeth the preacher*, but one truth: *Let us hear the conclusion of the whole matter: Fear God, and keep his commandments: for this is the whole duty of man*, and so we are called to *Remember now thy Creator in the days of thy youth*. To believe. To trust. To keep in remembrance. To turn away from vanity.

Finally, this strange doctrine being promoted by very foolish men says that it is not only **possible** that *those who were once enlightened, and have tasted of the heavenly gift, and were made partakers of the Holy Ghost, And have tasted the good word of God, and the powers of the world to come, If they shall fall away, to renew them again unto repentance*, but that God actually will force repentance and impose faith again upon the apostate, before they die, so that they are kept saved by God's sovereign will. 

A form of Ultra-Calvinism. 

They claim, contrary to God's word, that those that *crucify to themselves the Son of God afresh, and put him to an open shame*, those who go out from us and are manifest that they were not of us, will, by the sovereignty of God, be brought to faith, "believing again" just in time to not perish. 

Despite the fact that the Bible says this is impossible. Despite the fact that they claim to reject Calvinism. 

They so badly want to have the ability to reject God, kill the new man, break the seal of the Spirit, and still be "saved," they've invented a foolish and damnable heresy that tells people who reject the truth to not worry about it. They "believed" once, and that's good enough and if they trust in something else later, oh well. 

Paul wrote entire Epistles in the Spirit to warn against believing in vain. Telling people to keep in memory the truth of the Gospel he preached. 

Because once you believe the truth, once you repent, once you trusted on Christ Jesus alone to be saved, you have the Spirit of truth, and not the spirit of error, and cannot be deceived.

**1 John 4:2-6**
*Hereby know ye the Spirit of God: Every spirit that confesseth that Jesus Christ is come in the flesh is of God: And every spirit that confesseth not that Jesus Christ is come in the flesh is not of God: and this is that spirit of antichrist, whereof ye have heard that it should come; and even now already is it in the world. Ye are of God, little children, and have overcome them: because greater is he that is in you, than he that is in the world. They are of the world: therefore speak they of the world, and the world heareth them. We are of God: **he that knoweth God heareth us; he that is not of God heareth not us.** Hereby know we the spirit of truth, and the spirit of error.*

There is a heresy that is called "Continual Believeism" that teaches, among other damnable heresies (repent-of-your-sin, baptism for babies, etc) that "belief" is a work, an action. That "belief" isn't simply knowing something is true but requires ongoing, active faith maintained until death. A "perseverance of the saints," that makes a state of mind into a process. Just as they make repentance into a process. 

The new, foolish application of this heresy makes the same mistake those who actually endorse "Continual Believeism." They too make what is a change of mind and a knowledge that something is true into a process and a work. 

They make the same damned error. 

The ""Continual Believeism" heretics say that believers have free will and can choose to walk away from salvation by ceasing to believe or through unrepentant sin. 

The people taking that heresy and twisting it to mean that "believers have free will and can choose to walk away from salvation by ceasing to believe," but they will be forced to believe again, because they "had been saved."

It's two heads of the same damned coin and a misunderstanding of what believing is, simply repenting to the knowledge something is true, accepting something true as true, trusting on it being true. 

They turn it into an action, a work, and wrest with scripture to deal with it, rather than accepting that all those who have believed for salvation just know that what they trusted in is true, even if they doubt themselves, because it is the promise of God.

Call me Colombo, because one more thing; these fools are also applying the same logic Dispensationalists hold regarding the Jews. 

That a promise of God is a promise, and so that even though the Jews are unrepentant antichrists who rejected Jesus, they will somehow still be saved in the end because they had a covenant. That in the end, God will give them faith and they will believe, and so "all Israel shall be saved!" 

The covenant with physical Israel was conditional. They no longer have the promises because they broke the condition. They held the truth in unrighteousness, and did not wish to retain God in their knowledge. 

Salvation is conditional on belief, on knowing in our hearts that Jesus is the Christ. *If thou believest with all thine heart*...If you don't know that something is true with all your heart, you don't believe it. If you know something is true with all your heart, how could you ever reject it? 

It doesn't mean you have to continually work to believe. It doesn't mean you have to constantly remind yourself that it's true that the only way a man may be saved is by faith alone in the finished work of Christ. 

It just is.

If you come up with a doctrine that contradicts clear scripture, it falls on you to explain it and make it consistent. 

If you cannot explain Hebrews 6 and 1 John 2, to make it fit your opinion, then your opinion is wrong.

teachings.title: The laborers in the vineyard and lordship salvation
teachings.summary: Answers lordship and repent-of-your-sin teachers with Matthew 20, saying the saved are chastened by God but receive grace as the late laborers did.
teachings.text:
Lordshippers and repent-of-your-sinners are hypocritical vipers. 

They just want to judge other people. They want to rate their own righteousness by finding others who aren't living up to whatever arbitrary standards they have set.
