And it's always vague because they need to have wiggle room for their own sin. " You got to give your life to Christ!" What does that mean? Well it depends on when you ask them. 

"You have to repent of your sin and change your life!" What does that mean? Depends on when you ask them. 

It has to be vague and loaded with ambiguity and subjective judgment because they always have to have a way to justify their own sin. They always need to have someone else they can look down on. 

Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees. HYPOCRITES!

People who think this way also neglect to understand that we who are saved are chastened by God, who scourges every son he receives. 

"You can't just live however you want!" is code for "It isn't fair that you get paid a penny for showing up at the end, when I worked all day!" 

**Matthew 20:1-15**
*For the kingdom of heaven is like unto a man that is an householder, which went out early in the morning to hire labourers into his vineyard.

2 And when he had agreed with the labourers for a penny a day, he sent them into his vineyard.

3 And he went out about the third hour, and saw others standing idle in the marketplace,

4 And said unto them; Go ye also into the vineyard, and whatsoever is right I will give you. And they went their way.

5 Again he went out about the sixth and ninth hour, and did likewise.

6 And about the eleventh hour he went out, and found others standing idle, and saith unto them, Why stand ye here all the day idle?

7 They say unto him, Because no man hath hired us. He saith unto them, Go ye also into the vineyard; and whatsoever is right, that shall ye receive.

8 So when even was come, the lord of the vineyard saith unto his steward, Call the labourers, and give them their hire, beginning from the last unto the first.

9 And when they came that were hired about the eleventh hour, they received every man a penny.

10 But when the first came, they supposed that they should have received more; and they likewise received every man a penny.

11 And when they had received it, they murmured against the goodman of the house,

12 Saying, These last have wrought but one hour, and thou hast made them equal unto us, which have borne the burden and heat of the day.

13 But he answered one of them, and said, Friend, I do thee no wrong: didst not thou agree with me for a penny?

14 Take that thine is, and go thy way: I will give unto this last, even as unto thee.

15 Is it not lawful for me to do what I will with mine own? Is thine eye evil, because I am good?*

teachings.title: The election of grace
teachings.summary: Argues from Romans 11:5-6 and Galatians 3 that election is of grace, and that salvation for the Jews as Abraham's seed makes grace no more grace.
teachings.text:
Every damnable heresy in "professing Christianity" is based on rejecting the election of grace. They make grace contingent on merit, making grace no more grace. 

**Romans 11:5-6**
*Even so then at this present time also there is a remnant according to the election of grace. And if by grace, then is it no more of works: otherwise grace is no more grace. But if it be of works, then it is no more grace: otherwise work is no more work.*

Grace is the undeserved and unmerited favor of God. 

Here in Romans, Paul is writing to explain why physical Israel, Jews after the flesh, are not elect. That their blood relation to Abraham cannot save them. That it is by the election of grace man is saved. Continuing in verse 7;

*What then? Israel hath not obtained that which he seeketh for; but the election hath obtained it, and the rest were blinded.*

Which election? The election of Grace. And so, the heresy of dispensationalism fails when the scriptures are searched to see if it is so. And the damnable heresy of hyperdispensationalism is undone by the doctrine of grace. 

**Galatians 3:16**, **26-29**
*Now to Abraham and his seed were the promises made. He saith not, And to seeds, as of many; but as of one, And to thy seed, which is Christ*.

*For ye are all the children of God by faith in Christ Jesus.* *For as many of you as have been baptized into Christ have put on Christ. There is neither Jew nor Greek, there is neither bond nor free, there is neither male nor female: for ye are all one in Christ Jesus. And if ye be Christ's, then are ye Abraham's seed, and heirs according to the promise.*

The Jews being saved for being the seed of Abraham makes grace no more grace.

**Romans 9:6-8**
*Not as though the word of God hath taken none effect. For they are not all Israel, which are of Israel: Neither, because they are the seed of Abraham, are they all children: but, In Isaac shall thy seed be called. That is, They which are the children of the flesh, these are not the children of God: but the children of the promise are counted for the seed.*

teachings.title: What confidence is this wherein thou trustest
teachings.summary: The world respects ornate high places and Rome's trappings, but humble trust in the Lord in weakness is the believer's strength.
teachings.text:
Here in **Isaiah 36** we have the third telling of this historical event, where the captain of the Assyrian horde has come down through Samaria, along the Jordan, from Lachish, the city of Dan in the north, unto the plains before Jerusalem in the South.

Hezekiah is king over Judah, and while not a good king in the tradition of David, but he has trusted the Lord, preached by Isaiah, with his illness and been healed, being granted 15 years to his life by God. He had taken down altars to the false gods, in high places. And here the city is under siege.

The Assyrian Rabshakeh, speaking in Hebrew, calls out to the King's advisors on the wall, telling them of the futility of their position and asking *What confidence is this wherein thou trustest?*

What a question, and one our adversaries in the world, mockers and scoffers and those seeking us harm may ask. One our spiritual adversary, Satan, may corner us into answering.

Rabshakeh says who will you trust? Egypt, a broken reed, nothing one could put their confidence in. For us, God uses Egypt as an example of the bondage to sin and the world.

Or do you trust in the Lord? But notice it isn't the Lord God, but his natural man understanding of what God is, and what religion of the believers looks like.

*But if thou say to me, We trust in the Lord our God: is it not he, whose high places and whose altars Hezekiah hath taken away, and said to Judah and to Jerusalem, Ye shall worship before this altar?*

The false religion of worshipping God in high places and idols and altars, which the world sees vs our worship in our hearts, at the Temple of God's choosing. Hezekiah had done right, and Rabshakeh is mocking it.

The world sees the Roman Catholic Church, or any of its splinters this way, as the true religion of Christianity. If we reject those trappings, they think we weaken God, or doubt our faith.

We see this all the time, when the world makes fun of "Pastor Bob" with a strip mall church. The world respects the high places, the ornate temples made of hands. They don't fear the god of these places, but they understand it, the carnality of elegant churches, idols, altars.

To the world, trusting the Lord humbly, and in weakness is foolish. But to us, strength.

**2 Corinthians 12:8-10**
*For this thing I besought the Lord thrice, that it might depart from me. And he said unto me, My grace is sufficient for thee: for my strength is made perfect in weakness. Most gladly therefore will I rather glory in my infirmities, that the power of Christ may rest upon me. Therefore I take pleasure in infirmities, in reproaches, in necessities, in persecutions, in distresses for Christ's sake: for when I am weak, then am I strong.*

teachings.title: Woe unto you that desire the day of the Lord
teachings.summary: Performative worship and sacrifices without faith and mercy do not please God, as with Catholic and Zionist religion today, and such will face His wrath.
teachings.text:
*Woe unto you that desire the day of the Lord! to what end is it for you? the day of the Lord is darkness, and not light.*

Those unsaved masses calling for the day of the Lord to escape the judgment against them for their wickedness, God compares to a man fleeing a lion and meeting a bear, or seeking shelter in a house, only to be bitten by a snake.

So too, the fake believers in their solemn assemblies, offering sacrifices as if that's what justifies them before God, and calling upon Him to come quickly...they are the very reason God's wrath is upon them.

**Hosea 6:6**
*For I desired mercy, and not sacrifice; and the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings.*

Performative acts of worship, in Ephraim, to a golden calf worshipped in His name, do not please God. The blood of bulls and goats never washed away their sin. He took no pleasure in their songs and burnt offerings while they lived without faith, mercy and right judgement. Disobedient to the commandments that God gave them that it be well with them, and they should live long in the land.

God reminds us that the children of Israel in the wilderness offered sacrifices at the Tabernacle for 40 years, and yet they did not enter the promised land.

How much worse these who have borne the tabernacle of Moloch and Chiun, false and foreign gods, and the images thereof, including the star of their false God, which they invented themselves. Today they call it the star of David.

This message is obviously very relevant. Today we have Catholic-made churches claiming to worship the true Lord, with idols and sacrifices of bread and wine made to them. We have evangelicals yoked to unbelieving Jews, trying to hasten the day of the Lord, and carrying the star of their god.

And God of hosts, the Lord, Christ Jesus, will destroy them and carry them into captivity when that great and wonderful day comes. And there will be darkness and lamentation, wailing and gnashing of teeth.

teachings.title: Same gospel for Jews and Gentiles, and idols
teachings.summary: Shows from Acts 15:11 that the apostles believed they were saved by the same grace as the Gentiles, and from Acts 19 that early Christians opposed idols in worship.
teachings.text:
*Peter rose up, and said unto them, Men and brethren, ye know how that a good while ago God made choice among us, that the Gentiles by my mouth should hear the word of the gospel, and believe. And God, which knoweth the hearts, bare them witness, giving them the Holy Ghost, even as he did unto us; And put no difference between us and them, purifying their hearts by faith. Now therefore why tempt ye God, to put a yoke upon the neck of the disciples, which neither our fathers nor we were able to bear?

**But we believe that through the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ we shall be saved, even as they.***

The heresy that Paul taught a different gospel to Gentiles than the Apostles taught the Jews relies on a false interpretation of **Acts 15**. But it is made clear here in **Acts 15:11** that the Apostles in Jerusalem believed they were saved by the same grace as the Gentiles. By the Lord Jesus Christ.

**Acts 19:24-28** 
*For a certain man named Demetrius, a silversmith, which made silver shrines for Diana, brought no small gain unto the craftsmen; Whom he called together with the workmen of like occupation, and said, Sirs, ye know that by this craft we have our wealth. Moreover ye see and hear, that not alone at Ephesus, but almost throughout all Asia, this Paul hath persuaded and turned away much people, saying that they be no gods, which are made with hands: So that not only this our craft is in danger to be set at nought; but also that the temple of the great goddess Diana should be despised, and her magnificence should be destroyed, whom all Asia and the world worshippeth. And when they heard these sayings, they were full of wrath, and cried out, saying, Great is Diana of the Ephesians.*

Catholics, particularly Orthodox, all insist that graven images and "icons" were always part of worship for Christians, from the days of the Apostles. Obviously false, as Idolatry was consistently prohibited by God's commandments, and by the Apostles and Epistles, saying to flee idols and not to eat meats offered to them. 

But to really reinforce this idea, we have the story in **Acts 19** of the silversmith, Demetrius and the cause he's tired up against the disciples of Christ in Ephesus. Because the Christian teaching was against images in worship, Demetrius was able to argue their craft was in jeopardy. That they'd go bankrupt if people no longer required idols made of hands. 

If early Christianity only taught against images of false gods, and not the entire practice itself, their trade would not be unprofitable. Instead of Diana they could make a living with crucifixes and statues of the passed saints. 

It's just another example of how foolish these appeals to vain tradition are in light of the Bible.

teachings.title: The Olivet Discourse was spoken to believers
teachings.summary: Shows from the use of ye and they that Jesus spoke the Olivet Discourse to His disciples, with redemption drawing nigh for them.
teachings.text:
**Isaiah 7:14 **
*Therefore the Lord himself shall give you a sign; Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel.*

**Isaiah 9:6 **
*For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given: and the government shall be upon his shoulder: and his name shall be called Wonderful, Counsellor, The mighty God, The everlasting Father, The Prince of Peace*.

**Micah 5:2 **
*But thou, Bethlehem Ephratah, though thou be little among the thousands of Judah, yet out of thee shall he come forth unto me that is to be ruler in Israel; whose goings forth have been from of old, from everlasting.*

To Him gave all the prophets witness.
Amen

Dispensationalists falsely claim that the Olivet Discourse found in **Matthew 24, Luke 21** and **Mark 13** are "written to the Jews, not believers. There is no evidence of this, but there is clear evidence that Jesus was speaking to His disciples, believers, and made a clear distinction between "ye" and "they."

**Luke 21:7-28** 
*And they asked him, saying, Master, but when shall these things be? and what sign will there be when these things shall come to pass? And he said, Take heed that **ye** be not deceived: for many shall come in my name, saying, I am Christ; and the time draweth near: go **ye** not therefore after them. But when **ye** shall hear of wars and commotions, be not terrified: for these things must first come to pass; but the end is not by and by. Then said he unto them, Nation shall rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom: And great earthquakes shall be in divers places, and famines, and pestilences; and fearful sights and great signs shall there be from heaven. But before all these, they shall lay their hands on **you**, and persecute **you**, delivering you up to the synagogues, and into prisons, being brought before kings and rulers for my name's sake. And it shall turn to **you** for a testimony. Settle it therefore in your hearts, not to meditate before what **ye** shall answer: For I will give you a mouth and wisdom, which all **your** adversaries shall not be able to gainsay nor resist. And **ye** shall be betrayed both by parents, and brethren, and kinsfolks, and friends; and some of **you** shall they cause to be put to death. And **ye** shall be hated of all men for my name's sake. But there shall not an hair of **your** head perish. In your patience *possess ye your* souls. And when **ye** shall see Jerusalem compassed with armies, then know that the desolation thereof is nigh.

Then let **them** which are in Judaea flee to the mountains; and let **them** which are in the midst of it depart out; and let not **them** that are in the countries enter thereinto. **For these be the days of vengeance**, that all things which are written may be fulfilled. But woe unto **them** that are with child, and to **them** that give suck, in those days! for there shall be great distress in the land, and wrath upon **this people**. And **they** shall fall by the edge of the sword, and shall be led away captive into all nations: and Jerusalem shall be trodden down of the Gentiles, until the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled. 

And there shall be signs in the sun, and in the moon, and in the stars; and upon the earth distress of nations, with perplexity; the sea and the waves roaring; Men's hearts failing **them** for fear, and for looking after those things which are coming on the earth: for the powers of heaven shall be shaken. And then shall **they** see the Son of man coming in a cloud with power and great glory. And when these things begin to come to pass, then look up, and **lift up your heads; for your redemption draweth nigh.***

Jesus speaking to saved Christians, His disciples, uses "ye" and "you," but talking about the unbelieving Jews, uses "they" and "this people." 

"They" get the days of vengeance. "Ye" get "your redemption." It's a clear distinction. It is not "written to the Jews," but to believers.

teachings.title: Mount Moriah, where God provided a sacrifice
teachings.summary: The temple was built on Moriah where Abraham offered Isaac, a picture of Christ, and its cherubim were never bowed to, refuting idolaters who cite them.
teachings.text:
The construction begins, noting specific measurements and qualities of the decorative features and layout.

Some idolaters justify their bowing and serving images of men by pointing to the decorative and illustrative placement of Cherubim and pomegranates in the Temple design. No Israelites bowed to these things, representative of the pattern in Heaven. They didn't offer prayers or sacrifice to them. They served no purpose other than to make the house of the Lord reflect His temple in Heaven.

The location of the Temple mount, Moriah, where the Lord appeared to David, and where the sacrifices to the Lord took place by the threshing floor of Ornan, was also where Abraham brought Isaac to be sacrificed; **Genesis 22:1-2**

*And it came to pass after these things, that God did tempt Abraham, and said unto him, Abraham: and he said, Behold, here I am. And he said, Take now thy son, thine only son Isaac, whom thou lovest, and get thee into the land of Moriah; and offer him there for a burnt offering upon one of the mountains which I will tell thee of.*

There, in a picture of Christ, where Issac, Abraham's only begotten son, carried the wood up the mountain to be offered, with hyssop and crimson. And God the Father provided a substitutionary offering, a ram in a thicket of thorns.

The same Jerusalem where Jesus was brought before the high priest, near Golgotha where He gave His life.

Likely the same place Melchizedek the King of Salem offered Abraham's sacrifice. Where Christ will return to rule and reign. The place God chose to place His holy name.

teachings.title: Bonosus and the perpetual virginity of Mary
teachings.summary: Records the fourth century bishop Bonosus who taught against the perpetual virginity of Mary and was condemned by Rome.
teachings.text:
Bonosus was a Bishop of Sardica in the latter part of the fourth century, who taught against the doctrine of the perpetual virginity of Mary. His followers were later labelled "Bonosians" and considered heretical by Roman apostates.

The council of Capua (391) condemned Bonosus and tried to excommunicate him, but Bonosus did not stop using his episcopal functions.

The Bonosians rebaptized converts from Roman Catholicism.

teachings.title: Repent-of-your-sins is a false gospel
teachings.summary: Notes the inconsistency of KJV-only believers who claim grace alone through faith alone yet teach repent-of-your-sins and Lordship salvation.
teachings.text:
It is amazing to me that there are supposed KJVOists, who claim salvation is by grace alone through faith alone, and yet teach the false gospel of "repent-of-your-sins" which comes from satanic perversions.

Of course these same vipers will simultaneously denounce John MacArthur for Calvinism, while embracing his false "Lordship salvation" gospel.

teachings.title: Baptism does not save in 1 Peter 3
teachings.summary: Shows the order of operations in 1 Peter 3 and says those who see baptism as a means of grace are spiritually blinded to it.
teachings.text:
It always amazes me when a Protestant tries to use this passage to justify baptizing babies, or to say that it is a "means of Grace," That somehow the water water creates the ability for someone to believe. 

And when you show them this order of operations and break it down for them, they simply cannot understand it. They see baptism saves and call it a day. 

The only thing that can explain their inability to simply read the passage and follow along the order of operations is that they are spiritually blinded. They have a supernatural blindness to the truth

teachings.title: One mediator and boldness before the Father
teachings.summary: Contrasts the believer's access to the Father through the one mediator Christ Jesus with Catholic reliance on Mary, saints and priests.
teachings.text:
God tells us, who are saved, who have the Spirit of adoption, that we have one mediator with the Father, Christ Jesus, and one intercessor for prayer, the holy Spirit. We go boldly before the Father with confidence as sons.

But Catholics don't. They use idols and "Mary," and "saints" and priests as intermediaries. Because they know in their hearts they cannot go to the Father as sons. 

Most Catholics are just misled. Not full blown apostate reprobates. And they know in their hearts they cannot enter boldly before the throne. 

So the Catholic church tells them to go through stone and wood and to human intercessors, for their conscience's sake.  Very sad.

teachings.title: Repent is not penance
teachings.summary: Says false teachers have turned repent into Catholic penance and that its historical meaning is a change of mind.
teachings.text:
False teachers have perverted "repent" into penance, promoting the Catholic heresy, sneaking it into Baptist circles. They should be shut up by scripture, which shows these vipers teaching works salvation by a "repent-of-your-sins" false gospel. 

But barring that, the historical understanding and application of "repent," as a change of mind, especially upon reflection or new understanding, should also serve to shut them up. 

They don't hear God's voice, perhaps they'll listen to man's.

teachings.title: The Lord's Supper and the word Eucharist
teachings.summary: Distinguishes the Lord's Supper as a symbolic act of remembrance from the Catholic Eucharist as a ritual bestowing salvation.
teachings.text:
No offense intended to you or any saved believer who understands that the Lord's Supper is a symbolic act done with genuine thanks and awed remembrance of Christ's sacrifice when you break bread with fellow believers.

Generally those that use the term "Eucharist" mean an act that bestows some measure of salvation and done as a ritual or rite with meat and drink sacrifices to an idol as part of a perverse and blasphemous false gospel. 

If you happen to use the word in the sense of giving thanks and having remembrance of Jesus for what He did, this wasn't directed at you.

teachings.title: Woe to him that giveth his neighbour drink
teachings.summary: Habakkuk's woe pictures Babylon making nations drunk with abominations like Mystery Babylon, and is sound doctrine against drunkenness and the shameful things it brings.
teachings.text:
*Woe unto him that giveth his neighbour drink, that puttest thy bottle to him, and makest him drunken also, that thou mayest look on their nakedness! Thou art filled with shame for glory: drink thou also, and let thy foreskin be uncovered: the cup of the Lord's right hand shall be turned unto thee, and shameful spewing shall be on thy glory*

This is an allegory for the sins of Babylon, and sound doctrine on drunkenness and the warped and perverse results of it.

Its neighbors, the nations it takes over and the abominations of false gods they introduce to the captives are compared to alcohol being given to take advantage of another.

Similar to the Great Whore, Mystery Babylon;

*And the woman was arrayed in purple and scarlet colour, and decked with gold and precious stones and pearls, having a golden cup in her hand full of abominations and filthiness of her fornication...with whom the kings of the earth have committed fornication, and the inhabitants of the earth have been made drunk with the wine of her fornication.*

But, it also is a stark reminder of what alcohol does to people, and the disgusting things that come about from it.

God promises that for this sin, or leading others to drunkenness that they may be taken advantage of, Nebuchadnezzar's own nakedness will be revealed instead. His own shame and humiliation will be exposed.

When we read **Daniel 4**, we will see this.

teachings.title: The God of the Old Testament is the God of the New
teachings.summary: Calls the idea that the Old Testament God is a different or evil God a damnable heresy, and cites Hebrews 11:6.
teachings.text:
Here's a heresy that I have not encountered before. Possibly the dumbest one of all. People professing to be Christian who think that the Old Testament has nothing to do with Jesus. That the God of the Old Testament is a demon.

If you don't know that the God of the Old Testament is the same God as the New, you don't know God. This isn't up for debate. It is damnable heresy and you're perishing. Repent.

**Hebrews 11:6**
*But without faith it is impossible to please him: for he that cometh to God must believe that he is, and that he is a rewarder of them that diligently seek him.*

teachings.title: The Septuagint is a forgery
teachings.summary: Says there was never a pre-Christian Greek translation of the Hebrew Old Testament and that Jesus and the apostles did not quote from the LXX.
teachings.text:
Reminder that the forgery called the Septuagint, or LXX, is gnostic heresy and a perversion of God's word, invented by Alexandrian heretics after Christ's resurrection, full of Jewish fables of the so-called Apocrypha, and riddled with errors and contradictions. Embraced by the whore and her harlot daughters.

It is of the same provenance as the "modern versions" issued from "critical text" readings today. And like all modern versions, is designed to further the satanic "Ye, hath God said?" sowing of doubtful disputations. 

There was never a BC translation of the Hebrew into Greek, other than some verses from the pentateuch. There was no letter, no 72 Israelite scholars. And Jesus and the Apostles did not "quote" from it. It was a Jewish lie from the beginning, adopted by the apostate church of Rome.

**Luke 24:44-45**
*And he said unto them, These are the words which I spake unto you, while I was yet with you, that all things must be fulfilled, which were written in **the law of Moses, and in the prophets, and in the psalms**, concerning me. Then opened he their understanding, that they might understand the scriptures*

Jesus, opening the disciples understanding of the scriptures, lays out precisely the format of the Old Testament, and excludes all other works that some claim to be scripture. 

There is the Law of Moses, the Pentateuch - the first five books of the Bible, credited to Moses. The Prophets, the series of books telling the history of Israel through the prophets of God. And Psalms, the songs and Proverbs inspired by God. These are the oracles of God, the scripture that taught of Christ. 

There was no mention of apocryphal books or texts, because they did not write of Him.

teachings.title: The Septuagint myth
teachings.summary: Argues that the story of 72 scholars translating the Septuagint in 250 BC has no evidence behind it, and that the LXX people cite today is Origen's own work.
teachings.text:
It is harder to take seriously people who think the "Septuagint" (or the "LXX" as it's called) was really compiled and translated by "72 Israelite scholars" 6 each from the "12 tribes," in 250BC than it is to take seriously those who accept the "Dead Sea Scrolls" as authoritative.

It was a creation of the apostate Origen, in the second century AD, filled with errors, contains later apocryphal works, and was used to justify heresies of gnostics in the early Roman Catholic cult. 

Jesus cited the OT scripture, compiled in Hebrew by scribes of Levites, that He Himself had inspired. With jots and tittles. 

The "Letter of Aristeas" that supposedly commissioned this work, appears to have been a forgery written by the Alexandrian apostate Jew, Philo, in the first century AD, to justify his heresies. The "12 tribes" did not exist in 250BC, and there were no scribes in among the long scattered and destroyed 10 tribes of the Northern Kingdom. There is no evidence of the existence of a Greek translation, other than a copy of Deuteronomy 23-28, with zero indication that it was from a larger work, and dated to 150BC, a century later than the supposed Septuagint.

When people today talk about the LXX they are not referring to a translation from 250BC, but are entirely talking about the second column of Origen's Hexapla, where his own translation was recorded.

teachings.title: Salvation is by Christ's righteousness
teachings.summary: Warns against teaching that salvation depends on our own righteousness and reminds that all fall short of the glory of God.
teachings.text:
Too many false teachers are in the world teaching that our salvation is contingent on our ability to be righteous rather than by Christ's righteousness. Denying eternal life. Teaching salvation can be lost if we aren't "good enough." 

News flash, you aren't good enough. No one is. We all fall short of the glory of God.

teachings.title: Assurance is not presumption
teachings.summary: Answers the Catholic claim that faith in the gospel is a sin of presumption, pointing to the sealing of the Spirit and the knowledge of eternal life.
teachings.text:
One of the most pernicious and wicked damnable heresies of the Catholic church is to make faith in the Gospel into a "sin of presumption." 

They take the knowledge of salvation, whereby we know we have eternal life, sealed by the Holy Spirit unto redemption, the earnest of our inheritance, and blasphemously claim that the Spirit of God does no such thing. 

But we who are saved know that we have the Holy Spirit testifying within us that we are the sons of God. 

And we are called to share the glory of God found in his Mercy extended towards us with everyone. Having a ready answer for the hope that lies within us.

Needless to say, this person claiming that having faith in God's promise is "blaspheming the Holy Spirit" Is actually in danger of the very thing he's falsely accusing others of

teachings.title: James 2:17 used against the gospel
teachings.summary: Observes that those who use James 2:17 against the gospel hold to a self-righteous zeal not according to knowledge and are very hard to reach.
teachings.text:
When someone pulls out **James 2:17** as a Uno reverse card against the Gospel, they have admitted they aren't saved, and it is nearly impossible to get them to budge from their self-righteous position.

*For I bear them record that they have a zeal of God, but not according to knowledge. For they being ignorant of God’s righteousness, and going about to establish their own righteousness, have not submitted themselves unto the righteousness of God.*

They seek to establish their own righteousness, and so they oppose themselves. There are none righteous. Our only righteousness is imputed of Christ. 

*Knowing that a man is not justified by the works of the law, but by the faith of Jesus Christ, even we have believed in Jesus Christ, that we might be justified by the faith of Christ, and not by the works of the law: for by the works of the law shall no flesh be justified.*

I have never managed to free a person who has stumbled and been snared by **James 2:17**. All the scripture in the world, and they cannot see.

teachings.title: Christ left us His word, not a church
teachings.summary: Argues that the rock in Matthew 16 is the gospel Peter confessed and not Peter himself, and that Jesus left His word as a sword rather than a church institution.
teachings.text:
Who should we place our trust in? A church? A denomination, made of men? 

Or Christ Jesus. The rock of our salvation?

The difference between saved, born again Christians and those that believe "God left us a church, not a Bible!" comes down to their saying that the "rock" in Matthew 16 is a man, Peter, rather than the truth of the Gospel that Peter had just proclaimed, that Jesus is the Christ.

It is the good news, the Gospel, which is the key to Hell and death. The power to bind a soul to Heaven, or condemn it to Hell. The power to forgive a brother, bring Him to Christ and by doing so, Jesus builds His church.

"But Jesus only gave the power to Peter!!!" 

Two chapters later, while teaching all the disciples, Jesus said they all had this power. 

Jesus left us the Gospel. God's word. 

Not a church. 

God left us a sword.

Jesus left us His word, not a church. He left us a sword. 

He builds His church from the pillars that are saved believers. Adopted sons of God. And our fruit are those souls won to Christ, who trust in Him alone. 

Not "So long as I..." 
But "Because He said."

teachings.title: Denying the reprobate doctrine endangers the flock
teachings.summary: From Judges 19 he warns that churches that deny the reprobate doctrine and teach it is never too late let sodomites and predators in among the flock, then cover it up out of pride.
teachings.text:
It is worth pointing out that the Levite and his party were closer to a city of the Jebusites, but not wishing to lodge for the night in the city of a stranger, he sought the city of Gibeah, thinking they would be safer among Israelites, to be among Benjamin.

Very often Christians will be disarmed in their judgment by blindly trusting people at church. People professing to be fellow Christians. People who claim to have repented of their evil ways, who have a good story for a testimony, about turning from the most wicked sins to be saved.

Christians may even turn from dealing with an unsaved neighbor, to seek out the services of a "brother."

But God has given us fair warning. Their very countenance gives them away. Churches that harbor sodomites are like Benjamin did, allowing the wicked to creep in unawares, are endangering their flock.

It starts with denying the Reprobate Doctrine. Teaching that all men are able to be saved at any time, that it's never too late to repent.

But the idea that hearts are hardened, ears made dull, eyes blinded to the truth, that some are past the point of feeling, conscience seared as with a hot iron, given up and given over to a reprobate mind, that is, rejected of God, is taught throughout scripture.

In the NT, Paul, Peter and Jude write extensively on the subject. The preaching of Christ in the Gospels affirms it.

And after denying reprobation as real, congregations will begin to drift towards "repent of your sins" heresy. They may give lip service to "grace alone, faith alone," but they will sow the seeds for a works-based false gospel in the minds of the people. This leads to a certain prideful view, where the worse the sinner who "repents," the more powerful the testimony seems in their eyes. "Look who we helped turn around to Christ. Aren't we good?"

And so you have youth pastors and music directors who molest children or rape teen girls. Men who should have taken Christ's advice and drowned themselves in the sea, rather than offend little ones.

And the pastors and deacons who allowed these monsters in will do whatever they can to cover it up. In their pride, like the men of Benjamin, they would rather go down fighting to defend their poor judgement than do what's right, and admit they were wrong.

They will lie and claim it is to keep the testimony of Jesus Christ from being slandered, to defend the gospel from scoffers, but it is selfish and wicked.

And even good pastors, godly men who are saved by the right gospel, who have won hundreds to the Lord, can fall prey to their own pride and embarrassment at their lapse of judgement. And when it comes out, the damage done is far worse than had they done the right thing.

*For nothing is secret, that shall not be made manifest; neither any thing hid, that shall not be known and come abroad.*

teachings.title: The kingdom of heaven and the kingdom of God
teachings.summary: Sets Daniel 2:44, Matthew 4, Mark 1 and Luke 17 side by side to show the kingdom of heaven and the kingdom of God are one and the same.
teachings.text:
**Daniel 2:44**
*And in the days of these kings shall **the God of heaven set up a kingdom**, which shall never be destroyed: and the kingdom shall not be left to other people, but it shall break in pieces and consume all these kingdoms, and it shall stand for ever.*

**Matthew 4:17 **
*From that time Jesus began to preach, and to say, Repent: for **the kingdom of heaven** is at hand.*

**Mark 1:15 **
*And saying, The time is fulfilled, and the kingdom of God is at hand: repent ye, and believe the gospel.*

**Luke 17:20-21**
*And when he was demanded of the Pharisees, when **the kingdom of God** should come, he answered them and said, The kingdom of God cometh not with observation: Neither shall they say, Lo here! or, lo there! for, behold, **the kingdom of God** is within you.*

**Luke 13:28-29**
*There shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth, when ye shall see Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, and all the prophets, **in the kingdom of God**, and you yourselves thrust out. And they shall come from the east, and from the west, and from the north, and from the south, and shall sit down in **the kingdom of God.***

**Matthew 8:11-12**
*And I say unto you, That many shall come from the east and west, and shall sit down with Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, **in the kingdom of heaven**. But the children of the kingdom shall be cast out into outer darkness: there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth.*

There's no way a saved Christian can read these verses and come to the conclusion that they are two separate things. 

The only way they can come to that conclusion is if some false prophet told them so.

teachings.title: Christ our Passover, not a wafer
teachings.summary: At Easter he teaches Christ, the Passover lamb, is the bread of life by one finished sacrifice, not a wafer or cup of wine.
teachings.text:
And so we enter into *Pascha*, Easter, the Passover feast in which Christians remember Christ's triumphant entrance to Jerusalem, His final meal with the Apostles, His promise of a new covenant, the cup and the bread offered in remembrance of the sacrifice He would make, His betrayal by Judas, made with a kiss, His being presented before the high priests, a lamb without blemish, offered up as the Passover lamb, slain before the foundation of the world for the remission of sins for all men, especially them that believe. His 3 days and 3 nights in Hell, a burnt offering. His glorious resurrection on the first day of the week, with the keys to Hell and Death. The hope of eternal life given us in Jesus by the grace of God. We should remember that the bread of life is Christ.

Not a cracker. Not a wafer. Not some baked cube of wheat and water. The blood of Christ was shed on that hill in Jerusalem, it isn't in a cup of juice or wine. But we remember His covenant made by his literal blood and body. His blood was sprinkled on the Mercy Seat in Heaven, one time. One sacrifice.

We who eat of this bread, come down from Heaven, and drink of the living waters that flow from Christ, shall never hunger nor thirst again. We are redeemed by that promise. The Word of God made flesh.

Not by the drinking of blood and pollution of idols. Not by meat and drink offerings sacrificed to idols continually, never satisfying, never taking away sin. But by the finished work of Christ Jesus, given by the grace and love of God the Father. Amen

teachings.title: A healthy church keeps its shibboleths
teachings.summary: He welcomes the charge that fundamentalists keep shibboleths like separation and the KJB, the main one being the gospel of grace by which false teachers are known.
teachings.text:
After Jephthah's tragic victory in **Judges 11**, he finds himself in a similar situation as Gideon had a century earlier, back in **Judges 8**;

*And the men of Ephraim said unto him, Why hast thou served us thus, that thou calledst us not, when thou wentest to fight with the Midianites? And they did chide with him sharply.*

Here in **Judges 12**, rather than deescalate the conflict with the men of Ephraim with kind words as Gideon had, Jephthah chooses conflict and he and his men smite the men of Ephraim, driving them back across the Jordan.

It is here we get the term 'Shibboleth,' a word that the Ephraimites struggled to pronounce as the Gileadites did. By asking the fleeing men to say it, knowing it would betray them as of Ephraim, Gilead put them to the sword.

This shows that even just a few hundred years since Moses and the settling of the land by Israel, that distinct dialects and regional accents had occurred. The tribes of Israel were themselves nations. And subgroups like Gilead, which was the name of part of the land settled by Gad, on the east bank of the Jordan, had grown to be its own thing. God sets boundaries and habitations, dividing nations by blood and language, shifting over time as He judges them.

We often see the term 'Shibboleth' used today as a derogatory way of describing a longstanding belief that a group of people may share that separates them from others. A way of gatekeeping looked down upon by those with modernist views, seeking to infiltrate and influence the older group.

There have been those who have accused fundamentalists of maintaining Shibboleths, from matters of separation to the sole use of the KJB, and even to the nature of the gospel...All have been attacked as 'archaic' means of resisting change in the modern era, and to that we should say "Amen!"

Scripture tells us repeatedly of how we can recognize false teachers and warns of those creeping in privily, unawares, to spy out our liberty and to lead believers astray. The main shibboleth being the gospel of grace and reconciliation through faith in Christ. If someone brings a false gospel, we know they are not of God but accursed.

**Galatians 1:8-9**
*But though we, or an angel from heaven, preach any other gospel unto you than that which we have preached unto you, let him be accursed. As we said before, so say I now again, If any man preach any other gospel unto you than that ye have received, let him be accursed.*

A healthy church maintains the landmark shibboleths of the faith.

teachings.title: Inquire meekly, then rebuke false ways
teachings.summary: Believers should hate every false way but meekly ask professing Christians what they mean, testing them by the gospel before rebuking or accepting them.
teachings.text:
Now, the other application is that we should hate every false way, and there is no harm in asking someone professing to be Christian to explain their apparent behavior or statements that seem contrary to the Gospel.

As we see online especially, there are many who hold damnable heresies and doctrines of devils, claiming to be of Christ. There is no profit in blind ecumenicalism, and accepting everyone calling themselves Christian regardless of their beliefs. But we should trust someone who claims to be a believer, giving them the benefit of the doubt unless there is a sign that concerns us. And then, remembering Phinehas, inquire what they meant, meekly and with care. It could simply be a misunderstanding or a different way of phrasing something, perfectly innocent.

Yes, if they announce their beliefs in a false gospel or a different god, or some vain traditions and dead works, we should confront them with scripture and rebuke them. But there are times brothers as set at variance, when the truth is there are only surface differences caused by distance and absence of fellowship.

Thankfully, God's word has a shortcut to finding out if we share a common foundation; asking "What must one do to be saved?" Paul repeatedly uses the gospel as a way of assurance of common mindedness with the churches he writes to. That we all share the same foundational belief. As Jesus says of testing the spirit of a teacher, we shall know them by their fruits, by the beliefs of their followers. If they are saved by the gospel or if they believe some false way.

We need to meekly and humbly seek to know, before either grabbing a javelin or declaring peace, and always ready to provide a way out should they prove to be going the way of Balaam, and heading to the destruction of Baal-Peor. By giving them the true gospel in love. Amen

teachings.title: Preterism, amillennialism and contending for the faith
teachings.summary: Says preterism and amillennialism are signs of a wrong gospel or of a babe in Christ carried about by every wind of doctrine, and cites Jude on contending for the faith.
teachings.text:
Preterism and amillennialism are signs of either believing in vain with the wrong gospel, or in some circumstances, being a babe in Christ *tossed to and fro, and carried about with every wind of doctrine, by the sleight of men, and cunning craftiness, whereby they lie in wait to deceive*. Taken away by confident sounding men, rather than Biblical teachings.

*Beloved, when I gave all diligence to write unto you of the common salvation, it was needful for me to write unto you, and exhort you that ye should earnestly contend for the faith which was once delivered unto the saints. For there are certain men crept in unawares, who were before of old ordained to this condemnation, ungodly men, turning the grace of our God into lasciviousness, and denying the only Lord God, and our Lord Jesus Christ. **I will therefore put you in remembrance, though ye once knew this, how that the Lord, having saved the people out of the land of Egypt, afterward destroyed them that believed not..**..But these speak evil of those things which they know not: but what they know naturally, as brute beasts, in those things they corrupt themselves. Woe unto them! for they have gone in the way of Cain, and ran greedily after the error of Balaam for reward, and perished in the gainsaying of Core. These are spots in your feasts of charity, when they feast with you, feeding themselves without fear: clouds they are without water, carried about of winds; trees whose fruit withereth, without fruit, twice dead, plucked up by the roots; Raging waves of the sea, foaming out their own shame; wandering stars, to whom is reserved the blackness of darkness for ever. And Enoch also, the seventh from Adam, prophesied of these, saying, Behold, the Lord cometh with ten thousands of his saints, To execute judgment upon all, and to convince all that are ungodly among them of all their ungodly deeds which they have ungodly committed, and of all their hard speeches which ungodly sinners have spoken against him.  

These are murmurers, complainers, walking after their own lusts; and their mouth speaketh great swelling words, having men's persons in admiration because of advantage. But, beloved, remember ye the words which were spoken before of the apostles of our Lord Jesus Christ; How that they told you there should be mockers in the last time, who should walk after their own ungodly lusts. These be they who separate themselves, sensual, having not the Spirit. But ye, beloved, building up yourselves on your most holy faith, praying in the Holy Ghost, Keep yourselves in the love of God, looking for the mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ **unto eternal life**.*

teachings.title: John 3:16 is the whole gospel
teachings.summary: Walks through Jesus teaching Nicodemus and urges testing any doctrine against John 3:16, since anything that violates it is a false gospel.
teachings.text:
**John 3:14-18**
*And as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, even so must the Son of man be lifted up: that **whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have eternal life**. For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that **whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life**. For God sent not his Son into the world to condemn the world; but that the world through him might be saved. **He that believeth on him is not condemned**: **but** **he that believeth not is condemned already, because he hath not believed in the name of the only begotten Son of God.***

This set of verses contain everything anyone needs to know regarding salvation, Biblical repentance in the context of salvation. The clearest explanation of the gospel found in scripture. 

He that believes *not* is condemned. 

He that believes is not condemned.

Repent and believe; Turn from non-believer to believer. That is the Gospel.

*Sirs, what must I do to be saved? ... And they said, Believe on the Lord Jesus Christ, and thou shalt be saved*.

The same Gospel Jesus preached is given by Paul. 

Not believing that God so loved the world that He gave His only begotten Son is what makes a man perish. Believing that He did, and that His Son is Christ Jesus, gives a man eternal life. 

This is the choice. This is the repentance. This is the good news. That is the God, that is His Son. The gift is eternal. Everlasting.

It's an amazing thing, in **John 3** You have one of the head religious leaders of the Jews, Nicodemus, sitting down with the Son of God, and Jesus teaches him the Gospel. We are allowed to witness this. Think about it. Think about how amazing that is. What a blessing it is.

Nicodemus who is a teacher of the people, well versed in the law, one of the highest ranking Pharisees, rich, powerful, sitting down being instructed by the Lord. And missing it.

*If I have told you earthly things, and ye believe not, how shall ye believe, if I tell you of heavenly things?
*
We have the preserved word of God, spoken to man, and he received it not. 

And how many people today are like Nicodemus? And cannot read this in all and wonder and take it as God's word that this is how you are saved. That there's nothing more to it than this simple truth.

If someone cannot agree that the plain reading of **John 3:16** is the entire Gospel, they aren't saved. 

*For **God** so **loved** **the world**, that **he** gave **his only begotten Son**, that **whosoever** **believeth in him** should **not** perish, **but have** ***everlasting* life.***

That's it. That's the entire good news of the living God by His grace, His **love** for the entire world, not some. Not few. And for that love, The Father gave His Son as a gift. Not to some. But to  **whosoever**, without caveat or conditions except one, **that believes**. Believe means trust to be true. To have faith in. A secure knowledge. A lively hope. It doesn't mean anything more than that. He gave a gift of His Son to the whole world that if they believe in Him, they won't perish. They will never die. They **have** everlasting life. That means eternal. Never ending. 

This is not some esoteric rendition where the "God" means a mode of Jesus, not a Father sacrificing His son. Or of a Jesus that is not divine. Not where "the world" and "whosoever" don't mean "the world" and "whosoever." Where "believe in Him" actually means doing works and trusting in yourself, or a denomination, or rituals and sacraments. Where "perish" isn't wrath and Hell. Where "have" means "will have" or "used to have" "or could get" or "could lose." Where "eternal" doesn't mean eternal.

All of those things, as well as the addition of things and concepts not present in this or the verses that immediately follow them, culminating 20 verses later, God summarizing it once again in **John 3:36**;

*He that believeth on the Son hath everlasting life: and he that believeth not the Son shall not see life; but the wrath of God abideth on him.*

That's it. If you don't believe this is the sum total of the Gospel, the theology of salvation, you need to repent, and believe. Or the wrath of God abides on you.

Pro tip: When someone is bringing doctrine to you that sounds ok or a little sus, and you're just not sure if it's right or not, compare it to **John 3:16**. 

If it violates any of it, you know immediately it's a false gospel. 

There are some doctrines you have to get elsewhere, most actually. But salvation, the most important one, can be taught straight from **John 3:15-18** and **3:36**.

(Go ahead and try it in the comments. Think of a damnable heresy you've heard and see where it violates **John 3:16)**

teachings.title: Rapture anxiety and the pre-trib leaven
teachings.summary: Argues that the pre-tribulation rapture teaching feeds a weekly fear in children and congregants, while the biblical order of end times and secure salvation brings peace.
teachings.text:
There is an apostasy movement happening in evangelical circles that primarily focuses on normalizing sodomites and promoting feminism as a reaction to "religious trauma." It teaches a false and warped view of the gospel, that "Jesus is love," and so whatever you do that makes you "happy" is good. These "nu-Evangelicals" hold the Bible to be imperfect, that much of its teachings no longer apply, or were the opinions of "misogynists" and "homophobes" like Paul. 

They use a mix of genuine failure in their churches, and their own inventions of evil to rationalize their falling away. One of their primary excuses is something called "Rapture Anxiety," and the cause, they say, is the teaching of the heretical doctrine of the Pre-tribulation Rapture. The imminent return of Christ taught by most mainline evangelicals in America today. The primary doctrine of dispensationalism.

While we should note it is their own wicked hearts that has led them to this error, and the itching ears yearning for feel good doctrines from reprobates who have crept in unawares, turning aside to vain jangling, there is a basis of truth to the complaint. 

When a church goes all in on a false doctrine, that cannot be justified by scripture, but only through what amounts to gaslighting, it has an effect. When the doctrine teaches different gospels, different "dispensations," and that the church itself is a failure, due to be replaced by the Jews at any moment, it has an effect. Especially among children raised in it. Add to that the rise of "Lordship salvation," "Repent-of-your-sins" heresy and the holier than thou attitudes these bring, and it is no wonder that many fall for this satanic movement. The church having had a bad report. Lying and dissembling about scripture, and, because they teach a "fruit inspector" mentality, they inevitably fall into cover-ups and hypocrisy. They become respecters of persons, and make excuses for those that are elders, tithe more, volunteer more, etc, while condemning those who they judge are worse sinners than themselves. Who will be "Left Behind" if they don't get right. Heresy begetting damnable heresy. The leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy, enters a church and corrupts it over time.

Pre-trib rapture is leaven. The idea that nothing matters, that any moment you can be caught up to heaven and so you'll never experience tribulation, appeals to older congregants, but is terrifying to children who aren't secure in the gospel, because they are taught a confusing message of faith plus works. Who are told week after week that "At any moment, maybe before the end of this service, Christ might return!" Doomsday prophets, setting dates on charts are bad enough. But when that date is always "Now!" it becomes a weekly trauma. 

Biblical end times prophesy, the teaching of the rapture being after tribulation, after a falling away, after certain undeniable signs, the man of sin being revealed, etc...is meant to teach us patience and longsuffering. It is hopeful, and should increase our faith. The security of salvation by grace through faith making those that believe understand they are secure, sealed by the Spirit unto redemption tied with the understanding that that redemption may be well after our natural lifetime, leaves the believer in peace. 

The knowledge that the church isn't a "plan B," but the only plan for salvation, and the gospel being true, not changing for different people and eras, is meant to be a comfort, not a terror. Knowing we have already overcome the world in Christ. The peace that passes all understanding.

It would be the height of irony if Dispensationalism was the seed of the great apostasy, the "falling away."

teachings.title: What is written is sufficient
teachings.summary: Against a Catholic claim from John 20-21 of unwritten oral doctrines, he shows those verses speak of signs and say the written word is sufficient to believe and have life.
teachings.text:
Next he cites **John 20:30** and **John 21:25** claiming they teach that there are unwritten doctrines only known by oral tradition. Let's look at it in context;

**John 20:29-31**
*Jesus saith unto him, Thomas, because thou hast seen me, thou hast believed: blessed are they that have not seen, and yet have believed. And many other signs truly did Jesus in the presence of his disciples, which are not written in this book: But these are written, that ye might believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God; and that believing ye might have life through his name.*

**John 21:24-25**
*This is the disciple which testifieth of these things, and wrote these things: and we know that his testimony is true. And there are also many other things which Jesus did, the which, if they should be written every one, I suppose that even the world itself could not contain the books that should be written. Amen.*

These clearly are acts of Jesus, miracles and signs, not doctrines. But what does the Apostle John tell us? That what is written is sufficient to believe on Jesus Christ, the Son of God, and by believing, have life through His name.

If there were need of other records of the signs performed by Jesus, which are so many the world couldn't contain the books required to record them, in order to give us the knowledge to be saved, John wouldn't be able to truthfully write that what was given as testimony was enough.

teachings.title: More blessed to give: not oral tradition
teachings.summary: He answers the Catholic use of Acts 20:35 by showing Christ taught the same in Luke 6:38, so the written word, not tradition, preserves His teaching.
teachings.text:
Next is the claim that **Acts 20:35** says that Jesus' had testimony not found in the gospels. (They use their weird Latin abbreviation for Jesus here, INH). But is that what it says?

*I have shewed you all things, how that so labouring ye ought to support the weak, and to remember the words of the Lord Jesus, how he said, It is more blessed to give than to receive.*

They will say "see? That exact quote doesn't appear in the gospels!"

But does the idea contained in it?

**Luke 6:38**
*Give, and it shall be given unto you; good measure, pressed down, and shaken together, and running over, shall men give into your bosom. For with the same measure that ye mete withal it shall be measured to you again.*

So Jesus taught that it is more blessed to give, that by doing so, by the same measure it will be given back to you.

When Paul, in the Spirit is speaking to the church at Ephesus, the four Gospel accounts had not yet been written. He's not quoting the Gospels, but Christ, Who taught that the Spirit will bring to remembrance all that He said. Luke, in the Spirit is recording it.

And so it is God's intended word, written for our benefit, inspired and preserved, even if it is a paraphrase of a doctrine that was taught by Christ or a direct quote given by the Spirit of that same teaching.

It's a foolish argument to claim that since it is recorded this way here, it isn't what was taught and only available by tradition, when up to this point in Acts, all the words of Christ had been given by preaching.

teachings.title: The tradition Paul gave is written
teachings.summary: He shows Paul's tradition in 2 Thessalonians 3 is written in the epistle and that 2 Peter 1 says scripture came by the Holy Ghost, the opposite of Catholic claims.
teachings.text:
Quickly let me wrap this up.

**2 Thessalonians 3:6**
*Now we command you, brethren, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that ye withdraw yourselves from every brother that walketh disorderly, and not after the tradition which he received of us.*

Again, Paul writes what that tradition is.

*For yourselves know how ye ought to follow us: for we behaved not ourselves disorderly among you; Neither did we eat any man's bread for nought; but wrought with labour and travail night and day, that we might not be chargeable to any of you: Not because we have not power, but to make ourselves an ensample unto you to follow us. For even when we were with you, this we commanded you, that if any would not work, neither should he eat.*
*For we hear that there are some which walk among you disorderly, working not at all, but are busybodies. Now them that are such we command and exhort by our Lord Jesus Christ, that with quietness they work, and eat their own bread. But ye, brethren, be not weary in well doing. And if any man obey not our word by this epistle, note that man, and have no company with him, that he may be ashamed. Yet count him not as an enemy, but admonish him as a brother.*

**Acts 8:31** is referring to giving the Gospel which as we know has to come from a saved Christian using the word of God.

And finally, **2 Peter 1:19-21**
*We have also a more sure word of prophecy; whereunto ye do well that ye take heed, as unto a light that shineth in a dark place, until the day dawn, and the day star arise in your hearts:*
*Knowing this first, that no prophecy of the scripture is of any private interpretation. For the prophecy came not in old time by the will of man: but holy men of God spake as they were moved by the Holy Ghost.*

Peter is directly stating that scripture comes from the inspiration of the Holy Ghost. Not made up by men, not just given by their own imagination. That we can count on it even more than what Peter witnessed with his own eyes and heard with his own ears on the mount of transfiguration, when God spoke from the clouds.

He's literally saying the opposite of what the Catholic Church is trying to rationalize.

teachings.title: The Prophet like unto Moses
teachings.summary: Moses foretold Christ the Prophet, and gave the test for false prophets that Jesus repeated: ye shall know them by their fruits.
teachings.text:
Moses, speaking of Christ, tells the people that the LORD will raise a Prophet from among them, speaking the words of God. There is also a dual fulfilled prophecy here, regarding other prophets of the Lord that shall come, that they may be tested by what they preach, seeing if it is true. And a warning against the false prophets, and that those who are acting presumptuously, telling lies in God's name shall die.

It is the same warning given of Christ against false teachers; that you shall know them by their fruits. *If the thing follow not, nor come to pass*; if their preaching doesn't produce after the things of God, *ye shall know them.*

teachings.title: Little ones with no knowledge of good and evil
teachings.summary: Deuteronomy 1 shows an age of accountability, children being innocent without the law, against the original sin teaching behind infant baptism.
teachings.text:
Beginning **Deuteronomy**, which means 'second law,' Moses retelling of the events that led the Israelites to the verge of the promised land, and the restatement of the law of God. The events retold in this chapter are familiar to us, having just finished **Numbers**. But there is still doctrine to be found.

**Deuteronomy 1** has the clearest proof text on the idea that there is an age of accountability. That children do not carry some original sin, as some insist falsely, but are innocent without the law.

*Moreover your little ones, which ye said should be a prey, and your children, which in that day had no knowledge between good and evil, they shall go in thither, and unto them will I give it, and they shall possess it.*

This isn't a set age, but a spiritual condition. For some, the realization between good and evil comes younger, some older. Some developmentally disabled, it may never come at all.

This idea is reflected in Paul's writing, in **Romans 7:9**

**For I was alive without the law once: but when the commandment came, sin revived, and I died.**

The concept of infants being born with sin is a wicked one, but required by the apostate false churches that teach baby "baptism" in order to make a lifetime claim on a soul, to exert power and control over the masses. The heresy of baptismal regeneration leads to it, and for mothers especially, the idea that their baby could pass and end up in hell or "limbo" was too much to bear. And silly women carried away by false doctrine, like Eve, lead their men to stray. And so, heretical practices take root, and damnable ones at that.

**Matthew 18:2-4**
*And Jesus called a little child unto him, and set him in the midst of them, and said, Verily I say unto you, Except ye be converted, and become as little children, ye shall not enter into the kingdom of heaven. Whosoever therefore shall humble himself as this little child, the same is greatest in the kingdom of heaven.*

We need to humble ourselves as children to receive the grace of salvation. Knowing we are helpless in obtaining our own righteousness and totally reliant on the Father.

teachings.title: Baptized by one Spirit into one body
teachings.summary: 1 Corinthians 12 calls the proud Corinthians to humility as one body under Christ, not to make the gifts evidence of salvation as Pentecostals do.
teachings.text:
By the Spirit of God that has baptized us into the body of Christ, a spiritual baptism, pricked of the heart and sealed by the promise and made a child of God, we become partakers of the gifts given every man, according to the purpose of God.

*The selfsame Spirit, dividing to every man severally as He will.*

Paul, comparing the assembly of saints to a body, Christ as the head (both literally, as ruler and figuratively in this anatomical allusion), gives examples of the talents expressed by believers towards the edification of that body. Building up the church of believers.

The Corinthians, who we know were prideful, set at variance over who it was that led them to Christ, tolerating fornication among them, worse than the unsaved Gentiles, eating meats given to idols, profaning the ordinance of blessing the cup and breaking the bread when they gathered, believing heresies among them, and coveting, resenting and lording over each other when it came to spiritual gifts.

Paul throughout the epistle models the meekness and humility which each Christian should have, understanding that it is God through His Spirit that has granted us knowledge, understanding, to each a minister of the faith that we came to believe, and to each talents in growing the faith, building His church.

In **Romans 12**, the Apostle uses the same formulation;

*For I say, through the grace given unto me, to every man that is among you, not to think of himself more highly than he ought to think; but to think soberly, according as God hath dealt to every man the measure of faith.*

This humility and understanding that we stand by the grace of God, not of ourselves, as part of a single body, is an appeal to be of one mind, one towards another. None thinking they are more important than another. This is the context in both epistles.

But, as we know, many have taken **1 Corinthians 12**, and wrest from that scripture, a different doctrine than the understanding we are all joined as one under Christ, and make it about the gifts themselves, and applying them as evidence of salvation, resulting in entire denominations acting as the yet-unrepentant Corinthians.

Pentecostal denominations, Charismatics and the like, take this rebuke against Corinth, reinforced in Romans and elsewhere, and forge a blueprint for doctrines that aren't being taught by scripture.

teachings.title: Upon this rock: Matthew 16
teachings.summary: Explains that the rock in Matthew 16 is the confession that Jesus is the Christ, not Peter or a denomination, and what the gates of hell not prevailing means.
teachings.text:
**Matthew 16:13-18**
*When Jesus came into the coasts of Caesarea Philippi, he asked his disciples, saying, Whom do men say that I the Son of man am? And they said, Some say that thou art John the Baptist: some, Elias; and others, Jeremias, or one of the prophets. He saith unto them, But whom say ye that I am? And Simon Peter answered and said, **Thou art the Christ, the Son of the living God.** And Jesus answered and said unto him, Blessed art thou, Simon Barjona: for flesh and blood hath not revealed it unto thee, but my Father which is in heaven. And I say also unto thee, That thou art Peter, and **upon this rock** I will build my church; **and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it.***

Catholics cite verse 18, stripped of context, claiming that Simon Peter is the "rock," rather than the testimony that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of the living God. Despite "Peter," or *Petra*/*Cephas* meaning a small stone. (*Thou art Simon the son of Jona: thou shalt be called Cephas, which is by interpretation, A stone*). 

What they also miss is that it is this confession of the faith that Jesus says the gates of Hell shall not prevail against. The "i*t*" in that clause refers back to the "*rock*," which refers back to the Gospel, the truth of Who Jesus is. 

All those who believe on that truth are part of Jesus' church, and the gates of Hell cannot prevail against that confession; believing that Jesus is Christ. 

If we strip the Biblical context away, and try to make sense of it as Peter being the rock, and the church being a physical denomination on earth, what in the world does the phrase "the gates of Hell shall not prevail against" actually mean? 

There is no other reference to "gates of Hell" in scripture, other than Jesus possessing the keys to death and Hell at His resurrection (the Gospel). 

How exactly would Hell's "gates" prevail over anything? How does a doorway to Hell prevail against a church? It becomes a non sequitur in the hands of the natural man, and while it sounds epic, it carries no actual meaning in that incorrect context.

teachings.title: Access by faith into this grace
teachings.summary: We access God's grace, offered to all men, by faith as a free will choice, contrary to Calvinism, and salvation is a free gift without works.
teachings.text:
I wasn't going to take detours in this exercise of Dispensationalism in light of the book of Romans, but I cannot overlook the beauty of chapter 5 and the understanding that everything is in Christ Jesus; *By whom also we have access by faith into this grace wherein we stand, and rejoice in hope of the glory of God.*

Note this carefully. The Calvinist says the special boys chosen by God have access to faith by grace, but the Bible says the exact opposite. We access His grace, which abounds and is to all men, by faith. Just as Adam accessed death by the choice of sin, we access life in Jesus by the same free will choice.

*Therefore as by the offence of one judgment came upon all men to condemnation; even so by the righteousness of one, the free gift came upon all men unto the justification of life.*

Salvation is a free gift. Justification is of Christ. Offered to ALL MEN, by grace. Free. A gift, given without works, without being reckoned of debt. Without our having the glory. Without boasting, which is excluded.

*Therefore being justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ.*

This is the Gospel. And it is to all men. With the law or without. While we were yet sinners, Christ died for us.

*That as sin hath reigned unto death, even so might grace reign through righteousness unto eternal life by Jesus Christ our Lord.*

teachings.title: Justified by faith, offered to all men
teachings.summary: No fair reading of Romans yields faith plus works or salvation only for a chosen few, because Paul plainly concludes justified by faith and to all men.
teachings.text:
Again, it is impossible to read "*Therefore being justified by faith..."* and come away with "it's faith plus works."

Just as it's impossible to read *"to all men*" and say it's only for special boys, chosen because of their unique wonderfulness, "Hey, don't question a sovereign God. He just thinks I am super special and awesome."

God is not a respecter of persons.

It is impossible to say the Mosaic law did anything other than show man our own sinful nature, just as Adam transgressed under one commandment, then so too man transgressed all the more abundantly under the 600 or so contained in the law.

There is no fair reading of Romans that leads to these heresies. It is only by being a heretic first, and then searching for whatever scripture they can wrest with to torture into confirming their own vain imagination.

There are some who say the complex sentences and thoughts can be difficult for some to understand, but luckily for us God is not the author of confusion, and has Paul in the Spirit provide clear and concise summaries of each point as he concludes each argument.

"There is neither Jew nor Greek...."

"Therefore by the deeds of the law there shall no flesh be justified in his sight..."

"To him that worketh not but believes..."

"Therefore being justified by faith..."

teachings.title: The gospel is not 200 years old
teachings.summary: Traces the same salvation by faith in the sacrifice of the Lamb from Adam and Eve, Abel and Cain, and Enos in Genesis 4:26 to answer the claim that the gospel is new.
teachings.text:
There is a resurgence of unsaved people using the false argument that the Gospel by which we are saved is "only 200 years old." Many heresies come in cycles. You will see the same one suddenly pop-up from multiple people, and it is currently the trending heresy I am witnessing. 

The idea that the same salvation of Genesis is "new," is absurd. 

Adam and Eve, having sinned, sought to cover themselves with figleaves they sowed themselves. God corrected them and showed them, covering their sins with the lamb skins He provided, the blood shed representing Christ's, the redemption by faith. 

Righteous Abel believed God and He pleased the Lord. Cain sought to offer his own works and God rebuked him. And Cain in his pride became the first reprobate. 

**Genesis 4:26**
*And to Seth, to him also there was born a son; and he called his name Enos: then began men to call upon the name of the LORD.*

This is the same Gospel as we preach today. Faith in the sacrifice God offered for us. Calling upon the name of the Lord for salvation. Justified in the blood. Covered by the snow white wool of the Lamb slain before the foundation of the world. 

Amen.

teachings.title: Trusting anything but the finished work of Christ
teachings.summary: States that anyone trusting works, rites or turning from sin to be saved is perishing, and gives the gospel of grace by which whosoever believes on the Son is saved, plus nothing, minus nothing.
teachings.text:
If you are trusting in anything other than the finished work of Christ to save you from Hell and death, if you believe that your works play a role in justification before God at the judgment, if you are trusting in traditions, rites, your sacrifices, prayers to saints, carnal ordinances and sacraments, doing good works or turning from your sins to save you, you are assuredly perishing. You must repent towards the Gospel of grace and reconciliation.

The Bible is clear. 

The only salvation is by grace of God, the unmerited favor He extends to all, that whosoever believes on His Son, who was made flesh, lived a sinless life, died for our transgressions, suffered in our place, and rose again to life after 3 days and nights, the propitiation for our sin, and ascended into glory, the first fruits of the promise of eternal life that all believers share. Period. 

Plus nothing. Minus nothing.

teachings.title: Easy believism and the simple gospel of grace
teachings.summary: Answers those who mock the simple gospel as easy believism, saying they add burdens to what Christ paid in full, and calls for repentance toward the gospel of grace and reconciliation.
teachings.text:
People who use the term "easy believism" to derisively mock the simple Gospel of grace and reconciliation, are trying to keep men under the yoke of bondage. They deny that Jesus paid it all. They add burdens grievous to be borne, and lay them on men's shoulders. 

If you aren't sure you have eternal life, if you don't know for certain you have peace with God, if you are counting on your own ability to turn from sin, obey commandments or keep traditions of men, ordinances and sacraments to be saved, repent towards the Gospel of God. The truth that in Christ Jesus, all is forgiven. It doesn't seem easy to just believe, but that is the only way to heaven. 

**Galatians 2:16-21**
*knowing that a man is not justified by the works of the law, but by the faith of Jesus Christ, even we have believed in Jesus Christ, that we might be justified by the faith of Christ, and not by the works of the law: for by the works of the law shall no flesh be justified. But if, while we seek to be justified by Christ, we ourselves also are found sinners, is therefore Christ the minister of sin? God forbid. For if I build again the things which I destroyed, I make myself a transgressor. For I through the law am dead to the law, that I might live unto God. I am crucified with Christ: nevertheless I live; yet not I, but Christ liveth in me: and the life which I now live in the flesh I live by the faith of the Son of God, who loved me, and gave himself for me. I do not frustrate the grace of God: for if righteousness come by the law, then Christ is dead in vain.*

teachings.title: Easy-believism and the strait gate
teachings.summary: Salvation by believing on Christ alone, mocked as easy-believism, is the strait gate few find, because pride, works and the false hope of repent-of-your-sins preachers keep men from simply trusting that Jesus paid it all.
teachings.text:
**John 3:16-18**
*For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life. For God sent not his Son into the world to condemn the world; but that the world through him might be saved. He that believeth on him is not condemned: but he that believeth not is condemned already, because he hath not believed in the name of the only begotten Son of God.*

**Acts 16:30-31**
*And brought them out, and said, Sirs, what must I do to be saved? And they said, Believe on the Lord Jesus Christ, and thou shalt be saved, and thy house.*

This is the Gospel of faith, taught throughout the Bible. But it is derisively called "easy-believism" by those seeking to bring another gospel of works and self-righteousness.

If believing the Gospel for salvation were "easy," then why do so many people struggle with trusting in Christ Jesus alone for their salvation? Why does every false religion reject this simple faith for works and penance?

**Matthew 7:13-14**
