*Enter ye in at the strait gate: for wide is the gate, and broad is the way, that leadeth to destruction, and many there be which go in thereat: because strait is the gate, and narrow is the way, which leadeth unto life, and few there be that find it.*

Believing on Christ alone for salvation is the narrow way. The strait gate. And there really are few who find it.

Pride and vanity and inability to trust the word of God keeps people from letting go and trusting by faith. They want reassurance that it "worked" before they can let go. They are carrying so much of a burden, and yoked by the law, that they cannot fit through that strait gate. Like a camel trying to pass through the eye of a needle. And so they seek a wider path to their own destruction.

Or they want to force their way through by exhibiting signs of deserving it through their own acts of righteousness, which the Bible calls filthy rags. Greasing the entrance by their own good intentions, so that they can accept that they "deserve" to enter. Not realizing none deserve it, but we are given entrance through Christ.

They want to know without trust, so that they may believe, and so they never can come to the knowledge of the truth. Because *faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen*. And without visible evidence, they doubt, and are given false hope from the "Repent-of-your-sins" types who claim that they may know they are saved if they do certain acts, and behave a certain way. But that false hope gives way when any weight is put upon it, because their standards are impossible to achieve in the flesh. It is impossible to pass through that gate carrying our own works, which are wood, hay and stubble, fit to be burned.

We don't begin to be sanctified until we are in the kingdom already. Until we have passed through that gate. Without faith, it is impossible to please God.

So don't be fooled. Salvation is easy, from a works standpoint because it doesn't require any effort from us to believe that Jesus paid it all. But it is hard from a human standpoint, letting go of all the burdens that keep us from passing through.

teachings.title: Judgment on nations for innocent blood and idolatry
teachings.summary: God pours out judgment on nations that shed innocent blood and on apostate churches, like Rome and her daughters, that commit idolatry in His name.
teachings.text:
*For this city hath been to me as a provocation of mine anger and of my fury from the day that they built it even unto this day; that I should remove it from before my face, Because of all the evil of the children of Israel and of the children of Judah, which they have done to provoke me to anger, they, their kings, their princes, their priests, and their prophets, and the men of Judah, and the inhabitants of Jerusalem. And they have turned unto me the back, and not the face: though I taught them, rising up early and teaching them, yet they have not hearkened to receive instruction. But they set their abominations in the house, which is called by my name, to defile it.*

*And they built the high places of Baal, which are in the valley of the son of Hinnom, to cause their sons and their daughters to pass through the fire unto Molech; which I commanded them not, neither came it into my mind, that they should do this abomination, to cause Judah to sin.*

Again and again we see God's judgment poured out on nations that shed innocent blood, child sacrifice as part of worshiping false gods being the worst example of this.

And in addition to this, the evil committed in His name, in His house. The offerings to false gods. The Idolatry. The burning of candles and incense to them. All in His holy name, this is abomination to God.

Apostate churches that engage in these abominations, who call themselves of Christ  but yet do these wicked acts, will not harken to instruction He has given, who reject His gospel for their own vain traditions; all of this brings judgement on a people. And because of it, our nations are being destroyed today.

Catholicism and its harlot daughters, false teachers and damnable heresies, idolatry and cannibalism (coming from the Canaanites), meat and drink sacrificed to idols, consuming "flesh and blood," all of it is abomination and His wrath abides on the people who allow it.

teachings.title: The red heifer and the burnt offerings pictured Christ
teachings.summary: Reads the red heifer of Numbers 19 and the Levitical sacrifices as pictures of Christ already fulfilled, warning against the idea that they are a prophecy for the Jews today.
teachings.text:
The burnt offerings in the Old Testament were all a picture of Christ Jesus. Not a prophecy of the Jews today. See **👇**

**Numbers 19**
*And the Lord spake unto Moses and unto Aaron, saying,

2 This is the ordinance of the law which the Lord hath commanded, saying, Speak unto the children of Israel, that they bring thee a red heifer without spot, wherein is no blemish, and upon which never came yoke:

3 And ye shall give her unto Eleazar the priest, that he may bring her forth without the camp, and one shall slay her before his face:

4 And Eleazar the priest shall take of her blood with his finger, and sprinkle of her blood directly before the tabernacle of the congregation seven times:

5 And one shall burn the heifer in his sight; her skin, and her flesh, and her blood, with her dung, shall he burn:

6 And the priest shall take cedar wood, and hyssop, and scarlet, and cast it into the midst of the burning of the heifer.

7 Then the priest shall wash his clothes, and he shall bathe his flesh in water, and afterward he shall come into the camp, and the priest shall be unclean until the even.

8 And he that burneth her shall wash his clothes in water, and bathe his flesh in water, and shall be unclean until the even.

9 And a man that is clean shall gather up the ashes of the heifer, and lay them up without the camp in a clean place, and it shall be kept for the congregation of the children of Israel for a water of separation: it is a purification for sin.

*
The foolish and unbiblical "Red Heifer prophecy" was created in 1989 by an American Pentecostal preacher who practiced Zionist-dispensationalism, and who decided that, since he bred red cattle, and one of the carnal ordinances included a burnt offering of a red heifer, that should the Jews offer one, they could usher in the end times, forcing God's judgment and the second coming of Christ. 

Since then, Jews have been using this half-assed prophecy to fundraise off of gullible Christians misled by Scofield, wicked TV charismatics funded by Israel, and a generation of pastors trained to teach the worship of Jews over Christ. 

We see clearly in the one mention of a red heifer, that it was yet another picture of Christ Jesus. The cedar wood, the hyssop and the scarlet, present during the time Abraham set to offer his son Issac, upon the same hill Jesus would later be crucified on, and included in many of the burnt offerings described in the Levitical laws, all of which pictured Christ. 

The cedar of the cross. The hyssop soaked in vinegar. The scarlet of His blood given for us. The oblation given of a spotless sacrifice. A propitiation for our sin. To whom no yoke had ever been upon. 

This false teaching is having renewed interest today, as the Jews who say they are but are not, but do lie, attempt to join in the propaganda campaign going on now to meme judgment day into being. To trick God, and despair men. 

Don't be fooled! God's timing is His own and the sacrifices of the Old Testament were a picture of His Son, who has come already and in whom the sins of the world have already been paid by the blood He shed. He was the burnt offering, in Hell three days and nights, and resurrected into glory, overcoming the world. With the keys to Hell and Death. 

Be at peace in Jesus. Let no man deceive you. Be not afraid.

Remember that this is the reason God destroyed Israel and brought judgement upon Judah. Child sacrifice, as the Canaanites did.

teachings.title: Learn not the way of the heathen
teachings.summary: Astrology and idols are vanity and foolishness before the Creator, and the heathen worship created things rather than the living God.
teachings.text:
We are there in **Jeremiah** chapter 10, and the Lord, speaking through the prophet by the Spirit is casting judgments upon Judah, the remaining children of Israel, this time focusing on their adopting the heathen practices of idol worshiping of graven images. Wood carvings plated with molten metals, hammered into place and carried about for feasts and religious practices.

He begins by warning them not to be caught up in the signs of the sky. Astrology and the movement of the lights in the firmament, given as we read in Genesis as a way to mark time, but being used by those who worship idols and small gods that are of their own wicked imagination. To scare people into thinking catastrophe was nigh.

Babylonians especially had very advanced system of astrological prophesying, and God says this is vanity. Just as the workman and the founder, cutting down trees to make idols to Baal or the Queen of Heaven are vain.

It is important to see things as God sees them. And as He is the creator of all things, His view of the superstitious nonsense men invents to explain His creation, including to worship the things He created, is both insulting to a jealous God, and laughably foolish.

**Romans 1:21-25**
*Because that, when they knew God, they glorified him not as God, neither were thankful; but became vain in their imaginations, and their foolish heart was darkened. Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools, And changed the glory of the uncorruptible God into an image made like to corruptible man, and to birds, and fourfooted beasts, and creeping things. Wherefore God also gave them up to uncleanness through the lusts of their own hearts, to dishonour their own bodies between themselves: Who changed the truth of God into a lie, and worshipped and served the creature more than the Creator, who is blessed for ever. Amen.*

We worship the living God, through Whom all things were made. The heathen in their fear worship the sun, the moon, the stars. Idols made of wood and stone and molten metals.

**Psalm 115:5-8**
*They have mouths, but they speak not: eyes have they, but they see not: They have ears, but they hear not: noses have they, but they smell not: They have hands, but they handle not: feet have they, but they walk not: neither speak they through their throat. They that make them are like unto them; so is every one that trusteth in them.*

teachings.title: Jeremiah 10 is not about Christmas trees
teachings.summary: Jeremiah 10 condemns carved idols, not decorative trees, so believers may celebrate Christ's birth in good conscience and others should not judge them.
teachings.text:
**Colossians 2:16-23**
*Let no man therefore judge you in meat, or in drink, or in respect of an holyday, or of the new moon, or of the sabbath days: which are a shadow of things to come; but the body is of Christ. Let no man beguile you of your reward in a voluntary humility and worshipping of angels, intruding into those things which he hath not seen, vainly puffed up by his fleshly mind, and not holding the Head, from which all the body by joints and bands having nourishment ministered, and knit together, increaseth with the increase of God. Wherefore if ye be dead with Christ from the rudiments of the world, why, as though living in the world, are ye subject to ordinances, (touch not; taste not; handle not; which all are to perish with the using;) after the commandments and doctrines of men? Which things have indeed a shew of wisdom in will worship, and humility, and neglecting of the body; not in any honour to the satisfying of the flesh.*

There are many false teachers, Reddit theologians and sincere but misled believers, who have taken **Jeremiah 10** out of context, to make the claim that this chapter isn't about graven images, carved, fashioned and decked with plated gold and silver, idols that are being worshipped and feared as if they have power, and saying that it is explicitly about the tradition of the Christmas tree.

That it is, preaching against decorating your house with a plant while celebrating the birth of Christ Jesus. That the practice of having house plants and decorative trees is itself paganism. But what does God instruct?

**Isaiah 60:13**
*The glory of Lebanon shall come unto thee, the fir tree, the pine tree, and the box together, to beautify the place of my sanctuary; and I will make the place of my feet glorious.*

The Bible doesn't teach against use of plants as decoration. It shows us God uses evergreen trees to beautify His temple.

No one bows and serves a decorative house plant, they beautify their homes with them. No one worships a pine tree except pagan "druid" LARPers.

Even the most secular reprobate consumerist, who strips Christ from Christmas and makes it entirely about snowmen and reindeer and coveting things, doesn't look at the plastic tree covered in lights and tinsel in the corner of their living room and thinks, "I shall worship this." They don't even "venerate" it.

But that hasn't stopped some from judging believers in respect to holy days, and teaching doctrine of men for commandments.

There are plenty of reasons to not want to participate in traditional Christmas trappings, especially as they have become in the modern, consumerist world of greed. The lie of Santa, the works-based system that you have to be good, "repent of your sins or you don't get a present!" The profane and the blasphemous way our Jewish-subverted culture has secularized it all.

But most believing Christians see the season as simply a feast celebrating the miracle of the birth of our Lord and Savior, Jesus Christ.

Most take the season to reflect on scripture, give thanksgiving to God the Father for His Son, to sing Psalms and hymns praising Him. And decorating their homes, eating special meals with family. And giving gifts in the spirit of grace, just as God has given to each of us.

If you don't want to worship Jesus this way, and if you are convinced of yourself that it is a sin, then you should not do it.

And regardless of your conviction, **Romans 14** should apply;

*1 Him that is weak in the faith receive ye, but not to doubtful disputations.*

*2 For one believeth that he may eat all things: another, who is weak, eateth herbs.*

*3 Let not him that eateth despise him that eateth not; and let not him which eateth not judge him that eateth: for God hath received him.*

*4 Who art thou that judgest another man's servant? to his own master he standeth or falleth. Yea, he shall be holden up: for God is able to make him stand.*

*5 One man esteemeth one day above another: another esteemeth every day alike. Let every man be fully persuaded in his own mind.*

teachings.title: Justified by the faith of Christ, not the works of the law
teachings.summary: Answers the claim that works of the law means only ceremonial law, using Galatians 2 and Romans 4, and sets Christ's once-for-all sacrifice in Hebrews 10 against Rome's daily sacrifice.
teachings.text:
**Galatians 2:16-21 **
K*nowing that a man is not justified by the works of the law, **but by the faith of Jesus Christ, even we have believed in Jesus Christ, that we might be justified by the faith of Christ**, and not by the works of the law: for by the works of the law shall no flesh be justified*.

I just banned a pagan heretic from the chat, who insisted that works are needed for salvation. When presented with this emphatic passage from the epistle to the church at Galatia, he used the standard apologetics dodge that "works of the law" only pertains to Levitical ceremonial laws. 

This is false, as we see elsewhere (**Romans 4** for example), but even within this passage they always fail to address the other emphatically-made point, that man IS JUSTIFIED ***by the faith of Jesus Christ, even we have believed in Jesus Christ, that we might be justified by the faith of Christ***.

**Romans 4**
*What shall we say then that Abraham our father, as pertaining to the flesh, hath found?

2 For if Abraham were justified by works, he hath whereof to glory; but not before God.

3 For what saith the scripture? Abraham believed God, and it was counted unto him for righteousness.

4 Now to him that worketh is the reward not reckoned of grace, but of debt.

5 But to him that worketh not, but believeth on him that justifieth the ungodly, his faith is counted for righteousness.

6 Even as David also describeth the blessedness of the man, unto whom God imputeth righteousness without works,

7 Saying, Blessed are they whose iniquities are forgiven, and whose sins are covered.

8 Blessed is the man to whom the Lord will not impute sin*.

This defines it clearly, that works of the law is a debt, not grace, and that it pertains to sin. And what is sin?

**1 John 3:4-6**
*Whosoever committeth sin transgresseth also the law: for sin is the transgression of the law. And ye know that he was manifested to take away our sins; and in him is no sin. Whosoever abideth in him sinneth not: whosoever sinneth hath not seen him, neither known him.*

As we see in **1 Timothy 1:9**

*Knowing this, that the law is not made for a righteous man, but for the lawless and disobedient, for the ungodly and for sinners, for unholy and profane, for murderers of fathers and murderers of mothers, for manslayers*...

It's simple. But those carried away by their own vain conceits cannot see it.

**Hebrews 10:9-13**
*Then said he, Lo, I come to do thy will, O God. He taketh away the first, that he may establish the second. **By the which will we are sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all.** And every priest standeth daily ministering and offering oftentimes the same sacrifices, which can never take away sins: **But this man, after he had offered one sacrifice for sins for ever, **sat down on the right hand of God; From henceforth expecting till his enemies be made his footstool.*

The apostate cult of Rome, with its priests daily offering meat and drink sacrifice to idols, that profane Christ by turning His sacrifice once and for all, and the ordinance to remember it by, into a cannibal cult, deny that Jesus Christ, being the substitutionary sacrifice, the propitiation for sin that was offered once and for all, paid it all.

teachings.title: God hates idols among His people
teachings.summary: Idol worship by those claiming His name, such as Catholics and Orthodox, provokes God's wrath and is a leading reason for the curses on Europe and America.
teachings.text:
It should go without saying that our God, Whose name is Jealous, and Who demands by His righteousness all the glory, hates Idolatry. He hates the veneration and worship of idols, *especially* by those claiming to be of His people. The Second Commandment is again hammered home here in the opening verse;

*Ye shall make you no idols nor graven image, neither rear you up a standing image, neither shall ye set up any image of stone in your land, to bow down unto it: for I am the Lord your God.*

Those who call themselves by His name who bow before statues of stone, standing images and molten and graven idols, are what spark His wrath.

Catholicism and Orthodox Christianity, so called, the apostates who reject salvation by grace, and set up images to be served and bowed before in supplication, are the leading reason why Europe and America are suffering today. Why these curses and others spelled out by God throughout the Old Testament, are afflicting our land today.

When Asa became king and *he took away the sodomites out of the land, and removed all the idols that his fathers had made*, the Bible says he did what was right in the eyes of the Lord.

If we were to have a return to doing what was right in the eyes of the Lord, we who are His people would need to destroy every image and idol, from the blasphemy of St. Patrick's Cathedral, to every profane "crucifix," to every bathtub Mary in every Catholic yard, throughout the land.

teachings.title: Let no man judge you in meat or holy days
teachings.summary: Sanctification is not automatic or required for salvation, and believers must not be beguiled by philosophy, traditions or asceticism that pass for holiness.
teachings.text:
I would that all who believe on Christ for salvation come to the understanding that, as befitting a quickened spirit, a new man, we put off the lusts of the flesh and put on the things of God. Mortifying our members, being dead to sin.

But as Paul explains, this isn't automatic. It isn't even a necessity to salvation, as he is writing we who are saved by faith in Christ.

And because it is not automatic, and yet our new man cries out for us to be holy, many men take advantage of this conflict, warning within our members. They come with philosophy and vain deceit; that is the ideas of men that claim to know truth, often that is hidden, that doesn't come from scripture. Or from traditions of men, that things that come from the vain beliefs, and are adopted as religious practices, must be followed. These things aren't of Christ.

Christ in whom we not only have died with and been quickened, and redeemed, our sins done away with and the ordinances taken away. Nailed to His cross.

Therefore, we should not allow any man to judge us in meat, or in drink, or in respect to an holiday, or new moon, or sabbath, all of which were shadows of Christ, or any other condition that they teach for doctrine that are commandments of men and offered in their place.

This means that the vain philosophy of men, as well as the old testament strictures, have no power over we who are saved by faith in Christ. And men who place these things as stumbling blocks and snares are attempting to beguile us. Trapping us into things like voluntary humility, that is sackcloth and ashes. Self-flagellation. Aestheticism, the denial of self for the purpose of self-righteousness (*Touch not; taste not; handle not; Which all are to perish with the using)*.

Weird doctrines like the worship of angels (or saints). Things that they haven't seen themselves, but imagine in their fleshly mind. Things other than Christ who is the head of us who are saved.

Don't be misled by people who indeed seem holy, who may be able to make an argument of men in the wisdom of how they worship in their humility and neglecting things of the body. Unsaved and even reprobates, can fast for example. They may live without gluttony or abstaining from alcohol. They may be even living "cleaner" than some saved Christians. They may refuse to celebrate certain holidays or feasts, citing earthly reasons and the denial of themselves as a form of righteousness. But these are all lies and not of Christ, in whom is liberty.

Chapter 3 goes into details of how a saved Christian *should* seek to clean up their lives. These things that should be done because we are free in Christ and dead to the flesh. Not because man tells us to. Not to show our own holiness but to put off these deeds as new creatures, not beholden to the things of the flesh. But renewed in the knowledge of Christ, as the elect of God. Using the wisdom of His doctrines to teach and rebuke one another. Giving thanks to God through Christ Jesus.

It is the subtle difference between legalism and rejoicing that we are free in grace. And discernment is required.

teachings.title: White-knuckle Christians carried away by strange doctrines
teachings.summary: Believers outside a local church fall into strange doctrines, purity spirals and online crusades, seeking to establish their own righteousness.
teachings.text:
They tend to be carried away by strange doctrines, weird beliefs, Old heresies dressed up as new. And unfortunately, there are way too many people out there looking to take advantage of these people for a variety of reasons. Some malignant and others just out of ignorance or because of their own emotional baggage.

And like a white knuckle addict pushing themselves through sobriety, with the nagging realization that they are going to fail hanging over them, placing the entire burden on themselves, the white knuckle Christian does the same.

They begin to either set their own standard or adopt the commandments of men. And go about seeking to establish their own righteousness. Because they're not plugged into a local church and they're not doing actual things for God, they get caught up in nonsense crusades. Purity spirals. And the other trappings of online scenes.

teachings.title: Belief on the Son: what the record in John says it takes to be saved
teachings.summary: Strings together the believe passages of John and 1 John 5 to show that eternal life is given to those who believe on the Son, and that anyone who adds requirements to that belief brings another gospel.
teachings.text:
**1 John 5:9-12**
*If we receive the witness of men, the witness of God is greater: for this is the witness of God which he hath testified of his Son. **He that believeth on the Son of God hath the witness in himself**: he that believeth not God hath made him a liar; because he believeth not the record that God gave of his Son. **And this is the record, that God hath given to us eternal life, and this life is in his Son. He that hath the Son hath life; and he that hath not the Son of God hath not life.***

**John 1:6-8**
*There was a man sent from God, whose name was John. **The same came for a witness, to bear witness of the Light, that all men through him might believe.** He was not that Light, but was sent to bear witness of that Light.*

**John 1:11-13**
*He came unto his own, and his own received him not. **But as many as received him, to them gave he power to become the sons of God, even to them that believe on his name**: Which were born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God.*

**John 2:11**
*This beginning of miracles did Jesus in Cana of Galilee, and manifested forth his glory; **and his disciples believed on him***.

**John 2:19-23**
*Jesus answered and said unto them, Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up. Then said the Jews, Forty and six years was this temple in building, and wilt thou rear it up in three days? But he spake of the temple of his body. When therefore he was risen from the dead, **his disciples remembered that he had said this unto them; and they believed the scripture, and the word which Jesus had said.** Now when he was in Jerusalem at the passover, in the feast day, **many believed in his name,** when they saw the miracles which he did.*

**John 3:12**
If *I have told you earthly things, and ye believe not, **how shall ye believe, if I tell you of heavenly things?***

**John 3:14-18**
*And as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, even so must the Son of man be lifted up: **That whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have eternal life.** For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that **whosoever believeth in him should not perish,** but have everlasting life. For God sent not his Son into the world to condemn the world; but that the world through him might be saved.
**He that believeth on him is not condemned: but he that believeth not is condemned already,** because he hath not believed in the name of the only begotten Son of God.*

**John 3:36**
***He that believeth on the Son hath everlasting life:** and he that believeth not the Son shall not see life; but the wrath of God abideth on him.*

**John 4:39**-**42**
*And many of the Samaritans of that city **believed on him for the saying of the woman,** which testified, He told me all that ever I did.* *So when the Samaritans were come unto him, they besought him that he would tarry with them: and he abode there two days. **And many more believed because of his own word;** And said unto the woman, **Now we believe, not because of thy saying: for we have heard him ourselves, and know that this is indeed the Christ, the Saviour of the world.***

**John 4:46-50**
*So Jesus came again into Cana of Galilee, where he made the water wine. And there was a certain nobleman, whose son was sick at Capernaum. When he heard that Jesus was come out of Judaea into Galilee, he went unto him, and besought him that he would come down, and heal his son: for he was at the point of death. Then said Jesus unto him, Except ye see signs and wonders, ye will not believe. The nobleman saith unto him, Sir, come down ere my child die. **Jesus saith unto him, Go thy way; thy son liveth. And the man believed the word that Jesus had spoken unto him,** and he went his way.*

**John 5:24**
*Verily, verily, I say unto you, **He that heareth my word, and believeth on him that sent me, hath everlasting life**, and shall not come into condemnation; but is passed from death unto life.*

**John 5:37-39**
*And the Father himself, which hath sent me, hath borne witness of me. Ye have neither heard his voice at any time, nor seen his shape. And ye have not his word abiding in you: **for whom he hath sent, him ye believe not.** Search the scriptures; for in them ye think ye have eternal life: and they are they which testify of me.

**John 5:43-46**
I am come in my Father's name, and ye receive me not: if another shall come in his own name, him ye will receive. How can ye believe, which receive honour one of another, and seek not the honour that cometh from God only? Do not think that I will accuse you to the Father: there is one that accuseth you, even Moses, in whom ye trust. For had ye believed Moses, ye would have believed me; for he wrote of me.
*
**John 6:28-29**
*Then said they unto him, What shall we do, that we might work the works of God? **Jesus answered and said unto them, This is the work of God, that ye believe on him whom he hath sent.***

**John 6:35**-36
*And Jesus said unto them, I am the bread of life: **he that cometh to me shall never hunger; and he that believeth on me shall never thirst**. But I said unto you, That ye also have seen me, and believe not.*

**John 6:39-40 **
*And this is the Father's will which hath sent me, that of all which he hath given me I should lose nothing, but should raise it up again at the last day.
And this is the will of him that sent me, that every one which seeth the Son, and believeth on him, may have everlasting life: and I will raise him up at the last day.*

**John 6:68-70**
*Then Simon Peter answered him, Lord, to whom shall we go? thou hast the words of eternal life. **And we believe and are sure that thou art that Christ, the Son of the living God.** Jesus answered them, Have not I chosen you twelve, and one of you is a devil?*

**John 7:31-32**
***And many of the people believed on him,** and said, When Christ cometh, will he do more miracles than these which this man hath done? The Pharisees heard that the people murmured such things concerning him; and the Pharisees and the chief priests sent officers to take him.*

**John 7:38-40**
 *He that believeth on me, as the scripture hath said, out of his belly shall flow rivers of living water. (**But this spake he of the Spirit, which they that believe on him should receive**: for the Holy Ghost was not yet given; because that Jesus was not yet glorified.) **John 8:23-25**
*And he said unto them, Ye are from beneath; I am from above: ye are of this world; I am not of this world. I said therefore unto you, that ye shall die in your sins: **for if ye believe not that I am he, ye shall die in your sins**. Then said they unto him, Who art thou? And Jesus saith unto them, Even the same that I said unto you from the beginning.*

**John 8:30-32**
*As he spake these words, many believed on him. Then said Jesus to those Jews **which believed on him,** If ye continue in my word, then are ye my disciples indeed; And **ye shall know the truth, and the truth shall make you free**.

***John 8:44-46***
Ye are of your father the devil, and the lusts of your father ye will do. He was a murderer from the beginning, and abode not in the truth, because there is no truth in him. When he speaketh a lie, he speaketh of his own: for he is a liar, and the father of it. And because I tell you the truth, ye believe me not. Which of you convinceth me of sin? **John 9:35-38**
*Jesus heard that they had cast him out; and when he had found him, he said unto him, Dost thou believe on the Son of God? He answered and said, Who is he, Lord, that I might believe on him? And Jesus said unto him, Thou hast both seen him, and it is he that talketh with thee. And he said, **Lord, I believe. And he worshipped him*****.**

**John 10:25-27**
*Jesus answered them, **I told you, and ye believed not:** the works that I do in my Father's name, they bear witness of me. **But ye believe not, because ye are not of my sheep**, as I said unto you. My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me*.


**John 10:37-39**
*If I do not the works of my Father, believe me not. But if I do, though ye believe not me, believe the works: that ye may know, and believe, that the Father is in me, and I in him. Therefore they sought again to take him: but he escaped out of their hand

**John 10:42**
And many believed on him there.*

**John 11:14-16**
*Then said Jesus unto them plainly, Lazarus is dead. **And I am glad for your sakes that I was not there, to the intent ye may believe**; nevertheless let us go unto him. Then said Thomas, which is called Didymus, unto his fellowdisciples, Let us also go, that we may die with him.*

**John 11:24-27**
*Martha saith unto him, I know that he shall rise again in the resurrection at the last day. Jesus said unto her, I am the resurrection, and the life: he that believeth in me, though he were dead, yet shall he live: **And whosoever liveth and believeth in me shall never die. Believest thou this? She saith unto him, Yea, Lord: I believe that thou art the Christ, the Son of God, which should come into the world.***

**John 11:40**
*Jesus saith unto her, **Said I not unto thee, that, if thou wouldest believe, thou shouldest see the glory of God?***

**John 11:41-43**
*Then they took away the stone from the place where the dead was laid. And Jesus lifted up his eyes, and said, Father, I thank thee that thou hast heard me. And I knew that thou hearest me always: but because of the people which stand by I said it, **that they may believe that thou hast sent me.** And when he thus had spoken, he cried with a loud voice, Lazarus, come forth.*

**John 11:45**
*Then many of the Jews which came to Mary, and had seen the things which Jesus did, **believed on him**.*

**John 12:10-12**
*But the chief priests consulted that they might put Lazarus also to death;
Because that by reason of him many of the Jews went away, and believed on Jesus. On the next day much people that were come to the feast, when they heard that Jesus was coming to Jerusalem*

**John 12:36**
*While ye have light, **believe in the light, that ye may be the children of light.** These things spake Jesus, and departed, and did hide himself from them.*

**John 12:37-40**
*But though he had done so many miracles before them, **yet they believed not on him:** That the saying of Esaias the prophet might be fulfilled, which he spake, **Lord, who hath believed our report? and to whom hath the arm of the Lord been revealed?** Therefore **they could not believe,** because that Esaias said again, **He hath blinded their eyes, and hardened their heart; that they should not see with their eyes, nor understand with their heart, and be converted, and I should heal them**.*

**John 12:42-48**
*Nevertheless among the chief rulers also **many believed on him**; but because of the Pharisees they did not confess him, lest they should be put out of the synagogue: For they loved the praise of men more than the praise of God. Jesus cried and said, **He that believeth on me, believeth not on me, but on him that sent me.** And he that seeth me seeth him that sent me**.***** *I am come a light into the world, that whosoever believeth on me should not abide in darkness. And if any man hear my words, and believe not, I judge him not: for I came not to judge the world, but to save the world. He that rejecteth me, and receiveth not my words, hath one that judgeth him: the word that I have spoken, the same shall judge him in the last day.***

**John 13:18-20 **
*I speak not of you all: I know whom I have chosen: but that the scripture may be fulfilled, He that eateth bread with me hath lifted up his heel against me. Now I tell you before it come, that, **when it is come to pass, ye may believe that I am he. Verily, verily, I say unto you, He that receiveth whomsoever I send receiveth me; and he that receiveth me receiveth him that sent me**.*

**John 14:1**
*Let not your heart be troubled: ye** believe in God, believe also in me.***

*Jesus saith unto him, Have I been so long time with you, and yet hast thou not known me, Philip? he that hath seen me hath seen the Father; and how sayest thou then, Show us the Father? **John 14:12**
*Verily, verily, I say unto you, He that believeth on me, the works that I do shall he do also; and greater works than these shall he do; because I go unto my Father.*

**John 14:29**
*And now I have told you before it come to pass, that, when it is come to pass, ye might believe.*

**John 16:7-12**

And when he is come, he will reprove the world of sin, and of righteousness, and of judgment: Of sin, because they believe not on me; Of righteousness, because I go to my Father, and ye see me no more; Of judgment, because the prince of this world is judged. I have yet many things to say unto you, but ye cannot bear them now.*

**John 16:27**
*For the Father himself loveth you, because ye have loved me, **and have believed** that I came out from God*.

**John 16:29-32**
*His disciples said unto him, Lo, now speakest thou plainly, and speakest no proverb. **John 17:5-9**

Now they have known that all things whatsoever thou hast given me are of thee. **For I have given unto them the words which thou gavest me; and they have received them, and have known surely that I came out from thee, and they have believed that thou didst send me. I pray for them: I pray not for the world, but for them which thou hast given me; for they are thine.***

**John 17:20-23**
***Neither pray I for these alone, but for them also which shall believe on me through their word**; That they all may be one; as thou, Father, art in me, and I in thee, that they also may be one in us: **that the world may believe that thou hast sent me.** And the glory which thou gavest me I have given them; that they may be one, even as we are one: I in them, and thou in me, that they may be made perfect in one; and that the world may know that thou hast sent me, and hast loved them, as thou hast loved me.*

**John 19:34-36**
*But one of the soldiers with a spear pierced his side, and forthwith came there out blood and water. **And he that saw it bare record, and his record is true: and he knoweth that he saith true, that ye might believe. **For these things were done, that the scripture should be fulfilled, A bone of him shall not be broken.
*
**John 20:8**
*Then went in also that other disciple, which came first to the sepulchre, and he saw, and believed.*

**John 20:25-30**
*The other disciples therefore said unto him, We have seen the Lord. But he said unto them, Except I shall see in his hands the print of the nails, and put my finger into the print of the nails, and thrust my hand into his side, I will not believe. And after eight days again his disciples were within, and Thomas with them: then came Jesus, the doors being shut, and stood in the midst, and said, Peace be unto you.
Then saith he to Thomas, R**each hither thy finger, and behold my hands; and reach hither thy hand, and thrust it into my side: and be not faithless, but believing. And Thomas answered and said unto him, My Lord and my God. Jesus saith unto him, Thomas, because thou hast seen me, thou hast believed: blessed are they that have not seen, and yet have believed**. And many other signs truly did Jesus in the presence of his disciples, which are not written in this book*

**John 20:31**
*But these are written, that ye might believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God; and that believing ye might have life through his name.*

Let me post this again:

**But these are written, that ye might believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God; and that believing ye might have life through his name.
**
In case you aren't clear about what it takes to be saved. It isn't knowledge of the law, or adherence to the law. It isn't turning from sin, it isn't your willingness to turn from sin. It isn't that you were chosen to believe when others aren't. It wasn't because of who you are or where you were born or into what family or what genealogy you have or anything else about you. 

As the Gospel of John, which is the only book of the Bible specifically written to the unsaved that they may BELIEVE that the Lord Jesus is the Christ, and BY BELIEVING ye might have life in His name. 

That's the Gospel of God. That is the record of Him who sent Jesus, the Son of God, to die for our sins, and to be risen up again on the 3rd day, as the firstfruits of the promise. And by believing this, have eternal life. Sealed by the Spirit, become a child of God. 

**1 John 5:9-12**
*If we receive the witness of men, the witness of God is greater: **for this is the witness of God which he hath testified of his Son. He that believeth on the Son of God hath the witness in himself: he that believeth not God hath made him a liar; because he believeth not the record that God gave of his Son. And this is the record, that God hath given to us eternal life, and this life is in his Son. He that hath the Son hath life; and he that hath not the Son of God hath not life.***

Anyone, I mean this, anyone who adds requirements to this belief on Christ Jesus for salvation, in any manner, isn't saved, and is bringing a false gospel. Let them be accursed. I say again, anyone who adds *anything* to this record given by God of eternal life in His Son, let them be accursed. It's another gospel. Let them be anathema.

Every damnable heresy that adds to this simple Gospel, that God so loved the world that he gave His only begotten Son, that Jesus is the Christ, that all who believe on Him shall not perish but have everlasting life, seeks to take the glory away from God, cheapen His grace and puts Christ to an open shame, because every damnable heresy seeks to make us the focus, to be special boys who deserve salvation in some way. 

Every single one. 

There are none righteous no not one. All of us deserve death and Hell for our sins. Even if you "turned from your sins," you are still a sinner. Even if you cleaned up your life. Even if you stopped smoking and drinking and fornicating. You still lie. You still know good and do it not. You still have foolish thoughts. You still war with the flesh. It is an impossible standard to put on people to tell them they have to turn from their sins to be saved. And it is unbiblical and a false gospel anyway. 

*For they bind heavy burdens and grievous to be borne, and lay them on men's shoulders; but they themselves will not move them with one of their fingers.*

What the person who says you have to repent of your sins to be saved actually means is you have to be "as good as they are," or they will doubt your salvation. You have to live up to their standard, or it doesn't count. They are hypocrites. The worst hypocrites, *teaching for doctrines the commandments of men*. They preach against their pet sins and tell others they cannot come to Christ unless they follow these commandments of men. That believing on Christ isn't sufficient, and list vain and doubtful disputations as doctrines, their own inventions of righteousness, *and have omitted the weightier matters of the law, judgment, mercy, and faith: these ought ye to have done, and not to leave the other undone.*

They are angry, bitter, they hold their knowledge of the truth in pride, if they have it at all. If they are saved, they preach Christ out of contention. They *give heed to fables and endless genealogies, which minister questions, rather than godly edifying which is in faith*. Turning aside to vain jangling. *Desiring to be teachers of the law; understanding neither what they say, nor whereof they affirm.*

*This is a faithful saying, and worthy of all acceptation, that Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners; of whom I am chief.*

*Let nothing be done through strife or vainglory; but in lowliness of mind let each esteem other better than themselves.*

*For I say, through the grace given unto me, to every man that is among you, not to think of himself more highly than he ought to think; but to think soberly, according as God hath dealt to every man the measure of faith.*

*Who art thou that judgest another man's servant? to his own master he standeth or falleth. Yea, he shall be holden up: for God is able to make him stand.

For none of us liveth to himself, and no man dieth to himself. For whether we live, we live unto the Lord; and whether we die, we die unto the Lord: whether we live therefore, or die, we are the Lord's. For to this end Christ both died, and rose, and revived, that he might be Lord both of the dead and living. But why dost thou judge thy brother? or why dost thou set at nought thy brother? for we shall all stand before the judgment seat of Christ. For it is written, As I live, saith the Lord, every knee shall bow to me, and every tongue shall confess to God. So then every one of us shall give account of himself to God. Let us not therefore judge one another any more: but judge this rather, that no man put a stumblingblock or an occasion to fall in his brother's way. I know, and am persuaded by the Lord Jesus, that there is nothing unclean of itself: but to him that esteemeth any thing to be unclean, to him it is unclean.

Let not then your good be evil spoken of.*

teachings.title: Repentance and the gospel: not "of your sins"
teachings.summary: Argues that adding "of your sins" to repent changes the gospel, and that biblical repentance is a change of heart toward believing God for salvation by grace through faith.
teachings.text:
Generally when the doctrine of repentance comes up, we think of false prophets like Ray Comfort, or John Macarthur, Lordshippers and others who add the teaching of works to justification by faith. 

These vipers are neo-Catholics who deny the glory of God revealed in our redemption, found only in His grace and by the blood of Christ, eternal life in His resurrection, reconciliation and forgiveness, adoption into the kingdom. Heirs to the promise.

They add works of the law to justification and keep people in perpetual doubt of if they are truly saved. It is a means of control and it denies the liberty found in the Lord Jesus. 

There are others, many well meaning believers, who have been raised with false Bible versions, or taught by honest pastors misled by Bible college or extrabiblical reading, into appending "...of your sins" to the word repent. 

This phrase never appears in scripture. 

And, in my experience, these people are straining at a rhetorical gnat and swallowing a camel, by trying to square their trust in salvation by grace through faith, with a vain tradition. They create a semantic trap for themselves, to the detriment of the Gospel. 

They will say that repent of sins actually just means acknowledging you're a sinner **which is** part of biblical repentance. If we can't acknowledge we're sinners in need of salvation, how in the world could we accept the free gift of it?

And God's not going to quibble with them over their misunderstanding of the term or use of it. 

Brothers shouldn't fight each other over pedantic semantics. 

However, the danger of being trapped in that snare of allowing the preaching of men to autocomplete a biblical phrase with something that doesn't appear in the text, comes when you're giving people the gospel. It's sows confusion, and here is how. 

Let's just say someone approaches you online or in real life and says that they are heartbroken. They feel worthless and trapped in sin. They have an addiction or are in a position where they can't break free. They know they are damned, know God is real and have a head knowledge that Jesus might be the answer they are seeking, because the Spirit is working in them. 

And they desperately need help. 

And one comes to them and says, that all have sinned and fallen short of the glory of God, there are none righteous. That we're all sinners, deserving death and hell, the good news is Jesus paid that price for us and we only have to believe on Him and be saved. That while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us. That we may have peace with God through His son, with the eternal security that, even though we may sin in the flesh, we are sealed by the Spirit unto the day of redemption.

(This obviously is an abridged version of the Roman's road, where we show them from scripture all of these points because faith cometh by hearing and hearing by the word of God, I am summarizing because I am writing to those who have accepted this all to be true and called upon the name of the Lord, Jesus Christ, that they may be healed.)

And say another says to them repent of your sins and believe on the Lord Jesus Christ and thou shall be saved. 

The first example is using scripture that is very specific of what you need to believe, to repent towards, that they may be saved. It is good news. They feel trapped and unworthy. They are told that, just as they are God will forgive them in Christ. That none are worthy but God so loved us that He gave His only begotten Son. Leading them to say "Lord, have mercy on me, a sinner," and believe that in Jesus name they are forgiven. 

Jesus said our mission statement as Christians is to preach this good news to every creature. 

*The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he hath anointed me to preach the gospel to the poor; he hath sent me to heal the brokenhearted, to preach deliverance to the captives, and recovering of sight to the blind, to set at liberty them that are bruised*.

The second, even if they are well meaning and have the best of intentions to win these people to Christ, actually create more of a problem, because to the unsaved they only hear the first part and see it as the very obstacle they already told you they are struggling with. 

"I have to repent of my sins? What does that mean? Turn from my sins? Which ones? All of them? What if I can't? What if I relapse? What about things I didn't know were sins? Does it just mean willing to give up sin? I wish I could!"

It is bad news. We need Jesus because we are broken. Even the unregenerate man regrets their sin and dreads the looming punishment for it. How does telling them to turn from the sin they are trapped in in order to believe and be saved, save anyone? 

And even if you're saved by faith, if you give this as your gospel, You're going to have people who could have been saved, who desperately needed to hear the truth, discouraged and turned away. 

They may as well have gone to Ray Comfort for the gospel. Gene Kim. Some other reprobate. The Catholic Church. 

We don't get healed that we can come to Christ. We come to Christ so that we may be healed. 

*Sirs, what must I do to be saved?

Believe on the Lord Jesus Christ, and thou shalt be saved*.

I've done it before in past channels and it may have migrated its way to here, but I have literally gone over every single appearance of repentance in the Bible or any deviation thereof, and shown systematically what is being repented from and towards in each case.

This isn't some new doctrine found only in YouTube. This isn't some apostasy that came about in the last century. 

This is the gospel of God as it's taught in the Bible. 

While there may be secondary or tertiary doctrines that you don't like about certain preachers or pastors or soul winners or evangelists or any other saved Christian under the sun who's been saved by grace through faith, or if you've had personality conflicts or past experiences that traumatized you or any other thing other than biblical truth that leads you to doubt that repentance is a change of heart towards believing God that one might be saved in Christ, pray on it. That God may remove the thorns from your heart, so that you may be in better service to Hm and giving the gospel to others. 

Stop slandering people who have successfully and consistently given the gospel and gotten thousands of people saved.

teachings.title: The burnt offering: free will and substitution
teachings.summary: The burnt offering was offered by a man's own voluntary will as a substitute for his sin, refuting Calvinism and the Orthodox and Catholic errors on atonement.
teachings.text:
**Leviticus 1:3-4**
*If his offering be a burnt sacrifice of the herd, let him offer a male without blemish: he shall offer it of his own voluntary will at the door of the tabernacle of the congregation before the Lord. And he shall put his hand upon the head of the burnt offering; and it shall be accepted for him to make atonement for him.*

Just to review something I meant to point out yesterday; note that the burnt offering is both of a man's own free will, and is an offering for substitutionary atonement.

Not a man chosen before time by God. Not some elect men, who are drawn and compelled to offer it. But by his own voluntary will.

And this offering was in his place for the payment of sin. It was the faith in God that held the remission of sin, the blood and the fire that was a picture of that faith, showing the pattern of things in Heaven.

This is yet another blow to Calvinism and to the damnable heresy taught by the Orthodox Church that there is no substitutionary atonement with Christ, and the strange and contradictory attempt by the Roman Catholics to square vicarious penal atonement, which is the Biblical doctrine as we see reflected in Leviticus, and their own existing heresies, mainly from Augustine and his progeny.

Jesus, the lamb without blemish, sacrificed for our sins. A propitiation that takes away the sin of all who voluntarily trust on Him for our salvation.

teachings.title: Mark them which cause divisions
teachings.summary: God has marked reprobates in two clear ways, being sodomites or false teachers who usurp the Gospel for gain and lead others astray, and believers are commanded to mark and avoid them rather than dismiss these warnings.
teachings.text:
The eternal salute of these saints in Christ, who Paul calls fellow laborers in the preserved word of God is a mighty honor. Their qualities of faith and work towards the ministry of the Gospel are an example we should strive for.

Paul, having called out those he sought to honor to the churches in Rome, can't help but add more doctrine to what has been a master class of Christian theology.

Mark them which cause divisions. Who are teaching contrary to the doctrines they have learned. We have learned the same, being blessed by scripture. Then this command is for us as well. We should mark them and avoid them.

*For they that are such serve not our Lord Jesus Christ, but their own belly; and by good words and fair speeches deceive the hearts of the simple.*

A major theme to the epistles is warning against false prophets and those bringing in damnable heresy, and what is consistently noted is their tendency to be in it for filthy lucre sake. As Jesus said in **Matthew 23**;

*Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye devour widows' houses, and for a pretence make long prayer: therefore ye shall receive the greater damnation.*

Or Paul writing in **2 Timothy 3**;

*For of this sort are they which creep into houses, and lead captive silly women laden with sins, led away with divers lusts, Ever learning, and never able to come to the knowledge of the truth.*

False teachers are vipers. Reprobates. Dogs. Swine. **Never** able to come to the knowledge of the truth. Starting with warnings about reprobates, Paul finishes on the same topic from a different angle, and understanding that God has marked the reprobate in two distinct and clear ways that man may know who they are; if they are sodomites or false teachers (often both) who usurp the authority of the Gospel to promote damnable heresy and lead others astray, they are all together corrupt.

This isn't someone who is wrong on some secondary or tertiary doctrine. Or someone who disagrees with you about some verse meaning or whatever. It isn't an unsaved person who doesn't understand the Gospel.

This is the curse of those who turn the truth of God into a lie. Who hold the truth in unrighteousness. Who knowingly subvert and undermine churches for their own pleasure, recognition or wealth, passing themselves off as men of God.

**Jude 10-13**
*But these speak evil of those things which they know not: but what they know naturally, as brute beasts, in those things they corrupt themselves. Woe unto them! for they have gone in the way of Cain, and ran greedily after the error of Balaam for reward, and perished in the gainsaying of Core. These are spots in your feasts of charity, when they feast with you, feeding themselves without fear: clouds they are without water, carried about of winds; trees whose fruit withereth, without fruit, twice dead, plucked up by the roots; Raging waves of the sea, foaming out their own shame; wandering stars, to whom is reserved the blackness of darkness for ever.*

Some people think that many who preach the Reprobate Doctrine spend too much time on it, or consider it wrong to make assumptions about people's status as a saved Christian, or not. And generally speaking, we should give a professing brother or sister the benefit of the doubt. Carefully and with love correcting them from scripture if they stray. If it is a minor thing, like in Romans 14, we should ignore it and humor them in it that we not lead them to sin.

Given that context, and the understanding that, despite that understanding, the holy Spirit has inspired verse after verse, chapter after chapter, from multiple writers, over and over again in the New Testament, giving these warnings and how to recognize them. It is clearly for our edification. Those that reject it do so at their peril.

teachings.title: A zeal of God, but not according to knowledge
teachings.summary: Like Israel, zealous Catholics, Orthodox, Lordshippers and repent-of-sins preachers set up their own righteousness, but Christ is the end of the law for righteousness to believers.
teachings.text:
Following the end of the argument regarding Israel after the flesh and the utter rejection of the idea that they are saved by their kinship to Abraham in chapter 9, Paul begins chapter 10 of Romans by lamenting this sad fact; that his own people, Israel after the flesh have shut themselves out of the kingdom by seeking their own righteousness by works of the law rather than the righteousness of God by faith.

*Brethren, my heart's desire and prayer to God for Israel is, that they might be saved. For I bear them record that they have a zeal of God, but not according to knowledge.*

This same prayer and sad refrain, a testimony of ignorant zeal that is preventing those trusting in their works from obeying the law of faith, could apply to so many zealous Catholics and Orthodox, Lordshippers and Repent-of-your-sins types. Those who place their works, their turning from sin, pursuit of their own righteousness to be made worthy, rather than the humility to understand that none are righteous, that they may obtain God's grace and mercy through faith. They have a zeal for God, but go about to set up their own righteousness to their destruction. Just like Israel after the flesh.

*For Christ is the end of the law for righteousness to every one that believeth.*

They lack the understanding that by the end of the law for righteousness, actually establishes the law. **Romans 3**:

*Do we then make void the law through faith? God forbid: yea, we establish the law.*

God's judgment reveals His holy righteousness through His mercy and His wrath. His law is the instrument by which we understand it, and our failings and the need for salvation by grace through faith. And by submission to the righteousness of God, we become able to truly fulfill the law. Without the spectre of death and hell, but rather with charity and love through faith.

teachings.title: The children of the flesh are not the children of God
teachings.summary: Romans 9 shows Israel after the flesh is cut off and the election is of the seed, Christ, not individual Calvinist election, and God has mercy on whom He will.
teachings.text:
Having established all things regarding salvation by faith, and the implications to man: believers unto righteousness found in Christ Jesus, the new man, the Spirit, and the promise of the incorruptible that comes at the redemption (as well as the sin of the flesh in the meantime), unbelief unto death, and reprobates, twice-dead, hearts hardened, Paul now moves on to addressing the Jews after the flesh, considering these settled arguments from before.

If all these things are true, and the gospel is by faith in Christ, which the prophets who came before all testified, and the law was unto death (not because of the unrighteousness of the law, but rather the infirmities of the people), and if all are under sin, Jew or Gentile, and all require faith in Christ to be saved, for there is no difference, what then?

Paul begins by expressing his sorrow that his kinsmen, the unbelieving children of Israel after the flesh are cut off. That they have had the Kingdom taken from them, as Jesus said.

*Israelites; to whom pertaineth the adoption, and the glory, and the covenants, and the giving of the law, and the service of God, and the promises; Whose are the fathers, and of whom as concerning the flesh Christ came, who is over all, God blessed for ever. Amen.*

All of these blessings, and the seed pertaining to the promise that is Christ Jesus (concerning the flesh, note the distinction, especially those "mother of God" heretics), and yet Israel are cut off.

*They which are the children of the flesh, these are not the children of God*.

(Dispensationalists should read that again and again until it sinks in)

...*but the children of the promise are counted for the seed. For this is the word of promise, At this time will I come, and Sarah shall have a son. And not only this; but when Rebecca also had conceived by one, even by our father Isaac*.

The promise was of the seed, the seed being Christ in the flesh, who came of the line of Jacob, born second but given the inheritance and the blessing over Esau.

**Malachi 1:2-3**
*I have loved you, saith the Lord. Yet ye say, Wherein hast thou loved us? Was not Esau Jacob's brother? saith the Lord: yet I loved Jacob, And I hated Esau, and laid his mountains and his heritage waste for the dragons of the wilderness.*

This is pertaining to the seed, the promise of Christ, knowing Edom would be made desolate, the election is of Jacob/Israel, that Jesus would come from Judah, the root of Jesse, from the throne of David.

This is not about individual salvation of Esau or Jacob. The election of the seed is in Christ. And it served God that the older served the younger in the promise,  in the same way that the Jew made way for the Gentile.

But the law says the older shall have the inheritance, so what then, is God unrighteous?

*God forbid. For he saith to Moses, I will have mercy on whom I will have mercy, and I will have compassion on whom I will have compassion.*

We trust the judgment of God. Who knows beginning from end. That all are chosen in Christ, not unto belief. Not given faith by God, but predestined in Christ to be given the blessing, the promise and the inheritance, to all who believe.

And so God, in His wisdom, shows mercy to who He will show mercy. And compassion on whom He will.

And harden the hearts of those fitted for destruction. All to His glory. Because as we have established; the righteousness of God is revealed both in His mercy towards us, and the love that gave His only begotten Son for us, but in His wrath against those who hold the truth in unrighteousness.

teachings.title: Shall we continue in sin
teachings.summary: Grace is no license to sin; baptism pictures our death with Christ so we should walk in newness of life, though holiness is not automatic as Lordshippers imply.
teachings.text:
**Romans 6** builds on the conclusion of the doctrine of the law of grace, and the implications for that liberty which we have in Christ. That we are no longer dead in sin with the judgment against us in unrighteousness, but born again a new man in the imputed righteousness of Jesus Christ.

Having proven this, that we are justified before God by faith, and standfast in His grace, what then?

Shall we sin that grace may abound? If it glorified God to be forgiven our sin, would it be to His glory that we sin all the more? (Again, as some slanderously reported about the apostles, and those who continue this smear today, calling the glory of God "cheap grace" and "a license to sin")

Again, *God forbid. How should we, that are dead to sin, love any longer therein?*

We are free, in Christ, that when we are baptized as believers, it is into death with Christ, just as when we rise up from the water, it is a picture of our rising with Him into eternal life.

Even so, we should walk in newness of life.

If we are picturing the image of Christ in our baptism, death, burial and resurrection, then our old man, our sinful nature after the flesh should be considered nailed to the cross with Him. *That the body of sin might be destroyed.*

Being dead in Christ we are risen with Him, and risen, death has no more dominion over Him, or us through Him. We are dead to sin but alive unto God through Jesus Christ our Lord. Paul is really hammering this point home because it is not automatic that we who are saved turn from our sins. That the new man's presence doesn't preclude the old man's lusts of the flesh from warring in our members. Our eyes and tongue betray us. Our feet are swift to sin.

If we automatically became holy by our salvation, this wouldn't have to be taught us, and it wouldn't be given us as a reminder in nearly every epistle. If we were given to "show fruit" to prove we are saved, as Lordshippers and other hypocrites suggest, it wouldn't be necessary to explain the old man vs the new.

teachings.title: Justified before God and before men
teachings.summary: Paul speaks of justification before God by faith and James of justification before men by works, so there is no contradiction and James 2 does not teach a works gospel.
teachings.text:
Abraham is the example Paul uses, given us in scripture as a lesson in justification by faith to God, by grace not of debt. That the glory in our salvation is God's alone.

But what about before other men?

A man may say that faith without works is dead, being alone. That, to men, justification isn't seen of faith but by a man's works.

**James 2:18-23**
*Yea, a man may say, Thou hast faith, and I have works: shew me thy faith without thy works, and I will shew thee my faith by my works. Thou believest that there is one God; thou doest well: the devils also believe, and tremble. But wilt thou know, O vain man, that faith without works is dead? Was not Abraham our father justified by works, when he had offered Isaac his son upon the altar? Seest thou how faith wrought with his works, and by works was faith made perfect? And the scripture was fulfilled which saith, Abraham believed God, and it was imputed unto him for righteousness: and he was called the Friend of God.*

*A man may say...* The overlooked predicate for the argument James makes in his epistle, written to brethren, the saved, to encourage them to good works. A man may say that Abraham's faith was shown in his works and thus he was justified to others.

But we know that scripture says it was faith that justified Abraham to God.

*For if Abraham were justified by works, he hath whereof to glory; but not before God. For what saith the scripture? Abraham believed God, and it was counted unto him for righteousness.*

By comparing scripture with scripture we see that there is no contradiction, only context. That Paul is writing of justification before God in grace, while James is writing of justification before man, by doing good works in faith.

The rhetorical question asked by a rhetorical man, "Was not Abraham justified by works?" is answered by the holy Spirit in **Romans 4** and **Genesis 15**. Not before God, or he would have to glory. The boasting wouldn't be excluded. The law of grace would become one of debt.

The misuse of **James 2** to teach a false gospel of works is one of the great stumbling blocks to salvation and faith. But by comparison, context and understanding we see that there is no contradiction found, anywhere in the Bible.

teachings.title: Tares among the wheat
teachings.summary: A professed ex-sodomite who claims salvation by repenting of sin is a red flag, since Jesus, Peter and Jude all teach that reprobates creep into churches as tares among the wheat and can be known by their traits.
teachings.text:
"But this guy came to our church saying he was a sodomite for years and repented of it so he's saved!"

Repentance of sin isn't how we are saved. It is by faith alone. Right away it is a red flag, or should be.

**Matthew 13:24-30**
*Another parable put he forth unto them, saying, The kingdom of heaven is likened unto a man which sowed good seed in his field: But while men slept, his enemy came and sowed tares among the wheat, and went his way. But when the blade was sprung up, and brought forth fruit, then appeared the tares also. So the servants of the householder came and said unto him, Sir, didst not thou sow good seed in thy field? from whence then hath it tares? He said unto them, An enemy hath done this. The servants said unto him, Wilt thou then that we go and gather them up? But he said, Nay; lest while ye gather up the tares, ye root up also the wheat with them. Let both grow together until the harvest: and in the time of harvest I will say to the reapers, Gather ye together first the tares, and bind them in bundles to burn them: but gather the wheat into my barn.*

The tares, or weeds that resemble wheat but produce no fruit, Jesus warned they would be sown among believers.

Peter writes of reprobates coming in to churches, **2 Peter 2**, he preaches hard against them, calling them *natural brute beasts, made to be taken and destroyed, speak evil of the things that they understand not; and shall utterly perish in their own corruption; and shall receive the reward of unrighteousness.*

These are the tares among the wheat. This is the reprobate doctrine, and the warning that they shall creep in unawares, and sow discord and lead many astray.

**2 Peter 2:17-22**
*These are wells without water, clouds that are carried with a tempest; to whom the mist of darkness is reserved for ever. For when they speak great swelling words of vanity, they allure through the lusts of the flesh, through much wantonness, those that were clean escaped from them who live in error. While they promise them liberty, they themselves are the servants of corruption: for of whom a man is overcome, of the same is he brought in bondage. For if after they have escaped the pollutions of the world through the knowledge of the Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ, they are again entangled therein, and overcome, the latter end is worse with them than the beginning. For it had been better for them not to have known the way of righteousness, than, after they have known it, to turn from the holy commandment delivered unto them. But it is happened unto them according to the true proverb, The dog is turned to his own vomit again; and the sow that was washed to her wallowing in the mire.*

Peter is teaching the same Reprobate Doctrine as Paul.

And Jude;

*Beloved, when I gave all diligence to write unto you of the common salvation, it was needful for me to write unto you, and exhort you that ye should earnestly contend for the faith which was once delivered unto the saints. For there are certain men crept in unawares, who were before of old ordained to this condemnation, ungodly men, turning the grace of our God into lasciviousness, and denying the only Lord God, and our Lord Jesus Christ. I will therefore put you in remembrance, though ye once knew this, how that the Lord, having saved the people out of the land of Egypt, afterward destroyed them that believed not. And the angels which kept not their first estate, but left their own habitation, he hath reserved in everlasting chains under darkness unto the judgment of the great day. Even as Sodom and Gomorrha, and the cities about them in like manner, giving themselves over to fornication, and going after strange flesh, are set forth for an example, suffering the vengeance of eternal fire. Likewise also these filthy dreamers defile the flesh, despise dominion, and speak evil of dignities...*

Jude also provides a list of traits that you might know them, similar to Paul's in **Romans 1**:

teachings.title: The epistles are written to the saved
teachings.summary: Paul writes as one saved to fellow saints, so the epistles are to the saved, and false churches that call assurance the sin of presumption have another gospel.
teachings.text:
Continuing Romans 1, Paul having introduced himself by his relationship to God through Christ, and stipulating the faith shared by believers unto salvation, he addresses the Roman saints, thanking God through Christ (our prayers to the Father are in the name of the Son), that the Roman churches are world famous for their faith. That Paul prays for them and to be among them, without ceasing. (Note this isn't in vain repetition. It just is his saying it is frequently an ask he makes)

Paul says that he, as a servant to the gospel, the shared faith he previously stipulated, and as a minister to it, that he serves God with his spirit in the gospel of the Son, and calls God to witness his sincerity to the readers. This is a letter, and Paul wishes to convey earnestness that may not be discerned from text alone.

Paul's prayer is by the will of God he may have a safe and prosperous journey to them. All prayer should be to the understanding that God's will be done.

Paul himself longs to see them, that he may impart unto them some spiritual gift, that he may be used of God to be a blessing, or to edify the brethren there. And that he himself would be blessed, given comfort being with them by the mutual faith they share.

This is important to understand, it is why Paul began his letter this way, emphasizing what that faith is, in Whom, to what end, and that it is what joins him to these strangers half a continent away.

All epistles are written to the saved. They follow the Gospels in the Bible, because it is understood that by the testimony of them we would come to believe and accept the gift of salvation, eternal life in Christ Jesus, given by God's grace.

Most apostate religions claiming Christianity as their source, frame the epistles as written to the world in general. Not to the saved, because they teach that man can never know if they are saved or not. Because they teach works-based justification, they have another gospel.

But as Paul says here, *that I may be comforted together with you by the mutual faith both of you and me.* Paul is clearly saved, he is writing to brethren of their shared faith. They are saints. Forgiven in Christ. Just as we are saints today, if we've been born again in faith.

The naysayers today in the false apostate churches would charge Paul with the "sin of presumption," for assuming he is saved, let alone assuming others are.

Paul continues, writing that he intended to come to them in the past, but was "let hitherto," led to where he is now at that writing. He intended to come to Rome before, (and God will grant him this soon enough, though not as Paul might think, but rather as a prisoner for the faith), that he could bear fruit in the city that is the seat of power for the empire. That he could get people saved by the Gospel, even as he has among the other Gentiles, the other nations of Asia Minor where he had traveled.

He says he is a debtor to the Greeks and Barbarians, that is the people of the empire, of Macedonia, and to the nations considered barbarians, not of the formal Greco-Roman people, and to both the wise and unwise, the civilized and educated and the simple peasants, all of whom Paul has had great success in bringing to Christ. This has him excited to preach the same Gospel in Rome, to win souls.

It is here, Paul having established all these things, reemphasizes once again the Gospel he is a servant to, that he begins to transition from introduction and stipulations to the meat of the arguments he, in the Spirit, will make.

*For I am not ashamed of the gospel of Christ: for it is the power of God unto salvation to every one that believeth*.

The power of God unto salvation comes from the Gospel. The Gospel is as he has stipulated, that God the Father gave us His Son, who died and rose again, to fulfill the scriptures, given by the prophets, wherein He promised a redeemer. Faith comes by hearing the word of God. The preaching of the Gospel is being a servant of the Lord.

teachings.title: Study to shew thyself approved
teachings.summary: Paul's writings are scripture that the unlearned wrest to their destruction, so believers must study and rightly divide the word, comparing scripture with scripture, to guard against false doctrine.
teachings.text:
You can see how Paul builds an argument block by block, in one long thought that establishes the foundation of the idea he wants to convey. It is careful and methodical and of the Spirit in its simplicity, but confounding those who don't believe with its dense structure, making his writings a snare for those who don't actually hold the faith that he uses as the foundations for his epistles. Something that Peter addresses in his own epistle to the churches of Asia:

**2 Peter 3:13-17**
*Nevertheless we, according to his promise, look for new heavens and a new earth, wherein dwelleth righteousness. Wherefore, beloved, seeing that ye look for such things, be diligent that ye may be found of him in peace, without spot, and blameless. And account that the longsuffering of our Lord is salvation; even as our beloved brother Paul also according to the wisdom given unto him hath written unto you; As also in all his epistles, speaking in them of these things; in which are some things hard to be understood, which they that are unlearned and unstable wrest, as they do also the other scriptures, unto their own destruction.Ye therefore, beloved, seeing ye know these things before, beware lest ye also, being led away with the error of the wicked, fall from your own stedfastness.*

Peter both acknowledges Paul's standing as an Apostle, his writings as scripture, and that what he writes confounds the unlearned and unstable, the babe in Christ or the unbelieving. Peter appeals to them, saying since they have the faith, they should beware being taken by those who wrest with scripture out of ignorance or unbelief, by false doctrines pulled from the complexity of Paul's writings, as well as scripture in general.
