teachings.summary: Goes through the verses on repentance in the Gospels and Acts, noting beside each that it means to change mind and believe. Concludes that all of them say to repent and believe on Jesus Christ for remission of sins.
teachings.text:
**Mark 1: 14-15**
*Now after that John was put in prison, Jesus came into Galilee, preaching the gospel of the kingdom of God, And saying, The time is fulfilled, and the kingdom of God is at hand: repent ye, and believe the gospel.*

Change mind, believe

**Matthew 4:17**
*From that time Jesus began to preach, and to say, Repent: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand*.
- Change mind, believe (same context as Mark)

**Matthew 9: 12-13**
*But when Jesus heard that, he said unto them, They that be whole need not a physician, but they that are sick. But go ye and learn what that meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice: for I am not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.*
-All are sinners, being called to believe 

**Matthew 11: 20-21**
*Then began he to upbraid the cities wherein most of his mighty works were done, because they repented not:

Woe unto thee, Chorazin! woe unto thee, Bethsaida! for if the mighty works, which were done in you, had been done in Tyre and Sidon, they would have repented long ago in sackcloth and ashes.*

-They didn't believe even with the signs and miracles Jesus did. Even these notorious cities of the wicked would not only have believed, but done so with penance. In addition to believing. 
-Parallel verse Luke 10: 13


**Matthew 12: 41**
*The men of Nineveh shall rise in judgment with this generation, and shall condemn it: because they repented at the preaching of Jonas; and, behold, a greater than Jonas is here.*

- As we've already seen in **Jonah 3:10**, this is physical salvation from God's wrath, which God repents of, *seeing their works *of turning from sin. 
- Parallel passage Luke 11: 32

**Matthew 21: 32**
*For John came unto you in the way of righteousness, and ye believed him not: but the publicans and the harlots believed him: and ye, when ye had seen it, repented not afterward, that ye might believe him.*
-Change mind/believe

**Mark 2: 17**
*When Jesus heard it, he saith unto them, They that are whole have no need of the physician, but they that are sick: I came not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.*
- Change mind/believe (righteous don't need to change their mind and believe, but all sinners do)
- Parallel passage **Luke 5: 32**

**Luke 13: 1-5**
- covered in earlier post - they believe some who had died from evil deserved it due to their being greater sinners than those asking Jesus. Holier than thous are just as damned as those men unless they repent/believe 

**Luke 16:27-31**
*Then he said, I pray thee therefore, father, that thou wouldest send him to my father's house: For I have five brethren; that he may testify unto them, lest they also come into this place of torment. Abraham saith unto him, They have Moses and the prophets; let them hear them.
And he said, Nay, father Abraham: but if one went unto them from the dead, they will repent. And he said unto him, If they hear not Moses and the prophets, neither will they be persuaded, though one rose from the dead.*
- Change mind/believe, talks about Lazarus testifying, of persuasion, hearing not the prophets

**Luke 24:46-47**
*And said unto them, Thus it is written, and thus it behooved Christ to suffer, and to rise from the dead the third day: And that repentance and remission of sins should be preached in his name among all nations, beginning at Jerusalem.*
- Change mind/believe, which is how remission of sins is received (note two separate things being preached)

**Matthew 3: 1-3**
- parallel passage **Mark 1:14-15**

**Acts 20: 20-21**
*And how I kept back nothing that was profitable unto you, but have shewed you, and have taught you publicly, and from house to house, Testifying both to the Jews, and also to the Greeks, repentance toward God, and faith toward our Lord Jesus Christ.*
- Change of mind/believe, testimony 
- shows that faith towards=repentance towards 

**Acts:17:29-30**

*Forasmuch then as we are the offspring of God, we ought not to think that the Godhead is like unto gold, or silver, or stone, graven by art and man's device.***
***And the times of this ignorance God winked at; but now commandeth all men every where to repent: *
- Change mind/believe, 
- literally changing mind of the ignorance which God had winked at, repent of afore described ignorance of believing in idols

**Acts 26:17-19**
*Delivering thee from the people, and from the Gentiles, unto whom now I send thee, To open their eyes, and to turn them from darkness to light, and from the power of Satan unto God, that they may receive forgiveness of sins, and inheritance among them which are sanctified by faith that is in me. Whereupon, O king Agrippa, I was not disobedient unto the heavenly vision:*
- change mind/believe, turn to light from dark

Acts 2 deserves its own post(I have made a post on it at least once)

There's more. They are all the same. 

Repent and believe on Jesus Christ for remission of sins, alone.

teachings.title: You cannot be saved by repenting of sin
teachings.summary: Argues from 1 John 3:4, Jonah 3:10 and Romans 3 that turning from sin is a work and so cannot save, and that biblical repentance is a change of mind toward God and belief. Adds that a saved person should still turn from sin out of love for God, which is not repenting of sin to be saved.
teachings.text:
Periodic reminder that you cannot be saved, you cannot be justified in the sight of God, you cannot receive the gift of eternal life, through "repenting of sin."

The Bible says sin is the transgression of the law (1 John 3:4 - *Whosoever committeth sin transgresseth also the law: for sin is the transgression of the law.)*.

The Bible says turning from sin is a work. (Jonah 3:10 - *And God saw their works, that they turned from their evil way; and God repented of the evil, that he had said that he would do unto them; and he did it not.)
*
And we know the Bible says salvation is not of works, least any man should boast. That if sin is transgression of the law, and turning from wicked deeds a work, then adherence to the law is a work of the law, by which no one can be saved.  

This is made clear, in no uncertain terms, in Romans 3: 

*Therefore by the deeds of the law there shall no flesh be justified in his sight: for by the law is the knowledge of sin.

But now the righteousness of God without the law is manifested, being witnessed by the law and the prophets; Even the righteousness of God which is by faith of Jesus Christ unto all and upon all them that believe: for there is no difference: For all have sinned, and come short of the glory of God; Being justified freely by his grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus:

Whom God hath set forth to be a propitiation through faith in his blood, to declare his righteousness for the remission of sins that are past, through the forbearance of God; To declare, I say, at this time his righteousness: that he might be just, and the justifier of him which believeth in Jesus.

Where is boasting then? It is excluded. By what law? of works? Nay: but by the law of faith.

Therefore we conclude that a man is justified by faith without the deeds of the law.
*
Note that Biblical repentance is defined as turning from one thing, towards another, be it God repenting of punishment He intended to inflict on a people, Jews repenting of not believing Jesus was the Christ, or repenting of trusting in their dead works or Gentiles repenting of their faith in idols, repentance is always a turning towards a different belief or intent. 

The phrase "repent of sin" doesn't appear in scripture, nor does any similar implied doctrine regarding salvation. What we see over and over is belief, faith, that saved. What is mentioned is turning towards God and belief in His word, and away from whatever contradicts that word that one might believe in, in order to be saved.  

So, based on this, anyone telling you that you must repent of sin, turning from transgression of the law, in order to be saved is preaching a false gospel of works, and cheapening the gift of salvation given by God, paid for by Jesus precious blood, and adding to that perfect and priceless gift our own righteousness, what Paul calls "dung."

We must believe we are sinners in need of salvation to be saved. We must accept that God in His mercy, in grace, gave His Son Jesus Christ to suffer and die for all our sins, and that He rose Him from the dead, to show the promise of eternal life. This is the faith by which we are saved. 

If you are trusting in your ability to turn over a new leaf, to be reformed from sin, even your subjective "willingness" to "repent of sin", or anything else that you might do in order to be saved, other than believe, you're perishing. 

Jesus did it all. Paid it all. While we were yet sinners, we are redeemed in the blood. Clothed in white raiment, the imputed righteousness of Jesus Christ. 

Admitting you're a sinner isn't repentance, it's a humbling understanding that we cannot be holy or righteous on our own. The Bible says that the law is a schoolmaster to teach us this lesson. That God reveals it to us in our hearts, our conscience, so that no man has excuse. But this isn't repentance. 

The Bible says that having been saved, and free from the law, our sins erased and at liberty to do all things, even those that edify not, we still should turn from the sin that we did while perishing under the law. Should we continue in sin, God forbid. 

But this again isn't repenting of sin to be saved. It is turning from sin out of love for God.

teachings.title: Upon this rock: the confession of Christ
teachings.summary: The rock Christ builds His church on is the truth Peter confessed, that Jesus is the Christ the Son of God, not Peter himself, and believers are lively stones built on it.
teachings.text:
Next we see they've moved on, and having come to Philippi, Jesus is again teaching His Apostles, and begins asking "*Whom do men say that I the Son of man am?*"

The apostles say that the people say *He is John the Baptist: some, Elias; and others, Jeremias, or one of the prophets.* It is interesting that the popular consensus regarding Jesus was that he was first and foremost a hard preaching prophet. John the baptist, Elijah, and especially Jeremiah were known for their fire breathing preaching, condemning sin and wickedness of those around them.

Then Jesus asks, "*But whom say ye that I am*?" And Simon Peter, (*Thou art Simon the son of Jona: thou shalt be called Cephas, which is by interpretation, A stone*), answers, saying "*Thou art the Christ, the Son of the living God."*

To which Jesus responds; "*Blessed art thou, Simon Barjona: for flesh and blood hath not revealed it unto thee, but my Father which is in heaven. And I say also unto thee, That thou art Peter, and upon this rock I will build my church; and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it. And I will give unto thee the keys of the kingdom of heaven: and whatsoever thou shalt bind on earth shall be bound in heaven: and whatsoever thou shalt loose on earth shall be loosed in heaven.*"

Taken in context, we see that Jesus in confirming Peter's profession of faith, that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, that this truth revealed to Peter by God, and to all of us through His word and received by faith, is the rock upon which Jesus is building his church. His congregation of believers.

We see that Jesus originally calling him cephas or Peter, which translated means a stone, a chip of rock, is here paid off. A long setup punchline, used by Jesus to make a point regarding the gospel being **The Rock**, that the truth of Jesus being the long-awaited Christ is the cornerstone upon which the church is built. And we who believe, as Peter says in his Epistles, are as lively stones like him, making up the edification, the building up of the church, the congregation of which comes together on the day of the Lord.

We know that Jesus, upon his resurrection, had with him the keys to Hell and death. That rock, the truth of the Gospel, this spiritual bread, grants eternal life to those who believe. That the gospel itself is the key. That the truth of it is the rock.

And again these  things that are spiritually discerned, and twisted into perverse doctrines.

In the Catholic heresy, Peter becomes the rock, the church, an earthly institution built by men, the bread literal, and so literally flesh. The leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees added to the word, just as Christ warned.

teachings.title: Fruit of souls won, and false prophets who bear none
teachings.summary: Throughout the New Testament the work of believers is winning souls for God's increase, while false prophets with doctrines of works and philosophy cannot bring forth that fruit.
teachings.text:
Paul continues his greeting to the churches in Colosse, including a shout out to the early church in Laodicea, churches he himself didn't establish in person, as the Gospel has been preached throughout the world, faith to faith, to the Gentiles, beyond even Paul's direct ministry.

All believers, members of the body of which Jesus is the head, united in spirit, in the joy of peace with God through grace and faith, sharing the goal of bringing increase, the harvest of fruit of righteousness, winning souls to Christ with the Gospel of reconciliation. Bringing forth fruit meet for repentance. Turning those that heard and believe towards God.

We see in epistle after epistle, in the Acts of the apostles, in Jesus' own ministry, and His sending of disciples out, two by two into the highways and hedges. We see it in John the Baptist's preaching in the wilderness. It is faith shared and souls won. To God the increase.

The so called holy men, vipers chastised by John and Jesus Himself, Peter and Paul, were unable to bring forth this fruit, to lead believers to Christ.

Neither can false prophets, and yet they are here in Colosse as they were in Galatia, Ephesus, in the Judean wilderness, as Satan himself, trying to lead the churches astray, causing others to sin, and damning souls with their doctrines of works.

It's the same play as Satan in the desert with Christ. We see it today. They beguile us with enticing words, to *spoil you through philosophy and vain deceit, after the tradition of men, after the rudiments of the world, and not after Christ.*

teachings.title: John the Baptist and believer's baptism
teachings.summary: John baptized believers by immersion as the answer of a good conscience, not to wash away sin, and his hard preaching told the Pharisees that descent from Abraham would not save them.
teachings.text:
The prophet who comes before Christ. The voice crying out in the wilderness. Telling all men to turn towards God, that the Messiah is coming. John the Baptist.

Jesus cousin, raised by his righteous parents, bringing people to salvation and baptising believers, by immersion, in much water.

Baptism not being the putting away of sin, but the answer of a good conscience by those who have called upon the name of the Lord for forgiveness of sin and everlasting life. The same unbroken line of faith from John to modern, NT Christians. (Note it's not John the Catholic or John the Lutheran)

He eschews comfort. Eats ze bugs. And rips face with hard preaching. Matthew 3 captures a moment of John's style of fire-breathing, hellfire and damnation preaching, in this case against the Pharisees and Sadducees. The religious leaders of Judea, come down to be seen where the actions at. Maybe to be baptized to seem holy. But John calls them out.

*O generation of vipers, who hath warned you to flee from the wrath to come? Bring forth therefore fruits meet for repentance: And think not to say within yourselves, We have Abraham to our father: for I say unto you, that God is able of these stones to raise up children unto Abraham.And now also the axe is laid unto the root of the trees: therefore every tree which bringeth not forth good fruit is hewn down, and cast into the fire.*

Much as Jesus would later, as detailed in Matthew 7 and 23, he calls out these hypocrites, this generation of vipers, false preachers who bear bad fruit. Not souls won, ready to accept Christ. They bring forth no fruit, thistles. False prophets, which come to you in sheep's clothing, but inwardly they are ravening wolves.

Then he goes after their reliance on being special boys, born from Abraham, saying God could make a rock a son of Abraham. That their being Jews isn't going to save them. (RIP Dispensationalism).

He tells these reprobate hypocrites that Jesus who's coming, will sort them like chafe from wheat, into the fire. Cut down their tree, throw it in the fire. Brimstone-throwing preaching. Amen!

And Jesus, our Lord comes, whose shoes we aren't worthy to unlatch. And he goes down into the water, and straightway rises up out of the water with the Holy Ghost upon Him. And the blessing of the Father is given to the Son. Amen.

teachings.title: Sealed unto the day of redemption, against false churches
teachings.summary: Believers are sealed by the Spirit with eternal life, and churches teaching you can lose or must earn salvation, or that they are the body, are false churches that cannot save.
teachings.text:
Note the doctrines here, that unity of faith into the body, where Christ is the head. That we are sealed by the Spirit, given eternal life, testified by the new man within us, that we may know and have confidence in our trust in God. This is the promise of salvation.

Denominations that teach you can lose your salvation, that you must earn it, that only they can give it, that they are the head and the body, teaching the vanity of the mind and tossing their members to and fro with every changing wind of doctrine, rather than standing fast upon the unmoving rock of the Word...these false churches cannot save. They are the bondsmen, keeping people in chains.

teachings.title: No chosen people but in Christ
teachings.summary: Paul refutes the idea that Jews are God's chosen and Gentile believers lesser, there is only the one dispensation of grace, and Rome's sin of presumption keeps people from assurance.
teachings.text:
Again the focus of these first 3 chapters is attacking the idea that Jews are God's "chosen people," and that Gentile believers are somehow less-than in their inheritance. Paul puts this false notion to bed, emphatically. We are the second born who received the full inheritance and blessing. The Jews having sold it in their fornication for the pottage of earthly things.

Dispensationalists rely on the appearance of the word 'dispensation' in these passages, to justify their wicked heresy, while the text of it destroys them. There is only the dispensation of grace. The change is to extend it to all men, through Jesus Christ regardless of lineage.

There is no limit to the atonement, but the free will to believe the Gospel by those that receive it, and *In whom we have boldness and access with confidence by the faith of him.*

This destroys the damnable "mortal sin of presumption" made by the Catholic Church to snare the unsuspecting into never coming to salvation, and never having that confidence, put in bondage to dead works of the law, and reliant on the RCC to save them in the end. Sending millions to Hell.

teachings.title: All believers are saints
teachings.summary: Saint is the New Testament title for every believer, not a rank Rome bestows for works, and the peace announced at Christ's birth is peace between God and men through grace.
teachings.text:
Another point to make regarding the introduction, that Paul addresses to the saints and believers, terms which are interchangeable in the New Testament. All believers are saints. It's a title bestowed throughout to all who believe. It is not a select few whose Works were so good that they are honored here on Earth with the title. By making a church of man the arbiter, and basing it on works, the Catholic church has cheapened the term. I am a saint. If you believe you are a saint as well. Even if your backslidden, even if you need to turn from sins that are consuming your life. And as saints we should turn from sin, we should live a righteous life as possible. Live up to it.

Secondly Paul frequently writes that he prays for Grace from God to us the reader, and with that grace, peace.

The only piece we have with God is through his grace, and Christ Jesus. At the nativity the Angels announced peace on Earth. Goodwill towards men. This is a message from God to man, that he is granting them peace with Him, and goodwill through the birth of Jesus. The angel isn't saying that they'll be peace upon the Earth between men, but rather peace between God and men.

teachings.title: Tongues, prophecy and the preserved English word
teachings.summary: Tongues were languages and prophecy is preaching scripture to understanding, so services in a dead language, back-to-the-Greek scholars and Ruckmanites all err, and God has preserved His word in English in the KJV needing no outside interpreter.
teachings.text:
Paul continues his teaching to the Corinthians on spiritual gifts, having put in place the doctrine that we shouldn't covet and envy those who have received talents to the edification of the church that differ from ours, that all in the body serve the same head, that head being Jesus and through Him, the Father. Then making the case that being charitable, the love for others that God expressed to us, and Christ demonstrated on the cross, then we've a better gift than even those the Holy Ghost bestowed on many in this time. Specifically the ability to speak and understand foreign tongues, or languages.

The Bible is clear that this is the meaning. Not the nonsense gibberish of the pentecostal heathen. No where in the Bible does the term "speaking in tongues" exist (unless you read one of the perverted modern versions that sow false doctrine with confusion so often).

This gift is rather the use of those who can interpret or prophesy scripture to those who speak another tongue.

Like the Apostles and disciples on Pentecost, who spoke the Gospel to those pilgrims from all over the world, in Jerusalem for the feast. They spoke to understanding, and it amazed the crowd and acted as a sign, bringing thousands to belief as they heard the word of God in their native language.

Prophecy in the Bible is the preaching of scripture, and bringing the relevance of the word of God to the people. It is giving the Gospel to the unbelieving. It is teaching the law. It is relevant preaching to the building up of the church. It is the advice of proverbs taught at a mother's knee. It is the exhorting of the pulpit to the flock.

And if any of this be done in a language none of the hearers understand, as Paul says in chapter 13, it is of *sounding brass, or a tinkling cymbal.*

This goes for false religion that gives entire services in a dead language. It is to no one's edification but the speaker.

This goes for the "You must return to the Hebrew! You must return to the Greek! God's word is impossible to understand in English!" nonsense of puffed up "scholars" who take pride in their private interpretation and sowing confusion among the people to show how learned they are.

This goes to the Ruckmanites who take the preservation of the Word in the KJV to be a further revelation that is more perfect than the Greek and Hebrew, which is nonsense.

Paul says that if you have a gift of knowing a language that can be used for interpretation to the person being reached with the Gospel then use it, but not to show off to the believers who cannot understand it, which seems the case in Corinth.

As Pentecost showed us, God's word is powerful in any language, and in every tongue God, who is not the author of confusion can make His word known.

Verse 26 he wonders how it is so many in Corinth are puffed up by claims of their own doctrines and revelations and psalms, and strange tongues, etc. They apparently were many among them who, in covetousness and pride were deceitfully inventing whole doctrines and aping gifts they did not have, or bragging about gifts they were given and wasting them.

As for tongues, today we have the inspired Word of God, preserved by the Spirit, in English in the KJV. And we should be grateful that we need no one to tell us it's lingual meaning, as every word and term is defined in itself. There is no need to appeal to a concordance or other work of an unsaved man to explain to us the plain meaning of His scripture.

teachings.title: The spirit of the Lord's supper, not the flesh
teachings.summary: How often a church observes the Lord's supper matters less than the spirit of it, and treating the physical bread and wine as a source of grace, as Rome and her offshoots do, is eating damnation.
teachings.text:
How various NT churches decide to engage in a Lord's supper together is really not important, so much the spirit by which it is done. Some do it in honor of the day leading to His death burial and resurrection. Some do it weekly. Some do it every meal they have at church or at home. I tend towards that, at least in the blessing and remembrance.

What isn't good doctrine is placing more in the physical eating and drinking than the spiritual application. Or placing it as a source for grace and salvation. The Catholic version of this and the Protestant spin offs have at their heart the wrong motives spiritually, and so eat and drink damnation unto themselves.

As Jesus says in **John 6**, *It is the spirit that quickeneth; the flesh profiteth nothing: the words that I speak unto you, they are spirit, and they are life.*

Those that heard and didn't understand this were offended and many disciples left from following Christ, because they took spiritual things literally, just as the Jews condemned Him for these "dark sayings."

teachings.title: No real presence, only remembrance
teachings.summary: There is no sacrament in the Lord's supper; believers remember Christ and give thanks whenever they eat together, and transubstantiation and real presence are neither taught nor hinted at.
teachings.text:
BTW if I wasn't clear, there is no sacramental aspect to this, no Lord's supper as it were, it's the meals we have together with other believers we're to remember Jesus, with the breaking of the bread and the drinking of the juice of the vine, or anything else that we eat together.

The idea of a real presence, or the Hocus pocus of a transubstantiation, is neither implied nor even hinted at. When two or three are gathered together in his name Jesus is there. teachings.title: Luke 21 and the so-called three snares
teachings.summary: Answers a preacher's claim of a secret doctrine of three snares in Luke 21:34, showing that the snare in verse 35 refers back to the day of the Lord. Explains the order of events from Matthew 24, the signs, and why believers who watch will not be caught unawares.
teachings.text:
**Luke 21:33-36**

*33 Heaven and earth shall pass away: but my words shall not pass away.

34 And take heed to yourselves, lest at any time your hearts be overcharged with surfeiting, and drunkenness, and cares of this life, and so **that day** come upon you unawares.

35 For as **a snare** shall it come on all them that dwell on the face of the whole earth.

36 Watch ye therefore, and pray always, that ye may be accounted worthy to escape all these things that shall come to pass, and to stand before the Son of man.*

This caught my attention scrolling through Telegram, and because I wasn't certain what he was talking about by these so-called "three snares," I watched a little bit of the video. 

Wiles claims that Luke 21:34 seems as if it is a non sequitur, that Jesus in talking about the end times throws this bit about surfeiting, drunkenness and cares of this life in to his preaching, and that these are the secret "three snares" that all Christians must avoid if they want to go to heaven when Jesus' second coming is here. 

Rick Wiles and his co-host, Doc Burkhart further say they've never heard anyone else who claims to be an end times prophecy expert mention this doctrine Wiles "discovered." And they chastise viewers who don't "buy and read books" that could explain the "mysteries of Revelation" to them. He then hocks the second edition of his own book. 

That's all within the first 5 minutes. 

(Just to be clear for those wondering, surfeiting is a word that means being full of something that you've overindulged in)

When we turn to the actual chapter and verse in question, we see that the snare that is referred to in verse 35, refers back up to "that day," meaning the day of the Lord. The second coming, after the tribulation in those days, where the dead in Christ are risen and called up into the clouds, followed by the living who are saved at that time, caught up with Jesus, and the wrath of God begins being poured out for the next three and a half years. 

Jesus has just finished telling the apostles exactly the order of events, and how it will play out. We see the same account in Matthew 24. Jesus tells them, and us, that we will know that the time is growing close. We will see the signs. His coming will not be a surprise to those of us who are paying attention and who are studying his word and praying because all of those other things will have come to pass leading up to it. There are three and a half years of Great tribulation on Earth with the Antichrist and the persecution of the saints. He tells the parable of the fig tree, to draw a comparison to how you know what season it is based on these observations. Jesus warning about not being so full of the cares of this world, caught up and drunkenness, caught up in a form of worldly gluttony, so that we are able to pay attention to those signs and, that's not be caught unawares. Because it's to the unsaved that his coming will be like a thief in the night. That carnal Christians who are backslidden and not keeping their mind towards God, will also be taken by surprise, potentially.

Wiles turns this into some kind of weird works-based doctrine that if you're unhealthy, be it gluttony, drunk or a worry wart, you won't get saved when Jesus returns.

teachings.title: Pentecost tongues were real languages
teachings.summary: The Holy Ghost first indwelt believers when Christ breathed on them in John 20, and at Pentecost He filled them to preach the gospel in real foreign languages, not charismatic gibberish.
teachings.text:
Acts chapter 2 picks up now, 10 days after Jesus' ascension, the 120 disciples and Apostles gathered in church, waiting in Jerusalem as Jesus had instructed. As they waited, suddenly the great room they were in was filled with a rushing wind and flames of fire, filling those assembled with the Holy Ghost.

The traditional teaching of this chapter says that this is the first time the Holy Ghost is indwelling in believers, quickening their spirit the same way saved Christians experience today, calling upon the name of the Lord. It's often preached as "until Pentecost, no one had the indwelling of the Holy Ghost." The Bible says in the OT believers who called upon the name of the Lord and were saved by faith did not have the Holy Ghost permanently within them, but were often described as being filled with Him at times to do great feats, prophesy and preach, or be used in some way to the glory of God. I believe this is what's happening here, because in John 20:22 (which we just [read](https://t.me/HouseOfWews2/2295)), where risen Christ appears to them on Easter Sunday, the scripture says:

*And when he had said this, he breathed on them, and saith unto them, Receive ye the Holy Ghost.*

I believe this was when the Holy Ghost, the comforter and 3rd person of the triune Godhead, first indwelled in those who are quickened by faith, in God's grace.

I could be wrong but that's how it reads to me, otherwise John is contradicting Acts, impossible. Given the context of what happens next, I think my interpretation is correct.

Now, on the primary holy day of the feast of [Pentecost,](https://t.me/HouseOfWews2/2367) believing, practicing Jews from all over the world were required to make pilgrimage to Jerusalem and the temple for the feast of first fruits of the harvest, and the blood free will sacrifices of purification (Exodus 23:16, 34:22, Leviticus 23:16, Numbers 28:26).

The Bible says that these Jews came from every nation, and lists many of the nations in example. And as the 120, filled with the Spirit come out to the crowd this gathered, they begin to preach the Gospel to all, in their own languages. This miracle of God is astounding, as these faithful God-fearing people hear the good news of Jesus Christ in their native tongue.

Not the satanic gibberish of the Charismatics and so-called Pentecostals, but clear understandable language of those assembled there.

Not the mistaken doctrine that the disciples spoke Hebrew or Aramaic or Greek, and those assembled heard it in their own languages, but if speaking to a Mede or Libyan or whatever land the pilgrims were from, they were able to communicate the Gospel to them. How do we know this? By the reaction of the Jews from Jerusalem, who mocked what they heard as unintelligible chatter as their being drunken.

This is when Peter gives a blistering sermon addressed specifically to those mocking, and an indictment of the Jews of Judea.

Peter says obviously they aren't drunken, being only 9 in the morning, but that it's fulfilled prophecy. He then quotes Joel regarding how in the last days the sons and daughters will prophesy, and uses that verse to then lead them the further prophecy of Joel of the second coming of Christ.

Peter is not simply defending their speaking in tongues, but like Jesus did repeatedly in His ministry, Peter is using scripture they should be familiar with to bring them the Gospel. He quotes Joel 3's warning of what the day of the Lord will look like, and indicating to the crowd that it is all coming true. Warning them that if they are seeing sons and daughters with signs and wonders, preaching the word, maybe they should take heed of what the rest of scripture says. That "*Whosoever shall call on the name of the Lord shall be saved."*

This is the Gospel.

He continues, making clear precisely who Jesus is, what He did, that He did it among them as they well know, and that despite their knowledge they killed Christ. Peter lays the blame for this squarely on the Jews in Jerusalem.

teachings.title: Repent means a change of mind, not turning from sin
teachings.summary: Says repenting in relation to salvation is turning from a false belief to believing God's word, and that turning from sin is something everyone tries for many reasons, none of which save. Uses Jonah 3:10 to show God repented and the phrase repent of sin is not in the Bible.
teachings.text:
Repenting in relation to salvation is turning from a false belief in something to justify us before God, or turning from unbelief to believing His word. It's a changing of mind. I don't know anyone who is counting on their sin to justify them or bring them to righteousness, so repenting of sin in this context is foolish.  

Everyone, saved and unsaved feels regret and shame for their sin and, when conscious of it, tries to turn away from specific sins, whether through conscience sake, guilt, trying to work their way to self righteousness, trying to please others, to avoid punishment or consequences of their sin, etc ... 

The reprobate doesn't turn from sin out of guilt or to please God, but often will to avoid tradeoffs and mitigate consequences and risk. A reprobate may quit smoking, drinking, abstain from more vile affections for fear of jail. 

Everyone turns from sin at various points in their lives. 

We have things like New Years resolutions, diet and weight loss industry, screen time monitoring apps, aids to quit smoking, swear jars,  #NoNutNovember, appeals to "common decency," etc...all expressions of God's law written in our hearts bringing us to try and turn from the harmful and wicked things we do, for a variety of reasons and motives, selfish and selfless. 

None of that saves. 

Only faith in the risen Christ and belief in the promise of God that Jesus is the sole propitiation for all sin can save us.

*But if thine heart turn away, so that thou wilt not hear, but shalt be drawn away, and worship other gods, and serve them;
I denounce unto you this day, that ye shall surely perish, and that ye shall not prolong your days upon the land*

**Jonah 3:10**

 *And God saw their works, that they turned from their evil way; and God repented of the evil, that he had said that he would do unto them; and he did it not.*

Now this verse is not about spiritual salvation, it is about the physical salvation of the city of Nineveh who God had sent Jonah to be a prophet unto them and get them to repent of their wicked ways or he was going to destroy their city and kill all of them. Of course Jonah objects because they're not Israelites and he doesn't think that they deserve a warning then of course God corrects him on that but that's a story for a different time, what's interesting here is that we both see that repentance, or turning away from sin is viewed as a work by God, AND it shows that repenting cannot always mean "...of sin," because we see God who cannot sin repenting of the destruction he was going to visit on them having seen their good works 

So in one verse you have evidence that repenting of sin is a work, and that repentance does not always mean of sin, because God does it.

By the way this is the closest verse you can find in the Bible where repent of sin, or turning from evil ways, is mentioned. 

The phrase "repent of sin* doesn't appear anywhere in the Bible. And the concept relative to salvation appears nowhere in any of the Gospels or the Acts of Apostles or any of the Epistles. Where the term repent or even turn away, appear, it's always explicitly spelled out what they need to repent from, and turn towards believing God.

teachings.title: Repent in the KJV and the modern versions

teachings.text:

Curiously, it is fairly consistent when they choose to change scripture. The NIV and other other corrupt Bible transitions eliminate the 35 different times God is said to "repent" in scripture. Essentially removing from scripture the idea that God can repent. The only rationale one can draw from that is they know the idea of a sinless God repenting undermines their subversive, heretical claim that "repent" automatically means "turn from sin." They also remove other instances such as Exodus 13:17 and Matthew 27:3, which complicate the false works-based doctrine that they are trying to teach. 

It is impossible to come to any other conclusion than that is the agenda behind their selective censorship of the term from any instance that undermines their wicked doctrine.

*Sanctify the Lord God in your hearts: and be ready always to give an answer to every man that asketh you a reason of the hope that is in you with meekness and fear:*

teachings.title: No communion in John's gospel

teachings.text:

As we have said throughout the Gospel according to John, this is written specifically to the unsaved so that they may understand and come to salvation by faith. So it is important to recognize that there is no account of the breaking of bread and blessing of wine, which were symbols used to explain Jesus' coming trials and death in the other Gospel accounts.

If a ceremony of eating bread and drinking wine were necessary for salvation, it would be mentioned here. Of course if it were mentioned, it would contradict the entire message of God's grace giving us eternal life through belief on His Son found in every chapter.

teachings.title: What repent means: Acts 26:20
teachings.summary: Shows from Paul's testimony in Acts 26 that repent means to turn from false beliefs and turn to God, and that works meet for repentance follow salvation. Distinguishes knowing one is a sinner from repentance, and says faith alone saves.
teachings.text:
To be explicitly clear so no one can misunderstand:

We must turn from false beliefs regarding righteousness, and turn to believing God's report, obeying the Gospel, by trusting in Jesus Christ alone as the sole propitiation for our sins. This is what the Bible says **repent** means. 

But before we repent and believe, we have to first recognize we are sinners in need of salvation, damned without Christ. 

This is *not the same* as repentance, although it could be *the reason* for repenting. 

Knowing you're going to Hell and that God is offering you a way out is sufficient to bring many to repent and believe. Knowing God is just and not a liar is also sufficient to bring one to turn from the unfruitful and believe. 

According to the Bible, all men know the law written in their hearts, that they are sinners and worthy of death, and in need of salvation. *That they have no excuse. (Romans 1:20-21).
*
I hope that clears it up for everyone.

In Acts 26, Paul gives his testimony to Agrippa. 

Many false teachers point to this chapter, and verse 20 specifically, where Paul says that after his acceptance of salvation in Christ, he began his ministry and "*shewed first unto them of Damascus, and at Jerusalem, and throughout all the coasts of Judaea, and then to the Gentiles, that they should repent and turn to God, and do works meet for repentance.*"

What the subtle false prophet will do here is rhetorically ignore the clear meaning of the complete thought "repent and turn to God," remove the "and," and count on people not understanding what "do works meet for repentance" means. 

Repent means turn from. Nothing more or less. In this verse the context is clear: turn from whatever is keeping from believing God and turn towards God. Period. There is no mention of anything else here. If you were believing on something else to justify you, being a good person, worshipping idols and dead gods, turning from sin... anything else, turn away from that, repent, and turn to God. Not towards God. But fully turn to God instead.

AND, which as a conjunction here implies "then" rather than cumulative, do works meet, meaning worthy of, that aforementioned repentance. 

We are called once saved to do works worthy of that salvation. Reading Paul's epistles we see that is consistent with everything he wrote. Exhortation and edifying to act as one having repented and believed, and by faith been saved.

I would love to move on but this heresy persists and is spread by many in error, because false prophets appeal to our natural man nature that our salvation is in ourselves, in our hands, that we can maintain salvation by being self-righteous, that it's not a free gift from God.

BTW read all of Act 26, and see what Paul's testimonial of his own conversion entailed. He describes his false belief as a Pharisee, his persecution of those who had believed on Christ, that it was his thought, within himself to do these things. He believed he was right, in other words. And then he saw the light:

*13 At midday, O king, I saw in the way a light from heaven, above the brightness of the sun, shining round about me and them which journeyed with me.

14 And when we were all fallen to the earth, I heard a voice speaking unto me, and saying in the Hebrew tongue, Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me? it is hard for thee to kick against the pricks.

15 And I said, Who art thou, Lord? And he said, I am Jesus whom thou persecutest.

16 But rise, and stand upon thy feet: for I have appeared unto thee for this purpose, to make thee a minister and a witness both of these things which thou hast seen, and of those things in the which I will appear unto thee;

17 Delivering thee from the people, and from the Gentiles, unto whom now I send thee,

18 To open their eyes, and to turn them from darkness to light, and from the power of Satan unto God, that they may receive forgiveness of sins, and inheritance among them which are sanctified by faith that is in me.

19 Whereupon, O king Agrippa, I was not disobedient unto the heavenly vision:

*Paul in his own testimony says he had believed one way, sees the light believes Jesus' word, and now believes on Him. Biblical repentance.

Further he explains his ministry to the Gentiles, to turn them, which is the meaning of repent, from dark to light. From Satan to God. For what purpose? So they would have to "repent of their sin" to be saved?  Or in turning to light, to God, be saved and *have forgiveness of sins and inheritance *of those who have also been saved, *sanctified *by the same faith Paul has. Not by their "turning from sin" but by their faith in God.

This is the Gospel. Anyone preaching another is accursed. Period. No matter what else they may get right, if they do not get this correct they are false teachers.

Now again I stipulate that man is by nature one who seems to square circles and close gaps when faced with seemingly conflicting ideas, to bring them into harmony. 

Because of this, many believers who have accepted Christ unto salvation and then are exposed to preaching that tells them that they must repent of their sins in order to be saved, again a concept that doesn't exist in the Bible, will automatically in their own mind, take that to mean "admitting their are a sinner and regretting their sins," which all saved Christians would likely say was part of their coming to belief. 

But it was their faith that saves them, not acknowledging they need salvation, not regretting their sin. But believing Jesus died and was raised again so that God can give us the free gift of forgiveness and eternal life. 

There can be several reasons one accepts God at His word, but it is that acceptance, turning from not believing to trusting Him, that saves.

And so those who mentally put "of your sins" after "repent," and think it means acknowledge/regret, are in error, but not to the point of it being damnable heresy. Not at all. They are taking a biblical concept, applying the wrong word to it based on ignorance and hearing it said by so many, and just assuming that's what it means. 

But those who preach that we must turn from sin to be saved or to keep eternal salvation, that it is a necessary step, where our actions factor in to salvation, are teaching a damnable heresy of works salvation, and they should be rejected.

teachings.title: I will in no wise cast out
teachings.summary: John 6:37-40 refutes both Calvinism, since every one who sees and believes may have life, and loss of salvation, since Christ loses none given Him.
teachings.text:
The preaching Jesus gives that follows is so important, let's look at it again:

*37 All that the Father giveth me shall come to me; and him that cometh to me I will in no wise cast out.*

*38 For I came down from heaven, not to do mine own will, but the will of him that sent me.*

*39 And this is the Father's will which hath sent me, that of all which he hath given me I should lose nothing, but should raise it up again at the last day.*

*40 And this is the will of him that sent me, that every one which seeth the Son, and believeth on him, may have everlasting life: and I will raise him up at the last day.*

These verses are often used by Calvinists to say the Father chooses who is saved, but as we see in v40 *everyone* could see Jesus and believe. Not everyone will.

Those who say you can lose your salvation ignore that Jesus says those given Him by God's grace shall in no wise be cast out. That He **shall not lose any** who believe and are given Him. That they will have everlasting life and be raised up on the last day. **Everlasting**. You cannot lose your salvation.

Finally we have those who say you have to do the will of the Father to be saved, which is true, but they take it to mean obeying the commandments, repenting of all sin. But that is not the "will of the Father" Jesus teaches. He says His Father's will is that all who believe have everlasting life. To obey the Gospel. To accept His word.

teachings.title: The words I speak are spirit and life

teachings.text:

Jesus says that it's the spirit that is quickened, and that the flash profits nothing, that this is spiritually meat and drink, not literal. That "*the words that I speak unto you, they are spirit, and they are life."*

He's literally telling them that it's an allegory for a spiritual salvation, and yet some couldn't believe despite being called His disciples. Despite having some semblance of faith, but not unto belief and thus missing the point and the mark, and not getting saved.

teachings.title: Cephas, by interpretation, a stone

(remember this when you're reading Matthew 16)

The Bible defines itself and the translation is done in the text itself, so as to have no mistake about it. John gives us the word and translation (by interpretation) repeatedly throughout his Gospel, and it's for good reason.

teachings.summary: Points to the first commandment in the garden, the freewill offerings and the choices of the Old and New Testament as proof that man has a choice to believe. Answers the Reformed use of Proverbs 16:9 and sets Titus 2:11 against it.
teachings.text:
"What must I do to be saved?" 

Repent, change your mind about what you place your trust in, and believe on the Lord.

**Genesis 2**

*15 And the Lord God took the man, and put him into the garden of Eden to dress it and to keep it.

16 And the Lord God commanded the man, saying, Of every tree of the garden thou mayest freely eat:

17 But of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, thou shalt not eat of it: for in the day that thou eatest thereof thou shalt surely die.
*
Special boys "show me in the Bible where man has a choice! One verse!" 

Literally the first interaction God has with man is giving him one.

A simple bible study on the choices made by man throughout the Old Testament and New, and their consequences for not believing the Lord dispels the notion that there is no free will. The fact that God puts emphasis on sacrifices being free will sacrifices, pointing to Jesus and our choice to believe in His, should be sufficient. But it's the point of the entire Bible. 

Random example pop to my head, the book of Judges where "every man did that which was right in his own eyes" is the theme. That's them choosing to do what's right in their own eyes rather than in God's.

If Reformed Theology was simply **Proverbs 16:9,** it wouldn't be damnable heresy. 

*A man’s heart deviseth his way: but the LORD directeth his steps*

Instead that's the Motte and Bailey they fall back to when their false doctrines are attacked, "So you're saying the Lord doesn't direct man's steps?"

What will also often happen to these reformed special boys, when cornered with verse and logic, is they will demure, saying "oh I'm not a strict five point" or whatever and back down from whichever unsupported view that's been exposed, to maintain whatever other view isn't being discussed currently. Like arguing with a liberal, it becomes nailing Jello to the wall.

The calvinist giving their version of the "good news" is like a timeshare condo pitch that says "good news, you may have won a free weekend at one of our resorts..." It's just so obviously gross.

**Titus 2:11-12**

*11 For the grace of God that bringeth salvation hath appeared to **all men**,

12 Teaching us that, denying ungodliness and worldly lusts, we should live soberly, righteously, and godly, in this present world;*

teachings.title: God is not the author of evil
teachings.summary: Gathers James 1:13-14, Ecclesiastes 7:29, Jeremiah 19:5 and Romans 1:30 to show that God does not tempt or devise evil, and that men invent it. Answers the claim of total depravity that ascribes every wicked thing to God.
teachings.text:
**James 1**
*13 Let no man say when he is tempted, I am tempted of God: for God cannot be tempted with evil, neither tempteth he any man: 14 But every man is tempted, when he is drawn away of his own lust, and enticed.*

**Ecclesiastes 7**
*29 Lo, this only have I found, that God hath made man upright; but they have sought out many inventions*.

Jeremiah 19
*5 They have built also the high places of Baal, to burn their sons with fire for burnt offerings unto Baal, which I commanded not, nor spake it, **neither came it into my mind:***

Romans 1
*30 Backbiters, haters of God, despiteful, proud, boasters, **inventors of evil things,** disobedient to parents*,

James White is a reprobate. His damnable heresies require him to ascribe to God every wicked thing White and his fellow sons of Belial come up with. They believe in "total depravity" and call all men reprobate, because that is what they are. 

**2 Peter 2**
*1 But there were false prophets also among the people, even as there shall be false teachers among you, who privily shall bring in damnable heresies, even denying the Lord that bought them, and bring upon themselves swift destruction*.

teachings.title: Free will and the Calvinist "and"
teachings.summary: Says false doctrines are held by trading one false either/or for another instead of taking the Word as it is. Argues that denying man's choice denies the point of Scripture, and that Lordship and Reformed answers always add "believe AND...".
teachings.text:
What they do is position themselves within a theological false binary and endlessly rationalize their (false) positions based on what other (equally false) positions are, rather than just accepting the Word as is. 

When poked, they will invariably argue you're the opposing binary. It is a red-blue mentality applied to religion. It's how theological traps work (and all similar false binary rhetorical traps, too)

And because they can't escape from these prebuilt either/ors to see their own error, they can't reach understanding.

This is especially true in those who think they are clever special boys, because the snare is designed to hook their pride, and the larger their pride, the more entangled they become.

What those who deny man's free will in choosing to perish or accept God's word cannot explain is why, if it is His will who be given faith, (rather than God's will being "*all men to be saved, and to come unto the knowledge of the truth*"), why did He create all of Scripture as His testimony, and make spreading the Gospel, the Good News of that promise, the means of propagating salvation, "from faith to faith?" To having witnesses that His word is true?

They can't explain why there was His law in the garden, even one commandment, that Adam and Eve should have choice. That the entire OT is presenting the lineage of choice for both inheritance and blessing. Denying the will of man, denies the entire point of the Word, and ultimately that belief on that word is what saves us.

As for Reformed Theology and Lordship, they claim that their "surrendering to Lord Jesus," to make themselves "slaves to Him," (rather than servants, because slave denotes not having a choice), they aren't actually trusting in Him alone. They are trusting their corruptible flesh to perfectly obey, and instead of showing complete faith in God, putting it all on themselves.

That's not even getting into the blasphemy of claiming God dictates all manner of wickedness and sin, being an absolute sovereign of the world. (Reprobate James White claimed pedophiles rape kids because it is God's will, for example).

When asked how to be saved it's always "believe AND..." It is the "and" that damns them.

teachings.title: The Spirit reproves the world of sin: because they believe not on Me
teachings.summary: Reads John 16:7-11 and notes the KJV word is reprove, not convict, and that the sin named is not believing on Jesus. Warns that the newer versions' wording opens the door to repent-of-your-sin works salvation.
teachings.text:
**John 16:7-11**

*7 Nevertheless I tell you the truth; It is expedient for you that I go away: for if I go not away, the Comforter will not come unto you; but if I depart, I will send him unto you.

8 And when he is come, he will **reprove** the world of sin, and of righteousness, and of judgment:

9 Of sin, because they believe not on me;

10 Of righteousness, because I go to my Father, and ye see me no more;

11 Of judgment, because the prince of this world is judged*.

Public Service Announcement: In false new age versions, they use "convict" rather than the precise term, "reprove" in this verse, so they can insert the false doctrine of "repent-of-your-sin" works salvation. Don't be fooled!

When Jesus says the Holy Spirit will reprove for sin, note what the sin is; not believing on Him.

teachings.title: No limbo: Old Testament saints were saved by faith
teachings.summary: Shows that Adam and all Old Testament saints went to Heaven by faith in God's word, and that Limbo and purgatory are inventions. Points to Christ as the lamb slain before the foundation of the world and the blood on the mercy seat.
teachings.text:
No they didn't. "Limbo" is an invention of the RCC. 

Saved Christians know that Adam, and all OT saints, went to Heaven, the same way we do; faith in God's word. Jesus went to Hell to pay the price for all sin, Adam's to yours, and beyond. He freed the saved in the Old Testament the same way He's freed us. With His blood. 

Repent and get saved today! It's a free gift from God, and no institutions of man can give it to you, or deny His grace to you.

The Bible says that Jesus Christ is the lamb slain before the foundation of the world. That He was "foreordained before the foundation of the world." All believers were called upon to "inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world."

The notion of Limbo comes from unsaved false prophets, like Clement of Alexandria, who not understanding simple salvation, sought to rectify the ways of God to the feeble understanding of a natural man, stating that "it's not right" that the Patriarchs, "should be condemned without trial," when the wages of sin has always been death. Natural man questioning God's judgement is the source of most heresy. 

The scriptures teach us that there are none righteous, "no not one," and that since the first generation of man, we have been justified by faith alone calling upon the name of the Lord. 

Heaven and Hell. Those are the two choices before every man. There is no limbo. There is no purgatory. There is no working your way to righteousness. There is only the blood of the lamb on the mercy seat. The burnt offering of Christ. Amen.
